disease.name: Mineral Rot
entries: Upon contracting the disease, a creature feels immediately unwell and gains a level of {@condition exhaustion}. During its next long rest, the creature must make a successful {@dc 14} Constitution saving throw or lose half its Charisma score as its flesh begins transforming into a pock-marked, stony surface. The disease can be cured by magic during this stage.

The creature must repeat the saving throw during its next long rest, fighting off the disease on a successful save or succumbing to it on a failed one. Creatures who fail are changed into twisted moss-and-stone covered versions of themselves. Mindless and malicious, the creature attacks any living thing it meets. From this point on, creatures bitten by the afflicted must make a successful {@dc 14} Constitution saving throw or contract the disease. Once fully transformed, only a {@spell wish} spell can restore them.
Use the following template to apply the end stage of mineral rot to foes faced by the party. The disease raises a creature's challenge rating by 1, so adjust encounters accordingly:

items: Increase the AC by 2.
The creature gains resistance to slashing damage from non-magical sources.
The creature is immune to disease and poison.
The creature's unarmed attacks are magical.
The creature gains extra hit points equal to half its current hit point maximum.

If it does not already have one, the creature gains a bite attack with hit and damage ranges appropriate to its CR. Creatures bitten by this attack must make a successful {@dc 14} Constitution save or contract mineral rot. A successful save results in immunity to contracting the disease for 24 hours.

disease.name: Rime Disease
entries: Victims of rime disease lose 25 percent of their movement speed immediately and 25 percent per day for 3 days. On the third day, the victim transforms into an {@creature ice mephit}. The disease may be cured with a {@spell lesser restoration} spell or by pouring the melted remains of Oithois's claw over the wound.

item.name: Centaur Wrist-Wraps
entries: These leather-and-fur wraps are imbued with centaur shamanic magic. The wraps are stained a deep orange, and intricate patterns painted in blue seem to float above the surface of the leather. While wearing them, you may call upon their magic to reroll any attack made with a {@item shortbow|phb} or {@item longbow|phb}, and the resulting roll must be used instead. Once used in this way, the wraps must be held in wood smoke for 15 minutes before their magic can be used again.

item.name: Cloak of the Empire
entries: This voluminous grey cloak has bright-red trim and the sigil from an unknown empire on its back. The cloak is stiff and does not fold as normal cloth might. When hit by a ranged attack while wearing it, you may reduce the damage by your Charisma modifier.

item.name: Shroud of Oth
entries: The strands of this shimmering, silken shroud swirl like wisps of clouds. A plain golden band runs along its edge. Once attuned to it, you have resistance to radiant damage while wearing or carrying it. You can also cast the shroud over your head to render yourself invisible to celestial creatures and unable to be targeted by their abilities or magic. While hidden by the shroud, you can see the faint outline of a bent humanoid form staring at it from a nearby point. Ever-watching, the crone-like figure occasionally points at you ominously. For each minute you are hidden by the shroud, you must succeed on a {@dc 12} Wisdom saving throw or become {@condition frightened}, forcing you to remove it and ending the hidden effect.

entries.name: In Midgard
entries: This shroud belongs to Baba Yaga. It was stolen from her by a mystic in whom she put great trust and invited into her hut for dinner. The mystic betrayed the witch's trust, making off with several powerful magical objects. Grandmother can see the bearer of this shroud whenever they cast it over themselves. She knows their location and learns a detail about them each time she sees them. Inevitably, the witch will come for her shroud, sending one of the vela or some less comely minion to retrieve it. Should the PCs return the shroud to Baba Yaga, they may gain a small boon from her, though she may also transform them into cutlery as can be expected by the inconstant crone.

item.name: Shark-Tooth Crown
entries: Shark's teeth of varying sizes adorn a simple leather headband. The teeth pile one atop the other in a jumble of sharp points and flat sides, and three particularly large ones are stained with crimson dye. The teeth move slightly of their own accord when you are within a mile of a body of saltwater, snapping and clacking, producing a sound not unlike that of a crab's claw. While wearing it, you also have advantage on all Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) checks to navigate on or in bodies of saltwater. Additionally, you gain the following.

entries.name: Lord of Waves and Deeps (2/Day)
entries: As a bonus action, you may cast {@spell command} (save {@dc 13}). If the targeted creature is an aquatic beast, it fails the saving throw automatically.

item.name: Void-Touched Buckler
entries: This simple wood-and-metal buckler belonged to an adventurer slain by a {@creature void dragon wyrmling|ToB}. It sat for decades next to a small tear in the fabric of reality that led to the outer plains and has become tainted by the void, acquiring magical traits that reflect the cold chaos of the beyond. The buckler functions as a {@i {@item +1 shield}}. Also, as an action, you may invoke the power of the void. For 1 minute, a swirling magical aura envelops the buckler, and any creature that misses you with an attack must succeed on a {@dc 14} Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition frightened} of you until the end of their next turn. Conversely, any creature that hits you with an attack receives advantage on attacks against you until the end of your next turn. This ability cannot be used again until you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Hiding
entries: The goblin crew has total cover.

entries.name: Rolling Death
entries: The wagon can move through Medium or smaller creatures, and those caught in its path must make a {@dc 12} Dexterity saving throw to avoid being run over, taking 8 ({@damage 2d6 + 1}) bludgeoning damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Actions
entries: On its turn, the wagon can take 2 actions, choosing from the options below. It can take only 1 action if it has fewer than three crew. It can't take these actions if it has fewer than two crew.

entries.name: Blade Storm
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 3} to hit, reach 10 ft., up to two targets. {@h}9 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) slashing damage. With great enthusiasm and probably sound effects, the goblins swing two short swords at the end of extra-long poles attached to the wagon like oars on a boat.

entries.name: Fire the Cannon
entries: The goblins yell and fire their Cannon Turret, which is just a heavy crossbow mounted within the turret.

entries.name: We're Pretty Tired Boss
entries: The goblins tasked with pedaling and moving the wagon are already exhausted. At the beginning of each of the wagon's turns, roll {@dice d6}. On a 5 or 6, the wagon can move 40 feet that turn. Once moving, the wagon ignores difficult terrain thanks to momentum. (On a 1-4, the lack of movement doesn't take an action.)

entries.name: Hull
entries: Armor Class 13
Hit Points 65 (damage threshold 5)

entries.name: Weapon: Cannon Turret

Hit Points 15 (damage threshold 5)
{@atk rw} {@hit 4} to hit, range 100/400 ft., one target. {@h}9 ({@damage 2d8}) piercing damage.

entries.name: Destroyed
entries: If the war machine reaches 0 hit points, it is destroyed, and the {@creature fire elemental} trapped within is released. The elemental then moves and attacks the nearest target. However, its hatred of Briarskin is great, and if it comes within 60 feet of the necromancer, it notices and charges to attack her.

entries.name: Hiding
entries: The goblin crew has total cover.

entries.name: Rolling Death
entries: The war machine can move through Medium or smaller creatures, and those caught in its path must make a {@dc 13} Dexterity saving throw to avoid being run over, taking 16 ({@damage 4d6 + 2}) bludgeoning damage and 10 ({@damage 2d6 + 3}) fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Squash the House
entries: When the war machine comes into contact with a building made of wood or other plant matter, it ends its movement that round. On its following turn, it flattens the building to splinter and ash.

entries.name: Actions
entries: On its turn, the war machine can take 2 actions, choosing from the options below. It can take only 1 action if it has fewer than four crew. It can't take these actions if it has fewer than two crew.

entries.name: Prickly Doom
entries: {@atk rw} {@hit 3} to hit, range 30 ft., one target. {@h}16 ({@damage 3d6 + 6}) piercing damage. Excited goblins within concentrate their bow shots at a target within 30 feet while making childish bleating noises.

entries.name: Unleash the Hammer
entries: The war machine can attack with its hammer.

entries.name: Hull
entries: Armor Class 17
Hit Points 50

entries.name: Movement: Rollers
entries: Armor Class 18
Hit Points 30; -15 ft. speed per 15 damage taken
Speed 30 ft.

entries.name: Weapon: Hammer
entries: Armor Class 16
Hit Points 20
{@atk mw} {@hit 4} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}21 ({@damage 6d6}) bludgeoning damage. The huge hammer mounted on the war machine's front can be used to attack any creature in front of it.

vehicle.name: Burrowing War Machine
entries: This massive iron and steel machine is divided into two discrete sections. The forward 30 feet are dedicated to a rotating drill whose teeth are noticeably worn. The back portion consists of a 50-foot tube with three large treads spread equidistant around the tube. Two outlines that suggest doors are set into the body of the machine. The very back of the vehicle is a smoldering engine . . . what magic fuels this impressive wonder of metal?
The machine consists of a 30-foot-long mechanical drill made of magically durable steel mounted to the front of a 50-foot-long crew-and-passenger section.

A great magical engine comprises the back 10 feet, which sheds bright light for 25 feet around the machine and dim light for another 50 feet. The machine has an AC of 18 and 175 hit points. Its metal exterior grants it a damage threshold of 15. It resists all nonmagical damage and is immune to force damage. It has no actions and cannot move.

entries.name: Doors
entries: There are two doors in the midsection that can only be opened from inside. The doors have no visible hinges or handles. Forcing a door open requires a successful {@dc 20} Strength check. The doors open forcefully, and creatures caught underneath them must make a {@dc 13} Dexterity saving throw, taking 7 ({@damage 2d6}) bludgeoning damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Drill
entries: Powered up and running, the drill allows the machine to pass through natural elements, including dirt, clay, sand, rock, and ice. The drill leaves a 15-foot-diameter passage behind it, which typically caves in within a few moments. Creatures who come into contact with the drill while it is operating (whether shoved, falling, or other) must make a {@dc 13} Dexterity saving throw, taking 27 ({@damage 5d10}) slashing damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Engine
entries: The engine is magical, radiating enchantment magic. A successful {@dc 16} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check reveals that the magic is fading and that the machine's ability to continue traveling is compromised.

trait.name: Succor the Suffering
entries: A blemish harvester has advantage on attacks made against creatures that are diseased or cursed.

action.name: Multiattack

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 6} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d4 + 3}) piercing damage and 2 ({@damage 1d4}) poison damage. Creatures struck by this attack must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw or lose 2 ({@damage 1d4}) Charisma until they complete a long rest. A creature whose Charisma is reduced to 0 by this attack dies instantly and returns to life as a blemish harvester 24 hours later.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 6} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}10 ({@damage 2d6 + 3}) slashing damage.

action.name: Expel Rot and Ruin (1/Day)
entries: The blemish harvester expels a cloud of cursed gas in a 20-foot-wide cone. Creatures caught in the cloud must make a {@dc 14} Constitution saving throw, taking 11 ({@damage 2d10}) necrotic damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. Creatures that fail this saving throw are magically covered in boils and blemishes and lose 5 ({@damage 2d4}) Charisma until they complete a long rest. While affected by this ability, the creature is considered diseased and can be cured using remove disease as normal.

trait.name: Bleed the Dying
entries: The swarm's Sting has greater efficacy against injured creatures. When the swarm hits a creature that doesn't have all its hit points with its sting, the sting deals an extra 2 ({@damage 1d4}) poison damage.

trait.name: Devil's Sight
entries: Magical darkness doesn't impede the swarm's darkvision.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The swarm has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Swarm
entries: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny creature. The swarm can't regain hit points or gain temporary hit points.

action.name: Sting
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}12 ({@damage 3d6 + 2}) piercing damage or 7 ({@damage 2d4 + 2}) piercing damage if the swarm has half of its hit points or fewer.

action.name: Spew Blood

items.name: Knee-Bar
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 4} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}3 bludgeoning damage, and target must succeed on a {@dc 12} Strength saving throw or be {@condition restrained}. Dib can choose to maintain the Knee-Bar indefinitely but can take no move actions and is considered {@condition prone} while doing so.

items.name: Rampage

items.name: Bite

items.name: Hand Crossbow

items.name: Warhammer

items.name: Multiattack

items.name: Cloaked (3/Day)
entries: The scout has advantage on its next Stealth check.

items.name: Claws
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 4} to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) slashing damage plus 3 ({@damage 1d4 + 1}) cold damage. Creatures struck by this attack must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw or suffer from rime disease (see the {@i Rime Disease} disease).

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) piercing damage, and the creature must succeed on a {@dc 14} Constitution saving throw or contract mineral rot (see the {@i Mineral Rot} disease). A successful save results in immunity to the disease for 24 hours.

items.name: Annihilating Swathe
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 11} to hit, reach 5 ft., up to 3 targets. {@h}14 ({@damage 4d6}) slashing damage.

items.name: Breach-Empowered
entries: While within 10 feet of the breach, the wyrmling regenerates 7 hit points at the start of its turn. Once each round, the wyrmling can call on the power of the breach to give it advantage on a saving throw.

items.name: Pseudopod
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 3} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) bludgeoning damage. This attack deals no acid damage, though the ooze retains its corrosive quality toward armor.

items.name: Visions of the Leviathan (Recharge 6)
entries: All enemies within 30 feet must succeed on a {@dc 10} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition frightened} for 1 round.

items.name: Gibbering
entries: The mouther babbles incoherently while it can see any creature and isn't {@condition incapacitated}. Each creature that starts its turn within 20 feet of the mouther and can hear the gibbering must succeed on a {@dc 12} Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, the creature can't take reactions until the start of its next turn and rolls a {@dice d8} to determine what it does during its turn. On a 1 to 4, the creature does nothing. On a 5 or 6, the creature takes no action or bonus action and uses all its movement to move in a randomly determined direction. On a 7 or 8, the creature makes a melee attack against a randomly determined creature within its reach or does nothing if it can't make such an attack.

items.name: Dart
entries: {@atk rw} {@hit 4} to hit, range 20/60 ft., one target. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) piercing damage. Balf carries a magical dart that returns to his hand after being thrown.

entries: Balf makes two Dart attacks.

contents.name: Neither by Sail, Nor by Oar

rows: {@b An adventure for four to six characters of 1st level}

entries: That's it! I'm done. There's slime taking over the coast, so I'm out of here. I've family inland that are marginally more tolerable.

entries.name: Background
entries: Ten years ago, a handful of villagers discovered Biabzu performing rites to honor a dreadful sea god. Convinced her worship was depleting the village's fishing grounds, they drowned her in the nearby tidal pools.

Today, the village is beset by slime creatures that have ruined its fishing grounds and imperiled its residents. The PCs arrive and are hired by the village elder to investigate. During their investigation, they learn the source of the slime is an ancient underwater shrine dedicated to the same dreadful sea god. They also learn that Biabzu is alive in its depths. Before descending into the shrine, they are approached by Biabzu's sister, who implores them to spare her sister's life. The adventure concludes with the party facing Biabzu and the magic of the shrine.

{@b In Truth.} Biabzu's prayers to the sea god had no impact on the fishing grounds 10 years ago. The return of the fish after she was murdered was entirely coincidental. It was Elder Hom who led the mob that drowned Biabzu and sunk her body into the sea. Over the years since, the magic of the evil shrine transformed Biabzu into a {@creature sea hag}, who has awakened and is using the shrine to summon her slimy vengeance. To save the village's livelihood, the party must destroy the undead coral at the heart of the shrine, and to do that, they must face Biabzu and the eight statues that empower her.
Here are a just a few suggestions to bring the PCs into the adventure:

items: While adventuring elsewhere, the party learns of a dangerous shortage of fish at the markets. After investigating, they discover that the primary source for fish in the region is the community of Gullrock, which has not been able to supply the markets because of pervasive slime.

The party encounters a fisherfolk, far outside their normal grounds, who explains that they must risk these longer trips because their usual waters are filled with caustic slime. They inform the party the village of Gullrock is nearby and that there is coin to be earned if they are willing to help.

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: The following NPCs will be present for this adventure:

items: {@b {@i Ayanni Wavecrest.}} Ayanni is a middle-aged human woman whose lean physique suggests a life of labor. She wears a simple gray-and-blue dress with a gray shawl and worn leather boots. She carries no weapons. Her face is sad and resolved. Ayanni is not convinced her sister was to blame for the depleted fishing grounds 10 years ago, and she holds a grudge against Elder Hom and those responsible for Biabzu's death.

{@b {@i Elder Hom.}} Matina Hom is a middle-aged half-orc woman with curly graying hair and a face deeply lined from a life on the water and under the sun. She wears unadorned fisherfolk attire (commoner's clothing) and carries a boat knife (dagger) at her belt. She has been the elder of Gullrock for almost 15 years and is well respected. Matina has advantage on Charisma checks when dealing with other residents of Gullrock.

entries.name: Arrive in Gullrock
entries: Gullrock is a small fishing village that supplies nearby towns with fresh fish. The villagers are generally tired and anxious. In the last month, they have repelled four separate invasions by the strange slime that makes fishing a perilous activity. Morale is low, and many talk of leaving.

The village's tavern is called Planks. It is run by a dwarf named Braddle, who was a pirate and thief in a previous life and has now retired to safety and anonymity in the village. The inn costs 1 sp for a night and serves crab stew and watery wine for 5 cp. A young human warrior named Inna ({@creature guard}) can be hired here for 3 gp to help the party in Biabzu's lair.
The party is approached by Elder Hom shortly after arriving in the village.

entries.name: Meet with Elder Hom
entries: Elder Hom ({@creature commoner}) offers the party adventuring work. She offers 50 gp to each PC if they can stop the slime from attacking the fisherfolk and washing up on shore. She reveals the following information:

items: The slime has been arriving with growing frequency.
The slime is very common in some nearby tide pools.
The slime is vulnerable to fire but difficult to kill with knives and clubs.

entries: She directs them to the tide pools if they ask.

Elder Hom has no intention of discussing Biabzu or her murder. If confronted about Biabzu, she denies everything and claims that Biabzu was mentally unwell and likely took her own life. If Biabzu returns with the party, she flees the village to avoid consequences.

entries.name: Uncover the Truth
entries: {@b {@i Chatting with Villagers.}} The party can chat with any of the villagers about the current situation. The villagers are happy to complain about the loss of income and the terrible danger the slime presents. A PC who succeeds on a {@dc 10} Charisma (Intimation or Persuasion) check while interviewing a villager learns that a figure has been seen at night on the rocks by the tide pools. The figure is hunched, and a dull-green glow follows it.

{@b {@i Loose-Lipped Senior.}} While in Gullrock, the party encounters an old man in a thick, felted wool hat. He is confused and not overly helpful in their investigation. He does however mention, "A young woman took her own life at the tide pools many years ago." Her name was Biabzu, and she worshipped an evil spirit of the sea. The townsfolk were relieved she died since it replenished the fish stocks in the area.
He's seen the slime collecting in the tide pools.

entries.name: Learn Ayanni's Plight
entries: During their investigation and before they head to the tide pools, the party is approached by Ayanni. She can reveal the following:

items: Biabzu had a cherished doll from childhood. Ayanni gives the doll to the party if they are sympathetic toward her.
Biabzu was no follower of the dreadful sea god.
Something or someone caused her death. Her sister would not harm herself.

entries: She begs the party to bring her sister home to her alive.

entries.name: Brave the Tide Pools
entries: A stretch of rocky pools rises from the water. Foam, seaweed, and small sea creatures can be seen in the pools. A gull flies overhead, its call lost in the waves.

The pools are home to three {@creature Gray Ooze (Shrine-Tainted)|KPPreparedExpanded|gray oozes} (plus one additional ooze for each party member over four) with the following modifications: resistant to acid and cold damage, vulnerable to fire, and their Pseudopod attacks deal 5 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) bludgeoning damage but no acid damage, though they retain their corrosive quality toward armor.
The oozes attack the party, attempting to surprise them using Stealth ({@dc 13} to spot).

A search of the pools reveals a narrow crevasse in the rock. A Medium creature must squeeze through. A successful {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check reveals humanoid footprints in the muck leading in and out of the crevasse.

entries.name: Enter the Lair of Biabzu

entries: The narrow crevasse opens into a hallway made of finished stone. Dim light emanates from an unseen source at the opposite end of the passage, which slopes down steeply toward the light. Strange markings adorn some of the stones of the wall.
The crevasse leads to a ruined passageway under the pools. The passage is 10 feet wide and 8 feet tall. It is blocked by rubble on one end, and the other leads the shrine and lair of Biabzu.

{@b {@i Deep Calls Curse.}} A PC who succeeds on a {@dc 13} Intelligence ({@skill History} or {@skill Investigation}) check recognizes that the markings on the wall are associated with the dreadful sea god. The successful check also suggests the presence of a nearby important artifact and wards that protect it.

A PC who studies the markings long enough to make the ability check must also succeed on a {@dc 10} Wisdom saving throw or become cursed by the undead coral heart in the nearby chamber. The first time the cursed PC sees the coral heart, they are magically compelled to vocalize in an ululating whale-like call that resonates through the chamber. Any creature except Biabzu that hears the cry and is within 60 feet of the speaker takes 1 psychic damage. The curse ends after the call is made.
Read the following after the party makes their way down the sloping passage into the lair of Biabzu:

You enter a large circular chamber made of carved stone blocks. At the center of the chamber, under a dome of transparent magical energy, sits a dark-gray colony of coral. The chamber features eight large stone statues that circle the coral, depicting terrifying visages, all staring at it. Slumped on the floor near the coral is a young woman.

The young woman is Biabzu ({@creature sea hag}), using her Illusory Appearance ability to appear as she did before the shrine transformed her. She uses the ruse to her advantage, attacking anyone who draws near by surprise if she can, using Horrific Appearance. Biabzu is eager to slay the party and feed their remains to the undead coral at the heart of the chamber. Reasoning with her is impossible. If the party shows Biabzu the doll Ayanni gave them, she has disadvantage on her next attack.

{@b {@i Eight Faces.}} The statues are made of stone and cannot be destroyed without time and the proper tools. At the beginning of each round, two statues activate. Roll a {@dice d8} twice (rerolling doubles) to determine which of the statues activate, and then roll a {@dice d8} twice again and consult the Statue Activations table to determine what each statue does this round.
The statues deactivate if Biabzu is slain or if the coral heart is destroyed.

{@b {@i Coral Heart.}} This foul undead is protected by a magical dome. The dome and the coral can be destroyed. The dome has an AC of 14, 10 hit points, is immune to psychic damage, and is resistant to cold damage. The coral heart has an AC of 10, 30 hit points, and is healed by necrotic damage. Destroying the coral heart causes Biabzu to drop to 0 hit points immediately, knocking her {@condition unconscious}. Healing does not restore her to consciousness. She awakens, still as a sea hag, after {@dice 1d4} days. However, if she is the target of a {@spell remove curse} spell before this time passes, she awakens as her human self ({@creature commoner}) with all her previous memories.
{@b {@i Treasure.}} Each statue has a pearl embedded in its base (worth 10 gp each).

entries.caption: Statue Activations
rows: Any creature reduced to 0 hit points this round is instead reduced to 1 hit point.
Biabzu gains resistance to non-magical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.
Biabzu is healed for 5 hit points.
Biabzu is immune to fire damage.
Biabzu's Death Glare action affects any creature that can see her, but the save DC is 8.

On Biabzu's initiative, a 15-foot cone of fine salt sprays from the statue. Creatures caught in the cone must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition blinded} until the end of their next turn.

On Biabzu's initiative, a {@creature Gray Ooze (Shrine-Tainted)|KPPreparedExpanded} (same modifications as those in the tide pools, see above) appears in an unoccupied space within 10 feet of the statue. This ooze has only 1 hit point.

On Biabzu's initiative, the statue belches chlorine gas in a 15-foot cone. Creatures caught in the area must make a {@dc 12} Dexterity saving throw, taking 2 ({@damage 1d4}) acid damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: If Biabzu is slain, Ayanni flees the village. If Biabzu is returned to the village in sea hag form, Ayanni keeps her hidden and arranges for the curse to be lifted. In this case, the party receives a {@i {@item cap of water breathing}} from Ayanni as a token of thanks. The party receives payment from the village either way.

entries: We were traveling the old trade road up near the Blind Hills when we found it, the overturned wagon in the ditch. Evas took to the shadows, scouted ahead, and returned with strange details. The wagon had been transformed—such that it appeared to be a fierce fortress. Signs of goblin-work were apparent: broken shields reinforcing the walls, crude arrow slits cut into the driver's bench, a makeshift flag hanging limply atop the whole affair. We left it alone, but even at a distance, the smell of the odd fortress's unfinished moat made us wretch.

entries.name: Background
entries: Several months back, Dib Halfling-Chewer and his cronies were ejected from a nearby goblin clan for indiscriminate wrestling. Their antics, though hilariously entertaining to themselves, were destructive and dangerous to the rest of the clan. The goblins spent several nights in the wilderness before discovering an abandoned wagon by the side of a trade road. There, the homeless cadre transformed the wagon into a distinctly goblinoid fortress. They have had some success in assaulting and looting travelers on the road.

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: Assaulting the fortress is a combat encounter. The fortress may take two of the following actions on initiative 10 each round:

items: {@b {@i Spear Thrusts.}} {@atk mw} {@hit 4} to hit, reach 5 ft., two targets. {@h}5 piercing damage. Spear Thrusts have advantage against PCs attempting to lift the wagon.
{@b {@i Arrow Barrage.}} {@atk rw} {@hit 4} to hit, range 80/320 ft., two targets. {@h}5 piercing damage.

{@b {@i Fairly Hot Oil (Recharge 5-6).}} Multiple blobs of oil spray all creatures within 20 ft. Each target must make a {@dc 10} Dexterity saving throw, taking 2 fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries: Adventurers can defeat the fortress in a number of ways:

items: {@b {@i Fire.}} If the wagon takes fire damage, it has a 50 percent chance of bursting into flames. While aflame, the wagon takes 9 ({@damage 2d6 + 2}) fire damage each round on initiative 20. If the wagon takes 24 or more damage from being on fire, the goblins inside retreat to {@area 3|2.3|u}.

{@b {@i Kicking in the Door.}} The door at the back of the wagon is solidly reinforced. Forcing the door requires a successful {@dc 17} Strength check. The DC for this check is reduced to 14 if the fortress has less than half its hit points remaining. Once the door is forced, the goblins retreat to {@area 3|2.3|u}.

{@b {@i Kill It.}} The fortress has an AC of 14 and 40 hit points. It is resistant to piercing damage and vulnerable to fire damage. PCs may attack it as they would a normal, albeit immobile, target. Once the fortress reaches 0 hit points, the goblins retreat to {@area 3|2.3|u}.

{@b {@i Lifting the Whole Damn Thing Up.}} Lifting and tipping the fortress over takes 2 rounds. Each round requires a successful {@dc 17} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check made by at least one PC. The DC of this check is reduced by one for each PC assisting. PCs involved in lifting the wagon may take no other actions that round. Failing the check on the second round results in the lifting PC(s) having to start over. Successfully lifting the wagon results in the goblins retreating to {@area 3|2.3|u}.

entries.name: Wrestling Moves
entries: The goblins inside the fortress have advantage on all grappling-related checks and attacks. When forced into melee, they are as likely to attempt grabs and shoves as they are shortsword attacks. {@creature Dib|KPPreparedExpanded}, a regular goblin in every other way, gains the following:

{@b {@i Knee-Bar.}} {@atk mw} {@hit 4} to hit, range 5 ft., one target. {@h}3 bludgeoning damage, and target must succeed on a {@dc 12} Strength saving throw or be {@condition restrained}. Dib can choose to maintain the Knee-Bar indefinitely but can take no move actions and is considered {@condition prone} while doing so.

entries.name: Area 1: Exterior

entries: A large wooden wagon has been overturned a few feet from the road. An incomplete moat rings the structure, and the vapors from its gelatinous contents reach your nose even at 50 paces. The wagon has been reinforced with broken shields and scavenged planks. An unfortunate fox has been nailed unceremoniously atop a crude doorway. Slits and holes of various sizes have been bored and carved into the walls, and you hear whispering and rustling coming from within. A flag made from cloth scraps hangs unmoving in the still air.

The goblins do not leave the safety of the wagon willingly. They are interested in softer targets than a band of adventurers, so they stay under the wagon and operate its attacks as previously described. In general, if the wagon seems likely to be destroyed, the goblins retreat to {@area 3|2.3|u}.

entries.name: Area 2: Under the Wagon

entries: The inside of the makeshift stronghold is a dank and foul-smelling place. A small cauldron of rendered animal fat boils over a smoky fire. Several poorly crafted spears sit abandoned on the ground. A ladder suggests the wagon's inhabitants have dug into the ground below.
Once their fortress is breached, the five {@creature goblin||goblins} inside retreat to the throne room.
A successful {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check uncovers an oily sack hidden under a rock. It contains 25 sp and some shiny rocks.

entries.name: Area 3: Tunnel and Throne Room

entries: The tunnel, precariously carved and shored-up with planking, runs straight for 30 feet before turning sharply. Around the corner are the goblins' living quarters. A single sputtering torch illuminates the small chamber and the makeshift throne at the far end. Evil eyes blink from behind five small mounds of dirt and bedding. The sound of bow strings being drawn greets your ears.
The goblins make ranged attacks from behind half cover until forced into melee.

{@b {@i Spike Trap.}} At the entrance to the chamber is a simple spike trap. A successful {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check notices the trap, and a successful {@dc 12} Dexterity (thieves' tools) check disarms it. Failure to notice or disarm the trap causes six sharp spikes to spring out of the ground. PCs within 5 feet of the trap must make a {@dc 13} Dexterity saving throw, taking 3 ({@damage 1d6}) piercing damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

The throne hides Dib's treasure hoard. A successful {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check reveals the seat of the throne is loose and offset. Inside the throne is a small wooden chest containing 15 gp, 60 sp, and a scrap of cloth with Dib's fortress design notes scribbled in smudged ink.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: No doubt the local authorities are thankful the PCs removed the nuisance from the side of the road. What of the clan from which Dib and his entourage were expelled? How did the goblin develop such strong wrestling moves? Perhaps the entire clan practices unarmed combat—their desire to test their skills on civilized folk growing as the subterranean wrestling rings increase in number.

rows: {@b An adventure for four to six characters of 1st or 2nd level}

entries: I was taken by the evil dogs while camping near Agav's Bog. They dragged me into their lair, and it wasn't until I escaped that I knew the truth of the place: a great and bony wing buried in the side of a hill. They chained me in the dark with a candle made from foul wax and forced me to dig at the marrow. Their bonds were poorly made, and I fled several days later while they slept. What purpose did they have in mining that marrow? I cannot say.

entries.name: Background
entries: The Marrow Mines are dug in and around the fossilized wing of an unnamed leviathan. A small pack of {@creature kobold||kobolds} lives and works in the mines, which are heavily trapped. The kobolds defend the area fiercely and patrol the region around the mine. At night, several swarms of bats exit the mine and hunt in the nearby region.
The kobolds are led by Rikir, a large and brutish kobold who lost an eye in a fight with some nearby goblins. Rikir is responsible for the cunning traps dispensed throughout the place.

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: This adventure does not specify the number of enemies in any given encounter. Tailor the numbers to suit the desired challenge level.

{@b {@i Marrow.}} The marrow from the wing is an addictive substance for the kobolds, and some have been altered by its long-term use. In addition to Rikir, one in five of the kobolds encountered in the mines has gained the following action:
{@b {@i Visions of the Leviathan (Recharge 6).}} All enemies within 30 feet must succeed on a {@dc 10} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition frightened} for 1 round.
Kobolds altered in this way use the statistics of a {@creature Marrow-Touched Kobold|KPPreparedExpanded}.

Consuming the marrow causes horrific visions of storms and malevolent monsters winging their way through the skies. PCs who consume the marrow must succeed on a {@dc 14} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition paralyzed} for 24 hours. Paralyzed PCs can attempt the saving throw again every hour. At the end of their paralysis, the PCs discover they can read, write, and speak Draconic. This effect ends after five long rests.

entries.name: Rikir's Traps
entries: {@b {@i Box of Bats.}} The box of bats trap consists of a cleverly hidden tripwire that releases a {@creature swarm of bats} from a wooden cage 20 feet above. The bats attack anyone in the passageway. A successful {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check discovers the tripwire, which can be stepped over (no roll required) or disarmed with a successful {@dc 10} Dexterity (thieves' tools) check.

{@b {@i Centipede Pit.}} The pit trap consists of a well-disguised false floor covering a 10-foot drop into a pit. Three {@creature giant centipede||giant centipedes} attack anyone falling into the pit. A successful {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check discovers the false floor. PCs can skirt its edge with ease.

entries.name: Area 1: Entry

entries: The shoulder joint of a massive wing protrudes from the side of a hill. The bone has been hollowed out into a makeshift tunnel, and the osseous walls, floor, and ceiling are covered in strange smudge paintings that depict canine-like humanoids. Piles of bones and broken tools lie in heaps outside the entryway.

Of all the areas in the mines, the entry is the most likely to be trapped. In addition to the previously described traps, the entry is guarded by {@creature kobold} sentries. Unless great care is taken to eliminate the sentries, they alert the warren to the presence of intruders via whistles that, when blown, emit a single eerie note. The kobolds in the mines are generally on edge, but luring the sentries away from their position with intriguing sounds or flashing lights is not difficult. A secret tunnel just inside the entry is found with a successful {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check. The tunnel exits deep in the reaches.

entries.name: Area 2: Nexus

entries: The tunnel widens into a large, irregularly shaped chamber. Crude pots of crimson soil line the eastern wall. A smudge painting of a massive, winged creature dominates the room. A number of nest-like beds lie scattered on the earthen floor.

In the likely event that the kobolds are aware of intruders in their warren, they fortify their living quarters at the wing's nexus. Several {@creature kobold||kobolds} take half cover positions near the entry to the nexus and use slings as the PCs approach. Rikir and a few kobold guards take half cover positions at the back of the chamber and use their slings when the PCs pass the entryway. After the PCs have reached the room, all remaining kobolds engage in melee and attempt to block the PCs from targeting Rikir and his guards. The marrow in the pots is magical, and a successful {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check reveals it is likely dangerous to consume.

entries.name: Area 3: The Reaches

entries: The tunnel narrows until you must crouch to continue. At the end, you discover an opening into a large stone cavern. Piles of excrement litter the floor, and shuffling noises sound from the darkness above.

The wing's tips extend deep into the ground. Several {@creature swarm of bats||swarms of bats} live in the deep reaches of the wing, and they keep their distance from the rest of the warren. The bats aren't controlled by the kobolds, but they recognize the kobolds as allies and defend the kobolds if not outnumbered. They do not consume the marrow.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Notable treasures in the mines include a pot of red paint made from the marrow. The paint is nearly impossible to remove from most surfaces, and it dimly glows in an unsettling crimson hue. Deep in the reaches is a perfectly preserved feather from the monster whose bones make up the mine. It makes an excellent +1 staff, or it could be processed into a quiver of +1 arrows by the proper craftsperson. Rikir is fond of coins and baubles and likely has a small hoard kept tucked away in the nexus.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: Who is threatened by the mine's existence? What can be learned of the leviathan from which the mines are made? What other, more dangerous foes lurk beyond the reaches of this place?

rows: {@b An adventure for four to six characters of 2nd level}

entries: We had to walk quite quickly to escape it. I'm nearly out of breath. Well, last I saw, it was sort of chugging along down Topaz Way. It tried to climb the hill up to the silks market, but I think whoever is inside got tired? Goblins, no doubt. No, I wouldn't say it was careening through the city on a path of destruction. Definitely not—still quite a nuisance.

entries.name: Background
entries: The nefarious master wrestler Dib, the goblin, is "terrorizing" the streets of the town (or city). Since his defeat in his roadside fortress, the would-be chieftain has plotted his revenge. Gathering to him a new batch of dim minions, Dib has transformed a stolen merchant wagon into a machine of war. The wagon is powered by several goblins inside who, while devoted to Dib, lack the strength to pedal the thing quickly or consistently. Dib's plan to spread havoc through the streets has resulted in something a bit more disappointing.
In this light-hearted and quirky adventure, the PCs must confront the war wagon, gain entry to it, and defeat its defenders. The lives of several potted plants and a few market stalls depend on it!

entries.name: Running the Adventure

entries: A wagon that otherwise might haul crates of food to market has been capped with a crude wooden turret. The carpentry evident here is suspect. The turret is composed of old boards and rusted shields. Wherever gaps exist between the wagon and the turret, more wood was hastily nailed on. Multiple slits in the walls of the wagon and its cap allow its passengers to see out into the street. Small dead animals have been nailed to the wheels. The sad carcasses turn slowly as the wagon lurches forward.

The body of the wagon is a little over 12 feet long and nearly 7 feet wide. The turret sits on the back half and extends the height of the vehicle to 10 feet. There is a reinforced door on the left side. It can be forced open with a successful {@dc 18} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check. There is an emergency hatch on the turret that can be similarly forced open. The wagon will lurch around attacking the party until it is stopped. The PCs may devise any number of ways to stop the wagon from moving and gain access to the troublemakers inside. Reducing the wagon to 0 hit points, setting it aflame, or destroying one wall are all viable strategies. See {@b Breached!} below if the party gains access to the interior of the wagon. The war wagon is designed as a challenge rating 2.
The wagon uses the statistics of a {@vehicle War Wagon|KPPreparedExpanded}.

{@b Breached!} If the wagon is reduced to 0 hit points, if the door is forced open, or if other conditions expose the goblins or force them to flee, the wagon is considered disabled and can take no further actions. The interior of the wagon is very cramped and not suitable for toe-to-toe fighting. In general, the goblins then clamber out of the wagon and attack the party in the street. They are cunning fighters and make use of cover, flanking, and combat tactics.

There are six {@creature goblin||goblins} inside the wagon, including {@creature Dib|KPPreparedExpanded}. They are loyal to their boss but are not above fleeing if the fight goes badly. They came to town in the wagon in hopes of finding loot and murdering citizens with their amazing machine. They are equally happy killing heroes and taking their things. The goblins carry their normal equipment.

{@b {@i Wrestling Moves.}} Dib and his crew were once ejected from their clan's stronghold for indiscriminate wrestling. They have since continued the sport and enjoy wrestling more than most things (though looting and murdering are still top of the list). Two goblins who are next to the same opponent can coordinate and use their action to attempt a clothesline maneuver.
{@i With surprising coordination, two goblins clasp forearms and with gleeful enthusiasm attempt to clothesline you. While their motions are practiced, their balance is suspect.}

{@b {@i Clothesline (Requires Two Goblins' Actions).}} {@atk mw} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft., 1 target. {@h}3 ({@damage 1d4 + 1}) bludgeoning damage, and the creature is knocked {@condition prone} and {@condition stunned} until the end of their next turn. If this attack is successful, each goblin initiating the clothesline must succeed on a {@dc 13} Dexterity saving throw or also fall {@condition prone}.

entries.name: In Your Campaign
entries: This adventure requires a street located in a town (or city). It mentions a street passing around a small monument. It assumes the town has residents that can be threatened by creatures at the goblin power level. The wagon attack is unexpected and requires the party to act immediately. A citizen, rushing past the party while escaping the wagon, informs them of the trouble.

The scenario is a perfect starting point for a campaign against nearby goblin forces. Dib is a disgruntled leader of a ragtag group of wrestling enthusiasts and miscreants. His antics, while silly and fun, could easily prompt a more serious and dangerous storyline.

entries.name: In Midgard
entries: The city of Savoyne has seen strange attacks by a new band of dust goblins. The goblins arrive with various hastily constructed siege weapons, making a nuisance of themselves. The goblins who travel through and stay in the city are not pleased with their brethren's attacks as it greatly increases the tension between the city's human residents and themselves. Dib and his war wagon are but one example of this strange onslaught. The druids of the Oaken Ring would also see an end to these assaults.

entries.name: In the Street

entries: The wagon is puttering around a small monument and greenspace. People have fled the area, though a few hesitant guards watch on from a safe distance.
{@b {@i Monument.}} Pick an appropriate statue for the town. It provides partial cover.
{@b {@i Guards.}} Town guards will not join the combat until the threat is clearly gone, at which point they arrive and deliver a few blows or otherwise try to look helpful.

entries.name: Wagon Interior

entries: The interior is cramped and hot. Scraps of food litter the floor, and a haze of goblin sweat fills your nose. A ladder at the back of the wagon leads to the crossbow turret. A simple pedal drive is assembled toward the front with a mostly ineffective stick for steering. A few crates sit on the floor. Something has been written on one side of the crates.

There is nothing obvious of value inside the wagon. Some of the goblins made crude seat cushions from fur and moss. The crates at the back are marked in Goblin with the word loot. The crates are entirely empty. The "cannon" is a heavy crossbow in excellent repair, and a stack of 30 bolts sits next to it. A successful {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check made while searching the wagon reveals a loose floorboard and hidden compartment that contains a fat sack of silver coins (203 sp) and a few bottles of cheap spirits (worth 7 gp).

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The residents are relieved Dib's wagon has been stopped. Aside from the treasure found inside the wagon, the PCs are rewarded with free food and drink for several nights. A reasonable bounty (25-50 gp) might be paid by the local guard or leader.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: The primary concern of the town is determining if this is an isolated act of chaos by one goblin or an opening salvo in a larger offensive. Perhaps a goblin boss egged Dib on in an attempt to assess the town's defenses. What other strange assaults lurch down the old merchant road toward the peaceful community?

rows: {@b An adventure for four to six characters of 2nd level}

entries: True, I was hired to sail them past the Witch's Teeth-four adventurers looking to earn a name. Who was I to throw vinegar on their fancies? I took 'em within a rowboat's jaunt of the door on the rock. I know as much of the place as any sailor. That being nothing. The man who built that door and its innards was known as Pallon the Pious, a pirate of some renown. Given his actions in life, I don't know how he made right with any god when he died. The adventurers? Well, I imagine you lot want me to take you out. Perhaps you'll find your answer there.

entries.name: Background
entries: A famous pirate captain came to worship a lawful god in his final years. After a lifetime of plundering, pillaging, scuttling, and murdering along the coastline, the fearsome Pallon the Merciless rebranded himself as Pallon the Pious. But a history of violence is a hard thing to reconcile, and the salty old dog slowly succumbed to madness. His most precious possession was a set of scales that reflected perfectly his own inner conflict. The {@i Scales of Misjudgment} are buried deep in the treasure room of his crazed rock-island vault.

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: At differing times (GM's discretion) throughout the party's exploration of the vault, the guilt of Pallon magically threatens the PCs. Each PC is compelled to tell one story from their past where they did a great wrong. There is no saving throw to avoid this compelled confession. After the story is told, the PC must succeed on a {@dc 10} Charisma saving throw to avoid incurring a level of {@condition exhaustion}.

At the beginning of each of the location's two combats, the cruel nature of Pallon magically threatens to seep into the PCs' personas. All PCs must succeed on a {@dc 10} Wisdom saving throw or become merciless for 3 rounds. While merciless, PCs cannot assist or target other PCs with helpful spells and abilities. Passive effects are unaffected. The GM must use their discretion when resolving this effect.

entries.name: Area 1: Door

entries: A silver cup is fitted into the center of the door with a small inscription carved above it. A gull watches you from a nearby perch. Its eyes reflect the dull gray waters.

The inscription reads, "Give to receive." A successful {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) or Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check uncovers trace amounts of dried blood in the cup. The door slides open when 3 hit points worth of blood is poured into the cup. The door is extremely resistant to physical damage (AC 17; hp 70). Nonmagical attacks made against the door with anything but a proper sledge have disadvantage to hit. A successful {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) or Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check reveals a small release mechanism that can be activated with a successful {@dc 17} Dexterity (thieves' tools) check.

entries.name: Area 2: Descent

entries: A tunnel descends below the water line. The stonework is crude and unfinished, and the floor is littered with loose stones. A thin layer of briny ooze coats the place. At the end of the tunnel, you discover a small chamber, rotting wooden planks piled in a corner.

The chamber at the bottom of the tunnel has one exit leading to {@area 4|5.4|u}. A successful {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check made in the entryway reveals skeletal remains that clutch a palm-sized stone with the word wrongteous carved into it. A successful {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check also reveals a secret passage leading to {@area 3|5.3|u}.

entries.name: Area 3: Prayer Room

entries: Descending the cramped passage, you emerge into a circular chamber with a simple stone altar along the far wall. Scattered on the floor are a dozen stone tablets with carved inscriptions. Four slumping figures occupy the space directly in front of the altar.

The tablets contain incoherent ramblings and prayers. They are at once exalting the virtues of an unnamed god and threatening to unleash wrath upon wrongdoers. The four figures will stand and turn in unison when the PCs approach. The {@creature zombie||zombies} burble, "Wrong," as they shamble to attack. A successful {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check made on the tablets reveals a cryptic message from Pallon: "Overcoming evil requires much wrongteousness."

entries.name: Area 4: Judgment Room

entries: Unlike the entryway, this chamber features carefully built stone walls. Some craftsmanship is evident in the stonework, and the far wall suggests the frame of a door sealed by rock. Heaps of stones sit on the floor.

A simple examination of the room reveals the stones are inscribed with the word wrongteous. The far wall houses the sealed door that leads to {@area 5|5.5|u}. Beside the door is a hole just large enough to pass a carved stone through. An inscription near the hole reads, "Do wrong to begin judgment. Do wrong again to do right." Passing a stone marked wrongteous through the wall initiates the following:

items: The door into the vault (if intact) seals.

Magical radiant light flashes throughout the vault. All PCs must succeed on a {@dc 10} Constitution check or be {@condition blinded} for a minute. Any undead in the vault take 2 radiant damage. Spellcasters recognize the light is radiant.

entries: After the light flashes (for the first time only), three {@creature shadow||shadows} emerge and attack the party. On every round of combat, another stone marked wrongteous falls into the judgment room from a hole above. The party may continue to pass stones through the hole at a rate of one per round. Doing so requires an action. The shadows take the damage each time, but the party risks blindness. When the shadows are defeated, a stone marked {@i righteous} falls from the ceiling. Passing the {@i righteous} stone through the hole opens all doors in the vault.

entries.name: Area 5: Treasure Room

entries: A simple wooden chest sits at the center of this small chamber. Seawater seeps through the walls, and the smell of the ocean is strong.

The chest contains the {@i Scales of Misjudgment}, a silver set of scales and weights. Additionally, a handwritten note, written by Pallon states, "Here be the truth, all things are not balanced, and neither good nor evil can be weighed against the other." The scales do not work, and they provide consistently random measurements. They are worth 75 gp.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: What was the incident that compelled Pallon to seek atonement? Perhaps the answer is out there on the seas—a secret story kept by a creaky first mate. Where did the wrongteous Pallon hide his real treasure, and who did he hire to construct this strange vault of traps and undead?

rows: {@b An adventure for four to six characters of 2nd or 3rd level}

entries: Out past the spires, in the tyrannical rays of the midnight sun, there are cracks in the surface of the ice. Those cold and lonely breaches, what stirs in their depths? What constellations twinkle on their rimy walls? The nomads knew. Their stories passed from mouth to ear. Imagine what is lost in the transcription. These dead pages full of ink—so much earnest work. And to what end? As though this scribbling could capture all the facets of a voice telling a story. I aim to visit one myself. The breaches in the ice. To have before me that which I have loved as I would a child. Bah, save your judgment. What stirs your heart to wander this far from comfort?

entries.name: Background
entries: The party arrives at an abandoned outpost in a frozen landscape. The outpost appears to have suffered some strange attack. A half-mad scholar from a distant city hides within. He was drawn to the region by his visions of a breach in the nearby ice—a breach he believes leads to the realms beyond the stars. Heading east, the party finds that the breach is no simple chasm, and its scaled guardian does not appreciate its work being interrupted.
In this frozen and otherworldly adventure, the PCs must overcome rimy insects, a void dragon wyrmling, and the pull of the breach itself.

entries.name: Running the Adventure

entries: The outpost's edifices and low walls are made from wood and ice. The simple gate at the southern edge is intact and open slightly. Around and throughout the ruins are holes in the frozen ground. There are no bodies, but even from a distance, supply crates and loaded sleds can be seen between the abandoned buildings. A thick layer of snow blankets everything.

{@b {@i Walls and Gate.}} There is little to be learned about the outpost's fate from its defenses. (The grubs burrowed under the walls in the night.) Masons and carpenters in the party recognize the great skill that went into building the reinforced ice walls. The technique is easy to pick up and may be useful to the party in their future adventures.

{@b {@i Holes.}} The holes are the openings for rime worm grub tunnels. PCs who originate from the region likely know what they are. A successful {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check reveals the holes are made from a burrowing action, though there are no obvious claw marks in the ice but instead undulating ridges, suggesting melting.

{@b {@i Buildings.}} The buildings are intact. They are rough, frontier-like structures with little in the way of comfort. Most are small cabins for one or two occupants. A storehouse contains 30 days' worth of rations, a dozen full wineskins, and nine complete explorer's packs. A search of the outpost reveals the former occupants left without taking their valuables. A total of 75 gp and 230 sp is collected from pouches, sacks, and footlockers.

{@b {@i Quil.}} Quil is living in one of the buildings but will hide (Stealth 14) under some furs when the party enters the outpost. He shows himself once he sees the party are explorers. With the party's appearance, Quil sees an opportunity to be escorted to the breach. He offers them his spell scrolls (three 1st-level wizard spells) and 34 gp if they agree to investigate the breach with him. He needs a night of rest and preparation before striking out.

{@b {@i Return of Rime Worm Grubs.}} Just as the party settles down to their watches and to camp for the night (or shortly after they arrive at the outpost), the {@creature rime worm grub|ToB|rime worm grubs} responsible for killing and dissolving the previous inhabitants of the outpost return. The grubs arrive all at once, rising from the frozen ground and attacking. There are two (CR 2) or three (CR 4) grubs in the encounter. Add {@creature swarm of insects||swarms of insects} (tiny necrotizing worms) to increase the challenge.

entries.name: Quil, Scholar (Madman)

entries: You can cover your eyes, but the light finds your skin and troubles your sleep. Tomorrow, I search east. In my dreams, I saw the spires there and between them a breach.
{@b {@i What He Wants Most.}} To witness a fabled breach in the ice and learn the truth about it.

{@b {@i Physical Traits.}} Quil is a thin human. He is only 30 years old, but his relentless pursuit of these breaches, poor diet, and relative isolation have taken a toll on his body. He is pale, frail, and limps slightly from an injury traveling to the north. His bloodshot eyes dart from place to place and sometimes linger-glassy with thought. A wet cough has settled in permanently, and his fingernails and hair show signs of malnutrition.

{@b {@i Personality/Roleplaying.}} Quil is an obsessive. He first learned of the breaches in his work as a scholar while studying cosmology in a library back home. Recent visions have inspired him to travel north, where he hopes to find a breach. He is single-minded in his determination to discover and witness one of them. He believes they are key to understanding the outer realms. He is prone to ranting about the constellations but is not insane—yet. Conversations with Quil are centered on his studies of the stars. He is uninterested in small talk and only occasionally responds to queries about his past. He prefers to talk about his research. Quil sees the party as a means to an end and offers them everything he can to secure their assistance. He offers no credible threat to adventurers and can be killed with little effort.
Quil knows the following:

items: Long dead nomads had stories of the breaches, talking about starry magic.
Spires matching those in his visions rise half a day to the east of the ruined outpost.
The breaches in the ice are connected to the outer realms somehow.
The outpost was abandoned a few years ago after some kind of attack or catastrophe. Quil arrived less than a week ago.

entries.name: In Your Campaign
entries: This adventure requires a frozen landscape and an abandoned outpost. It assumes the party is traveling through the region, happening upon the outpost by chance. At the heart of the adventure is a rift between worlds, guarded by a dangerous and enigmatic dragon.

The {@creature rime worm grub|ToB|rime worm grubs} and {@creature void dragon wyrmling|ToB} can be replaced with {@creature swarm of insects||swarms of insects} (adding a 10 ft. burrow speed) and a {@creature white dragon wyrmling}.
The scenario presents an opportunity to introduce other planes of existence and could be tied into stories involving extraplanar threats.

entries.name: In Midgard
entries: North of Bjeornheim, at the foot of the Reaching Mountains, lies the breach in the ice. The outpost belongs to the humans of Bjeornheim, and with no word from that distant place for several weeks, they grow concerned. The party is sent to investigate the outpost, armed with the information that a scholar named Quil was the last soul to travel in that direction.

entries.name: The Breach

entries: Icy spires rise like obelisks around the long chasm in the ice. Small points of light dance across the surface of the spires, alternating between frenetic movement and stillness. Steam rises from the chasm as some unseen heat melts the ice below. Rainbow-colored light spills out of the breach onto the snow at its rim. The light is hypnotizing and accompanied by a low hum.

{@b {@i Ice Spires.}} These 15-20-foot fingers of solid ice ({@b A}, {@b B}, {@b C}, {@b D}) are currently acting as conduits for the dragon's void magic. They store and deliver energy as required by the dragon as it further grows the breach. A successful {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check reveals subtle claw marks on the surface of the spires, tracing otherworldly sigils. PCs who start or end their turn within 10 feet of a spire must succeed on a {@dc 12} Wisdom save or use their reaction to move their speed toward the breach (or fall {@condition prone} if no reaction is available). A successful save negates further saves against this effect.

{@b {@i Breach.}} The breach represents a {@creature Void Dragon Wyrmling (Breach-Empowered)|KPPreparedExpanded|void dragon wyrmling's} attempts at opening a portal to the space beyond the stars. The wyrmling gains +1 to its AC and regenerates 7 hit points at the start of its turn as long as it is within 10 feet of the breach. Once each round, the dragon can call on the power of the breach to give it advantage against a saving throw.

The breach is 15 feet deep. In the decades it has been here, the dragon has managed to open a 1-foot-by-1-foot rift at the bottom of the breach. The breach calls to mortals who get close, inviting them to leap in. PCs who start or end their turn within 5 feet of the breach's edge must succeed on a {@dc 12} Wisdom saving throw or fall (15 ft.) into the breach. A PC who starts their turn in the breach must succeed on a {@dc 15} Wisdom saving throw or lose the ability to move or take any actions except to dig into the icy floor.

{@b {@i Void Dragon.}} The dragon attacks anything approaching the breach. At the end of its turn, as a lair action, the dragon may cause any spire to speak a dark utterance in the language of the stars. Any PCs within 100 feet of that spire must make concentration checks as though having received damage.

{@b {@i Quil.}} Unless physically subdued, the scholar is drawn into the breach in the first round, where he begins to dig. Void energy from the breach kills him at the beginning of the second round, and he is transformed into a dread {@creature specter} and an ally of the dragon. Quil is lost and attacks the party.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The wyrmling has been working here for decades. Over time, several groups of explorers and would-be heroes have fallen victim to the breach and its guardian. Amid the frozen corpses are 111 gp, 300 sp, two uncommon potions, and a {@i {@item Void-Touched Buckler|KPPreparedExpanded}}.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: This breach is not the only one. The old stories told of several such breaches. Perhaps there are larger and more dangerous gateways out there in the frozen wastes. What threat do these enigmatic portals pose to the region? Surely other, more malevolent beings have learned of the breaches.

entries: How can something so big move so fast?

entries.name: Background
entries: Just outside a large city, the Temple of Infinite Cleansing and Boundless Miracles provides divine magical services to those in need. The temple provides these services for a much smaller fee than is typical, so it sees a large number of visitors each day.

Some locals suggest that the temple is responsible for the strange corruption around its premises—a corruption spreading north more and more each year. City politicians and leaders are unwilling to hear this suggestion, as traffic to the temple provides trade and coin in the city.
When the PCs are hired to haul a box containing "spiritual waste" into the temple's subterranean heap, the truth is revealed.

{@b In Truth.} The source of the temple's divine magic is not High Priest Shali. Instead, Shali is the servant of a {@creature Blemish Harvester|KPPreparedExpanded|blemish harvester} (see {@area 3|7.3|u}), living in the shadowy caves below the temple. The blemish harvester serves as Shali's patron, giving her access to healing magic in return for "meals," consisting of collected harm, disease, and curses.

Recently, her patron has demanded more food than she can collect, so she has hired adventurers to be eaten in addition to regular meals. This plan has worked twice already. She has no reason to believe a new party will overcome her patron.
Here are just a few suggestions to bring the PCs into the adventure:

items: Seeking healing or curse removal services in the area, the party is directed to the temple. High Priest Shali offers to trade the party free healing if they agree to her quest.
While visiting the area on other business, the party is approached by Delos Greenapple at a tavern. He offers the party his quest and buys their food and drink for that day (10 sp maximum).

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: Decide how to engage the party in the adventure by having Shali hire them directly or by having Delos seek them out while they stay in the city.

{@b {@i Delos' Request.}} This halfling politician seeks out the party when within the city. He explains the temple is not above board, but he needs proof. He offers the party 500 gp to bring him evidence that the temple of Temple of Infinite Cleansing and Boundless Miracles is dirty after all.

{@b {@i Shali's Request.}} The high priestess needs the party to dispose of a box of spiritual waste. They must carry the waste into the dumping grounds below the temple. She explains that the caves are sometimes occupied by monsters, so the job is too dangerous for her and her attendants. She offers the party free healing and 300 gp to perform the task.
The following NPCs will be present for this adventure:

items: {@b {@i Bolnus the Blemish Harvester.}} Bolnus is a malevolent intelligence from the outer planes. Its motives are alien and difficult to grasp for those on the Material Plane. It arrived several hundred years ago and has spent its time moving from major city to major city, feeding on disease, curses, and the misery of mortals. Bolnus always has at least one minion whom it provides with minor restorative magics. Whenever its minion uses this magic, the cured harms take on a physical form, which Bolnus consumes to stay alive.

{@b {@i Delos Greenapple.}} Delos is a halfling in his late 90s. He is well fed and rosy-cheeked. He wears a green velvet suit and a tall black hat. Delos is running for city council and has been approached by several temples in the city with concerns about High Priestess Shali. He has taken up their cause as an election ploy and wants to hire adventurers to gain Shali's trust and see what's below the temple.

{@b {@i High Priestess Shali.}} The High Priestess ({@creature cult fanatic}) is a dwarf in her late 290s. Her hair is bright silver and straightened with oil and heat. She wears simple vestments, including a tabard, robes, hood, gilded cord as belt, and soft leather boots. She is rarely without a smile. She carries a small censor at her belt, which she lights occasionally, filling wherever she walks with cloying floral incense. Shali has served her patron, the blemish harvester, for nearly a century, moving from city to city as suspicion of her healing arts dictates. What Shali wants most is to satisfy her patron's hunger and thereby maintain her position of power and wealth. Shali has advantage on all Charisma ({@skill Deception}) checks thanks to her patron's magic. She is perpetually surrounded by four to six armed attendants ({@creature cultist||cultists}).

entries: Warlocks who spend more than six hours within a mile of the temple can feel the blemish harvester's presence: {@i You sense a powerful mind nearby...}

entries.name: Corruption
entries: The spreading corruption north of the temple is the waste product of Bolnus itself, which seeps into the ground. A PC trained in Arcana who investigates the corruption to the north can learn the following on a successful {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check:

items: The corruption is magical.
It is the byproduct of a magical process.
It could be cleansed with a {@spell hallow} spell.

entries.name: Spiritual Waste
entries: This simple wooden box is tightly sealed with nails. The holy symbol of the temple is stamped onto one side of the box.

The box weighs 10 pounds, and its contents behave like a liquid if the box is jostled or shaken. A {@spell detect magic} spell reveals that the box is magical but does not indicate a school of magic. The box can be opened with a successful {@dc 17} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check, or if it receives 10 damage in one blow (AC 12, damage threshold of 9).

Destroying the box immediately spills the contents in a 20-foot radius centered on the box. Creatures caught in the spill must succeed on a {@dc 16} Wisdom saving throw or be cursed. While cursed, the creature is {@condition blinded} and {@condition poisoned}. The curse ends if the blemish harvester is slain or if the cursed creature is targeted by a {@spell remove curse} spell.

entries.name: Negotiating with Bolnus
entries: The entity is strange and intelligent. It is willing to negotiate to save its life. A PC who wishes to converse with Bolnus must use an action and succeed on a {@dc 10} Charisma ({@skill Intimidation} or {@skill Persuasion}) check to convince the entity to listen. From there, use roleplaying or successful {@dc 12} ability checks to determine a PC's success in the negotiations. Ultimately, Bolnus agrees to vacate the temple if the party lures Shali and her attendants to its lair and slays them while it watches. Such a terrible betrayal will sustain Bolnus for a long time!

entries.name: Lair of the Blemish Harvester
entries: Six coral-like yellow growths ({@creature awakened shrub||awakened shrubs}) mill about the area, providing dim light throughout the lair. The growths are not aggressive and do not join combat, fleeing into the pit if attacked (subsequently plunging the lair into darkness).
{@b {@i Bolnus Approaches.}} The moment a living creature enters the lair, Bolnus begins climbing up the side of the pit. The sound is distinctly insectoid.
{@b {@i Stench.}} The lair is filled with noxious gas from the blemish harvester.

entries.name: Area 1: Mezzanine
entries: The high-ground area to the north of the map is filled with bats that have no interest in battle. The bats reveal the presence of the aberration in the pit if someone uses {@spell speak with animals} or a similar ability.

entries.name: Area 2: Winding Approach
entries: The stone pathway around the central pit is patrolled by three {@creature shadow||shadows} that happily feed on the strange evil of the blemish harvester. The shadows try to surprise the party once they are clear of the main entrance.

entries.name: Area 3: Pit
entries: The pit is 75 feet deep. The bottom of the pit is filled with foul-smelling ichor to a depth of 10 feet. Creatures submerged in the ichor must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition poisoned} for an hour. The pit serves as the living quarters of Bolnus the {@creature Blemish Harvester|KPPreparedExpanded|blemish harvester}. Bolnus attacks the PCs within a minute of arriving in the lair.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: If Bolnus is slain, Shali and her attendants flee into the city and hide. The husk of the slain blemish harvester is more than enough evidence for Delos to close the temple. The halfling rewards the party as promised. If the party agrees to kill Shali on behalf of Bolnus, the aberration honors its word and disappears. Delos can be shown the lair as proof that the temple was a site of corruption.
