entries: Yar, welcome to the Yipping Retreat! Today we party, for tomorrow we may walk the plank!

entries.name: Background
entries: It's been three months since the ambitious kobold Taglo Zide assaulted the pirate's tavern formerly known as the Singed Parrot. In that time, the collector of junk and promises has transformed the rum-soaked port into a resort of sorts. The newly named Yipping Retreat is a chaotic mix of kobold warren, rentable "lairs," and enslaved pirates, mingling in the hope of turning profit.

Naturally, such a place has brought dangers to the area. The local communities want the retreat destroyed while criminals, monstrosities, and evildoers of all stripes enjoy the instability that it brings to the region. Adventurers looking to make a name for themselves would do well to shut the place down.
Here are just a few suggestions to bring the PCs into the adventure:

items: The ruler of the region has offered 400 gp to anyone capable of shutting down the Yipping Retreat. They offer all the information found in {@b Intelligence Briefing} (see below) to assist the party in their effort.

The party meets a sailor and former pirate with an interesting story. For the price of a bottle of spirits, the sailor tells the tale of the Singed Parrot, a pirate's tavern now ruled by kobolds and housing monsters of all sorts. The sailor believes a great treasure sits below it, unbeknownst to the current proprietor. For a second bottle of spirits, he provides all the information in {@b Intelligence Briefing} (see below).

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: The following NPCs will be present for this adventure:

items: {@b {@i Admiral Fishfang.}} The half-orc Admiral Fishfang ({@creature thug}) is one of six pirate prisoners left alive from Taglo's assault on the Singed Parrot. He is tall and emaciated, owing to the kobold's poor treatment of their prisoners. His brown hair and beard are long, scraggly, and grown out. Fishfang was once a charismatic and energetic tavern keeper, but after months of imprisonment, he has lost all but the slightest glimmer of hope to escape. He might be recruited into a scheme to overthrow Taglo if he's convinced it would result in his freedom. He is unlikely to reveal the location of his treasure without exceptional convincing.

{@b {@i First Fist.}} Taglo's head of security and chief bouncer is a hardened {@creature First Fist|KPPreparedExpanded|ogre} known as First Fist, who is large even by ogre standards and possesses a great, curly tangle of crimson hair pulled into an enormous topknot. He plods around the resort, keeping guests and resident kobolds in line. First Fist has a special hatred for halflings and gnomes. His steel knuckles instill fear in most who see them, and they are layered with dried blood.

{@b {@i Taglo Zide.}} Taglo Zide ({@creature Junk Shaman|CCodex|kobold junk shaman}) is a slender-framed kobold elder with bright orange scales that fade to pale yellow. He always wears a sturdy suit of junk armor, preferring to sleep in it (despite the negative effects). Taglo is having the time of his life running the Yipping Resort. It has gone better than he ever imagined, and his confidence is at an all-time high. Taglo enjoys rummaging around the junk on the second floor of the resort, drinking with orcs (provided First Fist is there to keep order), and "fishing" with his fire magic.

entries.name: Intelligence Briefing
entries: Deliver the following information to the party as needed:

items: The Yipping Retreat is run by the kobold Taglo Zide, a clever and charismatic collector of junk.
The place was formerly called the Singed Parrot and was run by a half-orc pirate known as Admiral Fishfang.
The kobolds slew most of the pirates when they took over, but some were spared and now work as prisoners to keep the place running.
Taglo's chief of security is an ogre known as First Fist.
The kobolds rent rooms to those who can pay, and their clientele has included orcs, hobgoblins, goblins, ogres, and lizardfolk.
Taglo keeps crocodiles as pets and guards.
Rumors suggest Admiral Fishfang buried a pirate's hoard of treasure below the place.
Constant chaotic revelry fills the place.
The second floor is filled to the rafters with Taglo's junk treasure. It is no longer a usable space.

entries.name: Resort Events
entries: Roll a {@dice d8} on the Resort Events table to determine what's happening at the resort when the PCs show up, or pick something appropriate. In general, an event lasts one day.

entries.caption: Resort Events
rows: {@b {@i Bad Wine.}} Any humanoid creature staying at the Yipping Retreat suffers the effects of drinking spoiled wine. They have disadvantage on all Constitution saving throws.

{@b {@i Big Yips.}} A traveling kobold entertainer sings drinking songs in {@area 2|8.2|u}, inspiring those in attendance. All kobolds have advantage on saving throws against spells and effects that would make them {@condition frightened}.

{@b {@i Craaaaaaabs!}} One hundred crabs have escaped their pots. The place is crawling with the pinching crustaceans, and there are plenty of pinches to go around. During combat in any area of the retreat, on initiative count 20, losing all ties, two random combatants must succeed on a {@dc 10} Dexterity saving throw or take 2 piercing damage.

{@b {@i Lost Coin Purse.}} First Fist lost his coin purse and has enlisted the resident kobolds to help him find it. Because of their high state of alert, kobolds gain a +5 bonus to passive Perception checks.

{@b {@i Magic Wine.}} Any humanoid creature staying at the Yipping Retreat gains the benefits of drinking magical elven wine. They have advantage on all saving throws against spells and magical effects.
{@b {@i New Junk.}} Taglo has spread an extraordinary amount of junk around the floor of the resort. All areas are considered difficult terrain.

{@b {@i Parties Unending.}} The revelry has increased dramatically! Dancing, whooping, and general pandemonium spread throughout the place. Ability checks to perform Deception, Sleight of Hand, Stealth, or to otherwise blend into the crowd have advantage.
{@b {@i Wet Wood.}} Someone threw wet wood on the hearths. The entire resort is filled with smoke. All areas are lightly obscured.

entries.name: Yipping Retreat Encounters
entries: Roll a {@dice d8} on the Yipping Retreat Encounters table to add encounters for the PCs or to modify or replace existing ones, or pick something appropriate.

entries.caption: Yipping Retreat Encounters
rows: Eight {@creature kobold||kobolds} clean the mess from the previous day's party.
Four {@creature kobold||kobolds} help an {@creature orc} guest to their table.
{@creature First Fist|KPPreparedExpanded|First Fist} (ogre, 91 hit points) and two {@creature kobold||kobolds} patrol, keeping peace.
Three {@creature crocodile||crocodiles} pad across the planks, looking for food.
Three veteran kobold warriors ({@creature Elite Kobold|CCodex|kobold elite}) play dice and drink.
A mess of ten {@creature goblin||goblins} eats raw fish and squabbles over pints of ale.
{@creature Junk Shaman|CCodex|Taglo Zide} and {@creature First Fist|KPPreparedExpanded|First Fist} (ogre, 91 hit points) move wooden crates of junk around the retreat.
Roll twice.
variable

entries.name: Area 1: Beach Landing
entries: The beach and connecting docks to the east are routinely patrolled by crocodiles and kobolds. The kobolds use the rowboats as fishing vessels with limited success. At least two {@creature crocodile||crocodiles} await anyone trying to land here without a proper kobold escort.

entries.name: Area 2: Tavern Room
entries: This large chamber is used to serve patrons and host parties. The stairs go to the now-inaccessible second floor. The secret passage to {@area 6|8.6|u} is the tavern's most well-known secret. The barrel is partially moved aside, allowing anyone looking at the barrels to easily discover the passage. An {@creature Elite Kobold|CCodex|elite kobold} (see Creature Codex) sits at the bar sipping ale. Three {@creature kobold||kobolds} scamper around serving drinks to the patrons.

entries.name: Area 3: Patio and Storage Tower
entries: Guests of the Yipping Retreat can often be found drinking and eating on makeshift patio furniture here. The tower is used to store 75 gp worth of dried food and ale. Three {@creature orc||orcs} lounge in the rickety patio chairs. One is completely asleep.

entries.name: Area 4: Prisoner's Quarters
entries: The prison workers and Admiral Fishfang are kept in this area when they aren't working the bars or cleaning the floors of the retreat. It is accessible via a guarded door and passage north of {@area 1|8.1|u}. From sunrise to midnight, Fishfang ({@creature thug}) and his five remaining crew ({@creature commoner||commoners}) sleep here.

entries.name: Area 5: Abandoned Dock
entries: The small sailing vessels and rowboats moored here have been abandoned by their owners and are generally ignored by the current residents. They are in various states of repair, though several are seaworthy. A {@creature plesiosaurus} lurks in the waters just by the boats. The monster is partially domesticated by the kobolds, who feed it regularly. It attacks any non-kobold creature who gets too close.

entries.name: Area 6: Storage Area
entries: {@creature First Fist|KPPreparedExpanded|First Fist} (ogre, 91 hit points) spends a great deal of time patrolling from {@area 6|8.6|u} and {@area 7|8.7|u}, guarding the stores. {@area 6|8.6|u} contains 100 gp worth of wine, spirits, and ale. Buried a few feet in the bare earth is Fishfang's treasure. A successful {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check while searching this area discovers evidence of the chest buried here, which contains 275 gp, 300 sp, 700 cp, a carved ivory narwhal (worth 50 gp), and a finely crafted, silver spyglass (worth 1,200 gp).

entries.name: Area 7: Tower
entries: This tower, accessible only from the interior passage, is used as storage for the tavern. Occasionally the tower serves as a rented room, in which case beds and other furnishings are dragged into the tower's lower level. The tower houses 100 gp worth of trade goods (spices, bolts of cloth, silver cups) that Taglo and his crew have stolen from passing caravans and trade ships.

entries.name: Area 8: Taglo's Quarters
entries: This small room once served as Admiral Fishfang's quarters and map room. Now, Taglo resides here among small piles of junk. Taglo keeps 2,000 sp in a large, locked chest ({@dc 14} to open) in the corner. He uses the silver to pay his kobold crew, who mostly return it to him through gambling and alcohol purchases.

entries.name: Area 9: Tavern Room
entries: Like {@area 2|8.2|u}, this chamber is used to host parties and entertain guests. A VIP table sits on an elevated platform in the western corner of the room: five {@creature Hobgoblin (Unshielded)|KPPreparedExpanded|hobgoblin} soldiers are currently being served there. They wear their armor and carry their longswords but do not have their longbows or shields (reducing AC to 16).

entries.name: Area 10: Garbage and Latrine
entries: This small room serves as the retreat's garbage disposal and toilets. A gaping hole, leading to untold depths (and filth), is surrounded by rickety safety fencing. A three-seat, makeshift outhouse can be found here as well.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: Did the PCs dispatch Taglo or maybe make a better deal? With Taglo gone, perhaps the party takes control of the port, flexing their entrepreneurial spirit. But other adventurers are sure to challenge their claim over time. Or maybe Fishfang takes it off their hands when the party realizes they're not finished with the adventuring life.

entries: Zombies! And goblins! And a war machine!!!

entries.name: Background
entries: Briarskin, the Gentle Necromancer, knew it was a mistake to hire goblins. Never again.

The goblins' leader, Dib Halfling-Chewer, spun her a magnificent tale of spies keeping an eye on pesky neighbors, of goblin cunning being at her command. So she betrayed her instincts and hired his shabby band, inviting them into her thorny lair where her whims were served by unquestioning undead.
Therein, she had just created her latest and greatest treasure—a war machine powered by a bound fire elemental—and intended to use the contraption to bring her neighbors to their knees.
Alas, Dib has a weak spot for such devices. As soon as he saw it, he had to have it and was already planning to steal it.

He soon succeeded and intended to test his stolen prize's capabilities by flattening the shabby little village of Thorns Mouth, a place he thinks very ill of, having once spent a night there as a prisoner and being tormented and laughed at by locals. Now they will pay.
Briarskin became terribly cross—as cross, in truth, as only a necromancer can be—and is readying an undead force to meet Dib's warband.
In the meantime, the locals of Thorns Mouth, alerted by their druid leader's awakened raven (who frequently makes spying missions nearby), have sent word to their ruler for urgent help.
Answering it are a rag-tag band of adventurers...!

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: The PCs, hired to go to the villagers' aid, arrive to find them in a panic-everyone save the {@creature druid} leader Dotterel and the awakened {@creature raven} Catchfly, hiding in {@area 2|9.2|u}. The PCs should have a few hours to organize a hasty defense, during which time they may use Catchfly to spy on their foe (soon to be {@i foes}).

entries.name: Multiple Foes
entries: This encounter features a three-way battle between the PCs and villagers, the goblins, and Briarskin's zombie horde.

The villagers are elderly (all the young folk went to the city long ago to seek their fortunes). Aside from the {@creature druid}, there are six able-bodied locals who {@i could} fight if encouraged by a rousing speech, and a successful {@dc 10} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check convinces them (treat as {@creature bandit||bandits}) to do just that. The other 30 locals ({@creature commoner||commoners}) are desperate not to fight but could help build defenses. If asked to do something dangerous (like putting out fires with goblins about), they do so half the time, fleeing to the cave if their courage fails them.
In combat, Catchfly can catch one {@creature scorpion} and drop it a foe every 3 rounds.

The villagers are sheep farmers (with 200 sheep scattered throughout the map). These are tended by six scrawny sheepdogs who bark a lot but are non-combative. However, a successful {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling}) check directs a hound to drive one or more clustered sheep 30 feet in a particular direction for a round. This may be useful in injuring sheep-riding goblins.

Briarskin ({@creature Briarskin|KPPreparedExpanded|mage}, replacing {@i greater invisibility} spell with {@spell blight}) is here for her war machine, and she commands 20 {@creature zombie||zombies}. At the start of the battle, she directs a dozen zombies, all wearing rags, to attack the machine, which ends very messily for the zombies. Play out the scene as a simple slaughter to show the machine's prowess, or perhaps have a few zombies escape and fight on. Keeping the rest back to use as she feels best, she tries to stay away from fighting herself, using spells to attack approaching foes. She escapes via a {@spell fly} spell if in peril or if the fire elemental approaches.

The goblins are here to cause havoc, of course. Dib uses the machine to try to flatten every building in the village, while his Sisters of Ruin—three goblins, each a {@creature spy} mounted on a {@creature worg}—ride about setting fire to things. Like the other 12 {@creature goblin||goblins} with them, they each have a dozen oil-tipped arrows and four torches.

The presence of so many sheep brings the goblins great joy, and they often mount and ride them, which then move 30 feet in a random direction while bleating. Use Dexterity ability checks to resolve any issues.
In a melee between a goblin and a zombie, roll {@dice 1d6}: on 1-3, the goblin is slain, and on 4-6, vice versa. Where two opponents attack a single foe, their side has advantage on the roll.

entries.name: Prepare for Battle
entries: Give the PCs a few hours to rouse the villagers and prepare the village for battle. This may be as simple as formulating a plan but could involve digging pits, building walls, and laying traps. Digging a 5-foot pit in the rocky ground and roughly covering it takes four characters 2 hours: such pits slow the machine's movement by 5 feet that round, and a 10-foot-long pit would slow it by 10 feet, and so on, though covering anything longer needs cunning or magic. Deeper pits can only be dug by magic as bedrock lies about 5 feet below the surface.

There are plenty of big stones about, and building a big pile (5-foot square) takes the same time as a pit and would slow the machine by 10 feet. The low walls do nothing to stop the machine's progress.
Be prepared to make quick judgements on other ideas.

entries.name: Facing the Beast of Dib
entries: A screaming, fiery beast of metal sheathed in aged oak, the {@vehicle Dib's War Machine|KPPreparedExpanded|war machine's} imprisoned fire elemental roars its hatred but obeys a control lever, which directs it up to 30 feet per round in any direction. The {@vehicle Dib's War Machine|KPPreparedExpanded|machine} is about 15 feet long and 10 feet wide. A hefty oak-and-iron shed sits atop it, which has a reinforced hatch at the back that can be forced with a successful {@dc 20} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check.

The PCs may have any number of ways to stop the machine. If it is reduced to 0 hit points, it is destroyed, releasing the fire elemental. As well as Dib (use statistics for a {@creature veteran}), there are six other whooping, laughing goblins within. The war machine is designed as a challenge rating 4.

entries.name: Area 1: Thorns Mouth
entries: Surrounded by scrubby thorns and deep valleys of unclimbable loose sandstone, Thorns Mouth consists of single-story adobe houses with thatched rooves. These burn admirably, so if hit by a torch or flaming arrow, the building catches fire, a character can extinguish these flames in 3 rounds, but otherwise, the flames devour the building. Anyone entering a burning building takes 14 ({@damage 4d6}) fire damage. Buildings burn for about 5 minutes. The war machine and its passengers are immune to fire damage.

entries.name: Area 2: Big Cave
entries: This large, cool cave holds supplies, and it hides a pond fed by an underground spring. Most of the villagers seek safety here—or would like to.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: If the PCs defeat the goblins and drive off (or kill) Briarskin, they are surrounded by the remaining villagers and cheered and paraded about. Later, they are honored with a feast, at which a special song is sung about them.
If at least half the houses in the village remain standing at the end, give the PCs an additional 25 percent XP reward.
But what of Briarskin's lair? Is now the time to strike her foul, thorny chambers? Has she fled there, awaiting the PCs with her truly horrid undead servants?

rows: {@b An adventure for four to six characters of 3rd or 4th level}

entries: We have drunk from the lake for a generation—its waters have quenched the thirst of chieftains! Poison, it is all poison now.

entries.name: Background
entries: A small band of centaurs have seen their water source fouled by unknown magic. When word of their plight reaches the PCs, they embark on a day's travel to the centaur camp. Along the way, they encounter injured wildlife and panicked bugbears. Terrifying storms beset the region, raining down acid and ooze. Agreeing to investigate the small, corrupted lake, the adventurers discover a long-buried evil has awakened-bringing with it oozing undead.
In this strange and gruesome adventure, the PCs must navigate the wilds, face the ooze storms, and confront a reanimated warrior who betrayed her god.

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: The party discovers the centaurs' plight while visiting a town in the region. A traveling merchant brings the news as she and her caravan have recently passed through the affected area. The merchant can meet the party in an inn where they are both staying or as the heroes purchase supplies in the local markets. She reveals the following information:

items: A clan of centaurs living nearby are plagued by strange storms.
The centaurs report their water source, a small lake, has been fouled.
The storms bring black rain that smells of death.
To make matters worse, bugbear warbands have been attacking the centaurs lately. They can spare no scouts to investigate the befoulment of their lake.
She traded with them before arriving here, and they seemed desperate.

entries: The merchant also provides instructions to find the centaur camp.

entries.name: What's Happening at the Lake?
entries: The entryway to the tomb of a long-forgotten evil has surfaced in the center of the lake. The tomb contains the buried remains of a hero who broke a sworn oath to her god. She and her accomplices were buried alive by the god's followers many years ago. Though her bones and flesh turned to dust long ago, her black heart persisted-growing in power and malevolence through the years. Eventually, the heart coalesced a new, oozing body to inhabit and in the process conjured strange storms and corrupted the small lake.

The tomb is now open, and dead things crawl from it. The magical storms herald her re-emergence. Choose an appropriate god for the campaign, and complete the story of the betrayal in a manner true to the game world. A few questions to help complete the narrative quickly:

items: Who is the god that was betrayed?
What was the nature of the broken oath?
Who was the betraying hero?
What does the re-animated oathbreaker want now?

entries.name: Traveling to the Centaur Camp
entries: The camp is 20 miles from the town. The road into the camp is good and traveled often. The party may use the road to travel 15 miles, at which point they will have to walk across the open plain. The party should encounter a rancid rainstorm on the way to the centaurs. Additionally, crossing the wilds is inherently risky, and challenging the heroes with a medium/hard difficulty encounter or two is appropriate:

items: {@b {@i Panicked Bugbears.}} Three (CR 4) or five (CR 5) {@creature bugbear||bugbears} are fleeing the site of a recent ooze storm. Their trajectory intercepts the heroes as they navigate a shallow ravine. The bugbears attack recklessly, and heroes with a high Wisdom modifier, or those trained in Insight, recognize that the creatures are spooked. One of them is badly burned on its legs and struggles to keep pace with its brethren. The brutes carry a variety of pillaged coins and jewelry worth 200 gp in total.

{@b {@i Tigers in the Grass.}} Two (CR 4) or three (CR 5) {@creature saber-toothed tiger||saber-toothed tigers} attempt to ambush the party as they ascend a small hill. The tigers strike at one target initially, attempting to bring it down, before dealing with the rest of the heroes. The tiger's bodies show strange burn marks and scars. A successful {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check reveals the burns are fresh and acidic in nature. Each pair of teeth from the tigers fetches 50 gp.

entries.name: Ooze Storms

entries: The dark sky crackles menacingly. Though no wind stirs the grass of the plains, the clouds move rapidly toward you. A few drops of blackened water fall onto your shoulders, and a strong scent of decay rises from the viscous precipitation. And then they begin to fall—masses of coal-colored ooze.

Choose when the party encounters the ooze storms. They appear suddenly and with little warning, so they might be added to a combat to increase its challenge. Shelter is hard to find on the plains, so the party should be rewarded for ingenious plans to mitigate and defeat the ooze storms. There are two distinct types of ooze storms in the region.

{@b {@i Oozers.}} The oozer storm clouds are much darker than the rancid rain clouds. A few oily drops fall but are quickly replaced by more menacing goopy tendrils that reach from the clouds to the ground. The oozer storm initially drops three {@creature gray ooze||gray oozes} near the party and then one (CR 4) or two (CR 5) {@creature ochre jelly||ochre jellies} at the beginning of the second round.

{@b {@i Rancid Rains.}} The sky crackles with lightning, and clouds gather. A viscous black rain falls on the region. Creatures caught in the rain are pelted with stinking droplets. The rain visibly affects the surrounding flora, causing it to wither, blacken, and die. Creatures exposed to the rain must make a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw, taking 6 ({@damage 1d10}) acid damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. The saving throw is repeated each minute the creature remains in the rain. A typical rancid rain lasts 5 minutes.

entries.name: In Your Campaign
entries: This adventure requires a small town (or city) and a small lake. It assumes the party encounters a traveling merchant. A journey through grasslands or plains with storms on the horizon is mentioned.
The {@creature gray thirster|ToB|gray thirsters} can be replaced with {@creature ghast||ghasts}.

The scenario requires the GM to decide a key story element: choosing a god from the game world's pantheon and adding a few details about a broken oath. The meeting with the oathbreaker can be a straight combat or an opportunity to further the story—perhaps the oathbreaker was unjustly killed or perhaps she now seeks redemption.

entries.name: In Midgard
entries: This adventure is set on the Rothenian Plain. The party's own business takes them wandering into the territory of the khan. In one of the wheeled cities, the PCs discover the centaurs' plight. The tomb belongs to a priest of Svarog, who fell to greed and murder. The priest along with several acolytes were buried alive in the tomb.

entries.name: Centaur Camp

entries: The centaur camp consists of six massive tents built around a central fire pit. Everywhere are large sacks strung together with leather strips. The exterior walls of the hide tents feature freshly painted symbols in white paint. Several of the massive creatures greet you at the camp's periphery. Their spears appear fashioned from whole, slender trees.

The leader of this small centaur band, Yarnak, joins his guards in greeting the party as they arrive at the camp. Yarnak is caught in a difficult position: he must keep his band together in the event the bugbears attack, so he cannot investigate the situation at the lake. The centaur camp is running out of water though, and they are loathe to abandon the camp as it has history and meaning to them. He offers the party a tidy chest of gold (500 gp) and a pair of {@i {@item Centaur Wrist-Wraps|KPPreparedExpanded|centaur wrist-wraps}} as a reward for dealing with the befoulment of the lake. He provides the following information:

items: The lake is 2 miles from the centaur camp.
The last visit made to the lake revealed the water had turned brackish and foul smelling.
A strange stone structure had risen from the ground on a small island near the middle of the lake.
The ooze storms are frequent near the lake.

entries.name: Dead Lake

entries: The small lake stretches out before you. Its water is the color of smoke and covered in sickly yellow foam. An old raft has been pulled ashore nearby, its condition suspect. In the center of the lake is a speck of land with a single tree. From a distance, you can see a half-sunken structure of some kind. The dirt beside the grimy stone walls looks recently churned.

The centaurs' watering hole is fouled by the evil risen in the middle of the lake. Animals avoid this area. Plant life along the banks of the lake has blackened and died. Milling around the edge of the lake eventually results in an attack by the undead drawn to the evil site.

{@b {@i Foul Waters.}} A successful {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check allows the party to notice streams of viscous-looking material pouring from the tomb on the island into the lake. Divine casters and heroes trained in Religion recognize that the befoulment is necromantic in origin.

The raft can be used to transport the party onto the island. The raft is visibly degraded. Unless repaired, the raft disassembles and dumps the party into the water just off the island. A successful {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check allows the party to repair the raft for use to and from the island.

The water here is poison. Creatures who drink the water must make a {@dc 20} Constitution saving throw, taking 21 ({@damage 6d6}) poison damage and being {@condition poisoned} for an hour on a failed save or half as much damage and no additional effects on a successful one. Creatures partially submerged or exposed to the water in a substantial way must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution save or be {@condition poisoned} for an hour.

{@b {@i Unquenchable Thirst.}} The betrayer was not buried alone. Her servants and accomplices were buried alive with her. They died horribly of thirst while lying in the stony darkness, able to hear the lapping water of the lake just out of reach. Two (CR 4) or four (CR 7) {@creature gray thirster|ToB|gray thirsters} rise from the water and attack the party as they consider how to cross the water.

entries.name: Oathbreaker's Tomb

entries: A shadowed entrance into a small tomb has broken the surface of the ground. Thick black ooze flows from the tomb, across the island, and into the lake. As you approach, a bony hand covered in oily black slime grasps the side of the entrance. "Who comes to welcome me?"
The tomb is small (only 10 feet by 10 feet) and half-submerged in mud and dark water. The walls inside are marred with scratch marks made decades ago.

{@b {@i Oathbreaker.}} She does not attack immediately but instead attempts to engage the PCs in conversation. Her aim is to determine if they might help her achieve her goal. Depending on what she wants (perhaps revenge or salvation), the party may agree to help or may refuse and kill her. In combat she ({@creature mummy}) is joined by one (CR 4) or two (CR 5) {@creature gray ooze||gray oozes}, which slough off her repulsive form with a sickening, wet sound. Slaying the oathbreaker ends the fouling magic and ooze storms. The water in the lake returns to normal within a month. Alternatively, the oathbreaker may end her necromancy if the party aids her to achieve her goal.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: As agreed, and provided the oathbreaker's magic has ended, the centaurs provide the party with the gold and {@i {@item Centaur Wrist-Wraps|KPPreparedExpanded|centaur wrist-wraps}}. The tomb contains no valuables, for the oathbreaker and her accomplices were stripped of their wealth before being buried.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: Depending on the nature of the betrayal, there are many directions to go. Does the party embark on a quest to redeem the oathbreaker? Perhaps the tomb serves as the entrance to a larger structure built under the lake—a grim repository for those who displeased their god.

rows: {@b An adventure for four to six characters of 3rd or 4th level}

entries: Gathered at the bottom of a low hill topped by a tall tower, the fey folk of Drywood Hall have gathered. A cacophony of cries, singing, and instruments begins as Danae stands with her arms raised, magic cascading from her fingers. Procession has begun!

entries.name: Background
entries: It is time for the fey inhabitants of Drywood to awaken the caretaker of their forest to make it safe from seasonal wildfires. Each year, at the beginning of summer, representatives from the fey communities send delegations to take part in an event they call Procession. During this time, the delegates sing and dance and engage in revelry while walking the winding path to their patron's home. Provided the procession is adequately boisterous, the old bear awakens and summons torrential rains to soak the forest.

This year, the forest fires have started early, and the fey folk of Drywood scramble to organize their Procession. Called to the forest by a promise of gold and allyship, the PCs arrives to a great disorder of fey creatures. Though the community is more than capable of organizing themselves, some delegates have demands that must be met before joining the effort. Complicating matters further, the forest fires have drawn minor fire spirits to the Drywood, who happily interfere with the Procession.
Hired by the dryad Danae, the party must negotiate stubborn fey and fiery threats in equal measure as they ensure that the Procession is successful.
Here are a just a few suggestions to bring the PCs into the adventure:

items: The party encounters a flock of {@creature flithidir|ToB2} fleeing ahead of a growing forest fire. One of the avian fey creatures implores the party to help them reach Drywood Hall, the gathering place for fey in the region. Once there, Danae finds and hires them to help safeguard the Procession.

The towns around the Drywood are visited by {@creature awakened tree||awakened trees} that bear paper messages offering 700 gp to those willing to help Drywood Hall. The trees can lead would-be heroes back to the hall.

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: The following NPCs will be present for this adventure:

items: {@b {@i Danae.}} Danae is the current elder in charge of Drywood Hall, the fey gathering place in the forest of Drywood. Danae chooses to appear as a copper-skinned humanoid with midnight-black hair that stands a foot upright from her head. Her emerald robes are magically conjured with a leafy pattern similar to scale armor. She speaks in a commanding voice, and her utterances are often accented by the sound of trees groaning in the wind. Danae wants the procession to occur as quickly as possible to extinguish the fires threatening the forest. She is a staunch defender of the hall and her forest home. Danae has the power to summon four {@creature awakened tree||awakened trees} once each day (as an action). She uses this power only to defend herself, the Drywood Hall, or the Drywood Forest itself.

{@b {@i Eely (Delegate).}} Upon the branches of a nearby tree is a {@creature flithidir|ToB2} named Eely. She is overwrought by the early arrival of the wildfires. She flits and flaps in a panic. As is typical to her kind, Eely is obsessed with the new and novel. Charisma checks to calm her must include facts, songs, riddles, or rhymes she has not heard. Eely's request is the retrieval of a sun nut, a small golden berry that grows on nearby shrubs. Finding a sun nut requires 20 minutes of searching and a successful {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check.

{@b {@i Goodrich (Delegate).}} Weeping on a toadstool near the hall is a {@creature fragrant one|ToB2} named Goodrich, who is traumatized by being alone on this journey to Procession. They routinely curl into a ball and weep. Charisma checks to calm Goodrich must be assurances that they are not alone and that friends are all around. Goodrich's request is for a PC to swear to be their best friend during the Procession. A PC agreeing to this must carry Goodrich on their back, reducing their speed(s) to 15 feet until the Procession ends.

{@b {@i Ob (Delegate).}} Huffing and stamping near the Drywood Hall is a {@creature scrofin|ToB2} named Ob, whose fear of the fires has expressed itself in a need for contest and physical exercise. Charisma checks to calm Ob must be bold and overthe-top tales of intimidating conquest and great feats of strength. Ob's request is a series of wrestling matches with each PC, taking a total of 20 minutes. The wrestling matches are determined using opposing Strength ({@skill Athletics}) checks. Win or lose, if each PC wrestles Ob, he joins the Procession.

entries.name: Arrive at Drywood Hall
entries: Before you is a three-tiered meeting hall made of stillliving trees growing into each other. A wide stair rises from the forest floor into the hall proper. All around you, fey creatures run, flit, and phase in a chaotic pattern of color and sound.
Roll a {@dice d4} and consult the {@b Drywood Hall Events} table to determine one or more random events occurring at Drywood Hall while the party is there, or choose something appropriate.

entries.caption: Drywood Hall Events
rows: A Large "ball" of squirrels is rolling around the hall, threatening to crush objects and creatures. Creatures caught in its path must succeed on a {@dc 10} Dexterity saving throw or take 7 ({@damage 2d6}) bludgeoning damage. A successful {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}), Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling}), or Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check can disband the squirrel ball.
Creatures within the hall itself are affected by a {@spell bless} spell. While affected, the creatures' limbs extend and shorten (painlessly) at random.

The panic of the fey creatures takes physical form in a thick layer of grass growing on most surfaces of the hall. This includes creatures, who find their clothes and armor covered in gently waving blades of grass. The grass regrows quickly if cut or damaged. Creatures affected by the grass find that their druid or ranger spells are cast one level higher than normal until they are 100 feet or more away from the hall.

The squabbling of two satyrs has manifested as a proliferation of reeking mushrooms all around the exterior of the hall. Creatures in the area must succeed on a {@dc 10} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition poisoned} until they leave. A successful {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check allows the party to fashion face coverings that nullify the effects of the stench.

entries.name: Meet with Danae

entries: Before you stands a tall humanoid in emerald-colored robes. Her long black hair rises from her scalp as though drawn toward the sky by magic.

Danae offers the party 700 gp from Drywood Hall's coffers if they agree to help her organize the Procession. While Danae busies herself with the magic required to awaken the hall's patron, she needs the party to calm and organize the unruly delegates before the procession can occur. She explains that the party must meet with the three delegates and convince them to join the procession before it starts in an hour. Danae reveals the following if asked:

items: The Procession is an ancient community event to awaken the Drywood Hall's patron deity from their slumber.
The patron is required to prevent the Drywood from succumbing to wildfires.
The patron is currently in the shape of a slumbering bear.
The patron resides in a tower nearby, which the fey creatures will march to shortly.

entries.name: Meeting the Delegates
entries: Successfully calming and organizing a delegate allows them to join the Procession. Failure results in that delegate missing the Procession. (See individual delegates above: Eely, Goodrich, and Ob.) There are two ways the party can approach this task:

{@b {@i Deceive, Intimidate, and Persuade.}} Through the use roleplaying or a successful {@dc 12} Charisma ({@skill Deception}, {@skill Intimidation} or {@skill Persuasion}) check, emphasize the social aspect of the task. If the PCs fail to talk their way to a solution, allow them to complete a delegate's request instead.

{@b {@i Complete a Delegate's Request.}} If the PCs complete the request, the delegate joins the Procession in time. Keep in mind that the party has only an hour to bring as many delegates to the Procession as possible.

entries.name: Guard the Procession
entries: The procession consists of the PCs, any delegates they convinced to come, and two Large swarms of fey creatures. The delegates and swarms are automatically hit if targeted by an attack. If any delegate or swarm receives damage during the procession, they flee immediately. At least one delegate or fey swarm must reach the doors of the patron towers for the procession to succeed.
Combat does not happen immediately, but follow these steps when it does to keep Procession orderly:

items: {@b {@i Initiative.}} The party rolls initiative.
{@b {@i The Fey Gather.}} The PCs, any delegates they calmed, and the two Large swarms of fey creatures gather at the bottom of the path as they wish.
{@b {@i Procession Begins.}} At the beginning of each round, the delegates and the fey swarms move 40 feet along the stone path. It should take them 4 or 5 rounds to reach the door.

{@b {@i Magmin Assault.}} At the beginning of the 2nd round, eight {@creature magmin||magmin} appear at the edge of the clearing, entering the initiative on count 10. The magmin are here to stop the Procession from succeeding and attack the PCs and the fey folk! Remember that if any delegate or fey swarm is damaged by a magmin (either directly or indirectly when it dies), they flee. In general, the magmin should target the PCs. They might attack the fey to add tension if required.
{@b {@i Procession Ends.}} The Procession ends once the magmin are defeated as long as at least one delegate or fey swarm reaches the door.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: If the Procession succeeds, the patron of Drywood Hall emerges from the tower and, with a tremendous roar, summons rain clouds that last for seven days. Wildfires in the area are extinguished. The patron retreats back into the tower for more rest as the fey folk begin their celebration in earnest. The party receives their payment, gains Inspiration, and has an opportunity to party with the Drywood Hall fey for several days.

If the Procession fails, the Drywood is imperiled by the growing fires. Drywood Hall falls under a heavy curtain of despair and misery, and the fey inhabitants of the forest squabble and begin plotting their escape. Further adventure may save the forest, but for now, Drywood Hall is demoralized.

rows: {@b An adventure for four to six characters of 4th or 5th level}

entries: Surrender won't stop an arrow already loosed.

entries.name: Background
entries: The earth churns in a city graveyard, revealing not undead but an ancient war machine. A great iron transport bores its way from depths below, disrupting funeral rites and sending the citizens into a panic. With an opportunity to investigate and reap the rewards of bravery, the party closes on the graveyard. There they discover that the pilots of the strange vehicle are soulless automatons who have spent an eternity burrowing toward the battlefront of a long-forgotten war.
In this action-packed and gritty adventure, the PCs must battle automatons, breach the iron transport, and put down its mad and malfunctioning commander.

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: The following NPC will be present for this adventure:

items: {@b {@i Yansha, Captain of the Guard.}} The PCs are either sought out by the captain or can encounter her in the streets. She tells a harrowing tale, involving heavily armored soldiers attacking citizen and guard alike near the graveyard. She describes a great war machine, bursting from the ground in the graveyard: {@i "I've never seen such cold and calculated violence. They don't make mistakes. I didn't see one swing of their hammers that didn't find a home . . . it was a slaughter."}

entries: A war machine has dug its way out of the graveyard of the town. Its passengers are soldiers in a war that ended a very long time ago. While most of the burrowing machines reached their destination and met their fate, this one strayed off course. Its pilot-commander was possessed by an evil spirit when the digger passed too close to the spirit's lair. The possessed commander has steered the transport in an erratic course over many years, finally surfacing in the graveyard. The soldiers are acting according to their protocols: they are at war and, after some delay, have arrived at the battle. The commander lurks in the bowels of the war machine, plotting their next move.

Unchecked, the soldiers and their leader begin attacking the citizens around the graveyard. Killing as many people and causing as much destruction as possible. Built for war and nothing else, the automatons play out their roles as soldiers in a war, regardless of their circumstances.

entries.name: In Your Campaign
entries: This adventure requires a town (or city) to be threatened by the emergence of the war machine. A guard captain prompts the PCs to action in response to the surprising appearance of the war machine, offering a way for the party to earn some renown with the locals. This is a combat-heavy scenario with mindless soldiers pitted against the party. The automatons inside the transport have likely already caused a great deal of violence in the area.
The {@creature fellforged|ToB|fellforged} can be replaced with a {@creature wraith}.

entries.name: In Midgard
entries: Long ago, the city of Valera created a dozen burrowing war machines to bolster its already formidable army. These diggers were crewed by clockwork soldiers and sent on various training missions, but several of the diggers were lost, presumed crushed under tons of earth and rock. Not all were destroyed though, and one has managed to dig itself all the way to the Free City of Siwal! There they play out their training with deadly consequences.

entries.name: War Machine

entries: This massive iron and steel machine is divided into two discrete sections. The forward 30 feet are dedicated to a rotating drill whose teeth are noticeably worn. The back portion consists of a 50-foot tube with three large treads spread equidistant around the tube. Two outlines that suggest doors are set into the body of the machine. The very back of the vehicle is a smoldering engine . . . what magic fuels this impressive wonder of metal?

The {@vehicle Burrowing War Machine|KPPreparedExpanded|machine} consists of a 30-foot-long mechanical drill made of magically durable steel mounted to the front of a 50-foot-long crew-and-passenger section.

A great magical engine comprises the back 10 feet, which sheds bright light for 25 feet around the machine and dim light for another 50 feet. The machine has an AC of 18 and 175 hit points. Its metal exterior grants it a damage threshold of 15. It resists all nonmagical damage and is immune to force damage. It has no actions and cannot move.

entries.name: Perfect Soldiers
entries: The {@vehicle Burrowing War Machine|KPPreparedExpanded|burrowing war machine} transports 18 soldiers ({@creature animated armor||animated armors}) and one commander ({@creature fellforged|ToB|fellforged}): 12 of the soldiers are performing maneuvers in the graveyard while the others guard the vehicle and the commander. The soldiers appear as black-iron-clad humanoids that march in unison and use every advantage the battlefield offers. The soldiers come in four varieties.

entries.name: Gunner
entries: In addition to their regular actions and traits, the gunner soldiers gain the following action:
{@b {@i Hand Crossbow.}} Ranged Weapon Attack: {@hit 5} to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 6 ({@damage 1d6 + 3}) piercing damage.
And their Multiattack action is modified:
{@b {@i Multiattack.}} The animated armor makes two Hand Crossbow attacks.
The gunner soldiers use the statistics of an {@creature Animated Armor Gunner|KPPreparedExpanded|animated armor gunner}.

entries.name: Hammerer
entries: In addition to their regular actions and traits, the hammerer soldier's Slam attack is replaced with the following:
{@b {@i Warhammer.}} Melee Weapon Attack: {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 ({@damage 1d8 + 2}) bludgeoning damage.
And their Multiattack action is modified:
{@b {@i Multiattack.}} The animated armor makes three Warhammer attacks.
The hammerer soldiers use the statistics of an {@creature Animated Armor Hammerer|KPPreparedExpanded|animated armor hammerer}.

entries.name: Scout
entries: In addition to their regular actions and traits, the scout soldiers gain +7 to Stealth, and their base move speed is 40 feet. They also gain the following trait:
{@b {@i Cloaked (3/Day).}} The scout has advantage on its next Stealth check.
The scout soldiers use the statistics of an {@creature Animated Armor Scout|KPPreparedExpanded|animated armor scout}.

entries.name: Shield Bearer
entries: In addition to their regular actions and traits, the shield bearer soldiers have +2 to AC, owing to the massive, grimy metal shields they carry. These shield-bearing soldiers are resistant to non-magical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.
The shield bearer soldiers use the statistics of an {@creature Animated Armor Shield Bearer|KPPreparedExpanded|animated armor shield bearer}.

entries.name: Graveyard
entries: The party encounters the soldiers before reaching the graveyard. There are two units of six soldiers each, out wreaking havoc in the streets. A unit typically consists of two shield bearers, two hammerers, one scout, and one gunner. (A unit's composition may differ based on the needs of the GM, but the increased challenge of adding foes to an encounter should be minded.) The modifications to the animated armors (see {@area Perfect Soldiers|12.2|x} above) increase the challenge rating offered by these foes normally, and a full unit should provide a medium to hard encounter (CR 7) for the party. Here are two possible encounters involving the soldiers:

items: {@b {@i Breaking In.}} A unit of soldiers is attempting to force their way into a home where a dozen innocents have taken refuge. Uncontested, the soldiers break into the home within 2 rounds. A fight in the street awaits the party as they intervene, using the environment to their advantage as much as possible.

{@b {@i Fortified Position.}} A unit of soldiers has taken over a two-story building. The gunner fires at anything in the street from the second floor and has threequarters cover. The building's two entrances are barred (AC 15, 30 hp) and guarded by a shield bearer and one or two hammerers.

entries.name: Assault on the War Machine

entries: The machine sits in the center of the graveyard. Two soldiers with heavy shields patrol. A few crypts offer hiding places on the way to the machine, but the area immediately around it is clear.

{@b {@i Explosive Traps.}} Large explosive traps have been sunk into the grounds of the graveyard and are triggered by creatures moving over them. Spotting the traps requires a successful {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check, and dismantling one requires a successful {@dc 14} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) check. There are at least 10 such devices, forming a perimeter around the war machine. Creatures within a 10-foot radius of a device when it explodes must make a {@dc 14} Dexterity saving throw, taking 14 ({@damage 4d6}) fire damage on a failed save or half the damage on a successful one.

A unit of soldiers (see {@area Perfect Soldiers|12.2|x} above) protect the vehicle and the commander inside it ({@b B}). They will rush to engage enemies, avoiding their own traps. A scout soldier patrols the perimeter of the graveyard in stealth. It waits for the right moment to strike, preferring to attack once the party has confidently engaged the rest of its unit.
Battling past the soldiers, the PCs may carefully enter the vehicle:

This dark and cramped metal hall smells of oil and earth. A grating sound rises. There, at the threshold between the forward cockpit and the main chamber, a hulking metal monster. Its head is bathed in crimson light.

The commander ({@creature fellforged|ToB|fellforged}) starts combat at the doorway ({@b A}). It seals the doors to the war machine on the 1st round before hissing and charging any party members inside. It is happy to fight in close quarters. The door can be opened by a PC who reaches the cockpit (see {@area War Machine|12.1|x} above for rules on forcing the door open). The wraith inside the fellforged armor has no intentions beyond murdering its enemies and cannot be reasoned with or convinced to surrender.
A successful {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check made while examining the cockpit reveals the decades long course the war machine took.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The soldiers carry no valuables, and the war machine contains only the essentials for keeping the crew running. Two {@i {@item Elemental Gem, Red Corundum||elemental gems (red corundum)}} serve as part of the power source for the machine. They may be removed from their housing in the cockpit and used as normal.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: The story may continue in a number of ways. What was the outcome of the war these soldiers were supposed to be a part of? Local powers may wish the source of the war machine investigated, starting a longer adventure that reveals the origin of the automatons. And how many more such machines strayed off course?

rows: {@b An adventure for four to six characters of 4th or 5th level}

entries: Evil can be hidden away for a time, but it always finds a way.

entries.name: Background
entries: Once, the forest was protected by a powerful druid, Diarmuid. For centuries, Diarmuid tended the forest and kept its greatest secret safe from outsiders. At the heart of this forest was a gate thought to be left behind by celestials in an era not even the tallest trees could recall. The druid called the artifact Atym, an old elvish word meaning "abandoned."

What Diarmuid did not know was that Atym was neither abandoned nor disabled. The druid discovered the gate was an infernal deception. Its celestial runes and design were meant to hide its true nature: a secret door to hell. Upon learning this, the druid sacrificed himself to surround the artifact in impenetrable vines. For an age, the gate was sealed away and hidden until an incursion of undead resulted in a battle near the Atym Gate. A community of centaurs won that battle and discovered the cracked carapace of vines and the gate within.

With the gate revealed, the undead have redoubled their efforts to control the forest. The centaurs, desperate to repel the monsters, seek to summon celestial allies through the artifact. The centaurs are busy fighting undead, so their leader, Charia-Kas, hires the party to escort her to the Atym Gate and help her to activate it.
Here are a just a few suggestions to bring the PCs into the adventure:

items: While passing through the forest, the party discovers centaurs engaged in combat with undead warriors. The adventurers learn of the centaurs' need for help defending their home and are invited to meet with Charia-Kas.

The party is hired by a group of scholars to investigate the forest and find the rumored celestial artifact. Once there, the party becomes embroiled in the local conflict between centaur and undead, ultimately meeting with Charia-Kas.

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: The following NPC will be present for this adventure:

items: {@b {@i Charia-Kas.}} The young leader of the centaur community is dressed in finely made studded leather armor. She carries a spear made of owlbear bone and hardwood. Her hair is cropped almost to the scalp, and her dark eyes are watchful and piercing. Charia-Kas loves her home and is distraught by the presence of the undead. She paints her flanks to count the number of undead warriors she has slain.

entries.name: Order of the Cold Hearth
entries: The undead warriors comprising the Order of the Cold Hearth have been commanded by their leader, Dorromar, to secure the Atym Gate. The undead are frequently encountered in the forest and surrounding areas. Their banner, a stone hearth wreathed in shadowy flame, is carried by a fearsome warrior known as Charn.
Roll a {@dice d4} and consult the {@b Order of the Cold Hearth Encounters} table to challenge the PCs, or choose something appropriate.

entries.caption: Order of the Cold Hearth Encounters
rows: Three {@creature ghoul||ghouls} haul a freshly killed elk back to camp.
Two scouts ({@creature wight||wights}), hidden in the treetops, watch for signs of the centaurs.
Three {@creature ghast||ghasts} chase an injured wolf.
Charn ({@creature gladiator}) and two soldiers ({@creature guard||guards}) scour the area for centaur tracks.

entries.name: Meet with Charia-Kas
entries: At the centaur village of Greentide, the PCs are presented to the leader, Charia-Kas ({@creature centaur}, 72 hit points). In her hall made of magically bent wood, hide, and thatch, she asks the party to help her activate the Atym Gate. As a reward, she offers the party an amber-encased treant sapling (killed and preserved thousands of years ago) worth 2,000 gp. She reveals the following:

items: An ancient artifact has been revealed at the heart of the forest: a gateway to the celestial planes.
The undead of the Order of the Cold Hearth are arriving in ever-greater numbers. Controlling the gate is imperative for the survival of Greentide.
The artifact is still protected by druidic wards.

entries: The party must escort Charia-Kas to the gate and assist her in activating it, summoning celestial allies to help Greentide repel the undead.

entries.name: Travel to the Atym Gate
entries: The path from Greentide to the Atym Gate winds through the forest for 3 miles. Use the following complications as appropriate or feel free to move the action to the {@area Defend Charia-Kas|13.6|x} section below. Note that Charia-Kas must survive the trip. Have her retreat from combat if she is gravely injured:

items: {@b {@i Mob of Shrubs.}} A thicket of {@creature awakened shrub||awakened shrubs} flees the undead. The shrubs are not hostile or interested in fighting. The six shrubs in charge communicate the loss of their "root place" several days ago. A successful {@dc 10} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check reveals valuable information about the undead, providing the party with Inspiration.

{@b {@i Undead Incursions.}} Use the {@area Order of the Cold Hearth Encounters|13.1|x} table to reinforce their presence in the forest. Resolve the encounters with simple narrative combat or a generic forest battle map.

entries.name: Defend Charia-Kas

entries: Approaching the cracked dome of vines, you see within a great artifact consisting of a central device and three connected gateways. In the dappled light, the Atym Gate shimmers and glints.

Entering the area triggers the encounter with the druid's guardians. Three {@creature vine golem|ToB2|vine golems} attempt to surprise the party as they approach: {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check to notice the creatures. The golems appear within 5 feet of each gateway. For parties with more than four PCs, add an additional golem for every two over. For example, a party of six PCs would encounter four golems. For a 4th-level party, reduce each golem's hit points to 33 ({@creature Vine Golem (Weakened)|KPPreparedExpanded|vine golem}).
Charia-Kas remains outside the dome until the guardians are defeated, at which point she races to the central console.

entries.name: Power Up the Gate
entries: The central console must be activated for the Atym Gate to function. The infernal designers of this artifact went to great lengths to hide its true purpose, delighting in the magical trap at the core of the design.

The console radiates strong conjuration magic. Its infernal nature is undetectable through any means. A successful {@dc 13} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check determines the gate has likely never been used.

Only Charia-Kas has the knowledge to operate the runes on the central console. She stands at the center, ready to touch the runes in a sequence she learned when the gate was first discovered. When the PCs are ready, they may signal the centaur to start. Charia-Kas does not fight while performing the sequence and takes no actions to defend herself or move from the central console. The following events are triggered when Charia-Kas begins the sequence:

items: The gates crackle to life. Bright crimson light fills the portals. The air is suffused with the scent of sulfur. The centaur looks at you with sudden panic in her eyes. "What is happening?" she cries.

From each of the three portals, a {@creature Blood Imp Swarm|KPPreparedExpanded|blood imp swarm} emerges and attacks the nearest creature it can see. For 5th-level PCs, increase each swarm's hit points to 48. The swarms attack Charia-Kas if no other targets are within reach.

entries: Once the swarms are defeated, the Atym Gate's final trap is triggered, surrounding Charia-Kas in magical infernal fire. The flames consume the centaur within a round, after which they dissipate, revealing Charia-Kas in her infernal transformation.

entries.name: Defeat Charia-Kas
entries: Flame turns to smoke, from which Charia-Kas emerges—wholly transformed. Her equine body has taken a more canine form. Bright red flaming runes run over her flesh. Her eyes regard you cruelly. "The gate is so much more than I thought," she says with a crackle of fire in her voice.

Charia-Kas ({@creature Charia-Kas (Infernal)|KPPreparedExpanded|infernal centaur}, 88 hit points) attacks the party. On initiative count 20 (losing all ties), Charia-Kas activates two of the following effects (or for 4th-level PCs, activate only one effect):

items: {@b {@i Brimstone Barrier.}} A partially solid barrier of sulfur surrounds Charia-Kas, granting her half cover. This effect ends on initiative count 20 of the following round.
{@b {@i Flaming Roots.}} Fiery roots erupt under one randomly targeted PC. The roots attempt to grapple the PC (escape {@dc 12}). The roots disappear on initiative count 20 of the following round.

{@b {@i Minor Fireball.}} A minor fireball appears and explodes on one randomly targeted PC. That PC, and any creature within 5 feet of them, must make a {@dc 12} Dexterity saving throw, taking 9 ({@damage 2d6 + 2}) fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries: To reduce the difficulty of the encounter, or to add variety, use the following:
{@b {@i Diarmuid's Restoration.}} Creatures who end their turn in one of the blue pools magically regenerate 3 hit points (including creatures reduced to 0 hit points).

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: After Charia-Kas is defeated, the party discovers she inadvertently opened portals to the infernal planes. With the Order of the Cold Hearth pressing to control the place, the PCs may feel compelled to deactivate the portals . . . somehow. Returning to Greentide, the party must inform the centaurs that their leader has fallen. They receive their promised reward, but the centaurs' morale is low.

rows: {@b An adventure for four to six characters of 4th or 5th level}

entries: The first spell cast has not yet finished its work.

entries.name: Background
entries: Strange lights in the desert lead the PCs to a longforgotten oasis. Traveling toward the lights, the PCs are threatened by magic so old that it defies categorization. Arriving at the withered shore of a blood-colored pool, the PCs discover an ancient dial and three tooth-like columns, rising from the ground. Turning the dial results in the water being magically siphoned into the cavities within the columns. If the pool is emptied, a small door is revealed in the crimson-stained muck. The party must defeat a blood-infused water elemental before proceeding.

Once inside, the PCs share a room with an ongoing dark ritual, running since the origin of the world. The keeper of the place, an immortal fey within a powerful suit of armor, offers little explanation as to the nature of the ritual, and he seeks to ensure they tell no one of the Claret Wellspring.

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: Approaching the Claret Wellspring activates the powerful magical defenses left behind by its creator. Spellcasters whose primary statistic is Intelligence feel subtle force waves starting at one mile. A successful {@dc 14} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check reveals the magic is old and primal in nature, and PCs with a scholarly background gain advantage on this check. If the check surpasses the DC by 3 or more, the PC learns something profound about the nature of magic in the world, and they have advantage on all Intelligence checks for 24 hours.

{@b {@i Shockwave.}} When the PCs are within half a mile of the oasis, the defenses trigger. A massive wave of force explodes out from the wellspring. PCs must first succeed on a {@dc 12} Strength saving throw or be thrown backward 20 feet, taking 7 ({@damage 2d6}) bludgeoning damage as they tumble across the sand. A successful {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw prevents the PC from being {@condition deafened} for an hour by this effect. Finally, all PCs envision the first time they encountered magic and feel compelled to share it. Refusing to share their experience causes 2 ({@damage 1d4}) psychic damage.

entries.name: Ritual of Endings

entries: Before you, a dark sphere revolves in a sea of stars, passing through hues from crimson to royal blue in an unending pattern. A single musical chord plays eternally, its notes tear at the tethers that bind your mind to reality.

The ritual of endings is one of several rituals that maintain the magic of the first spell. None know the ultimate aim of the original spell, but its secrets may yet be revealed by brave adventurers and scholars. The actions required to stop the ritual, and the effects of such tampering, are entirely for the GM to decide. A successful {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check allows a spellcaster whose primary attribute is Intelligence to learn a minor version the ritual. It may be cast weekly, requires 500 gp worth of materials (GM discretion), and increases the caster's spell saving throw DC by +1 for the week.

entries.name: Armor of the Keeper

entries: Interlocking plates of black metal refuse even the slightest reflection. From its heart, suspended in a sphere of flashing magical light, a tiny fey-like creature stares at you enigmatically.

Mechanically, the armor is a {@creature minotaur}. It behaves as an additional opponent, albeit under the control of the wearer. While inside the armor, the wearer gains advantage to saving throws against spells. The armor does not interfere with the wearer's actions or abilities. Treat the armor and wearer as two separate targets when resolving spells and effects. The wearer may be targeted normally but is immune to attacks and effects that would force it out of the armor. If the armor reaches 0 hit points, it "dies," and the wearer is ejected.

entries.name: Area 1: Beside the Oasis

entries: A blood-colored pool surrounded by withering vegetation sits at the feet of three towering stone columns. The jagged columns rise like teeth from a maw buried under the sand. A stone dial sits upon a small pedestal on the far side of the water, its face marked with four distinct lines.

The dial has four positions. Turning the dial requires a successful {@dc 10} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check. Turning the dial clockwise from its starting position begins the transfer of water from the pool to the hollow columns. When the dial reaches its final position, the pool is emptied, revealing the small door to {@area 2|14.4|u}.

{@b {@i Emptying the Pool.}} On the round after the pool empties, the water in the columns sprays up into the air and forms a {@creature Blood-Infused Water Elemental|KPPreparedExpanded|water elemental} that attacks the PCs. Damaging the elemental causes the creature's "blood" to fall to the sand adjacent to it. The blood forms characters in Draconic. Upon its death, PCs who read Draconic can study the script with a successful {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check to reveal the following message: {@i "Before words were divine ambitions."}

In addition, the flora beside the pool animates and threatens to entangle the party. On initiative count 20, the fibrous plants lash out at the feet of one PC within 50 feet of the empty pool's edge. A successful {@dc 12} Dexterity saving throw avoids being pulled {@condition prone}. When the elemental is defeated, the plants cease their attacks.

entries.name: Area 2: Soundless Vault

entries: This cramped triangular chamber is supported by two dark stone columns at its center. Sound is strangely muted here, voices carrying only a few feet before disappearing into the darkness. The stale air suggests the vault has been closed up a long time.

The ritual in {@area 3|14.5|u} is responsible for the auditory effects. Spoken messages do not travel more than 5 feet before being silenced. Spells and effects requiring targets to hear instead fizzle and fail if the target is more than 5 feet away.

{@b {@i Eternal Guardian.}} The small chamber is occupied by the ritual's eternal guardian, a {@creature mamura|ToB|mamura} inside the {@area armor of the keeper|14.2|x} (see above). The armor and the mamura take their actions on the mamura's initiative. In combat, the mamura fights with its Claw and Whiptail Stinger attacks from the safety of the armor while the armor uses its Gore liberally, charging when able. Each round on initiative count 5, the columns (AC 10, hp 15) each make one attack (ranged 20/40, {@hit 6} to hit, 3 ({@damage 1d6}) fire damage). Destroying both columns triggers a minor cave-in, causing 4 ({@damage 1d6 + 1}) bludgeoning damage or half as much damage on a successful {@dc 10} Dexterity saving throw. The key to {@area 3|14.5|u} is located in the armor, and it is discovered by anyone searching the remains. The script above the door to {@area 3|14.5|u} is written in Draconic and reads as follows: "Here rises the end."

entries.name: Area 3: Ritual Alcove

entries: The door opens to a small alcove. Ringing the alcove at shoulder height are three locked compartments. A dim light emanates from the deepest point of the alcove, and a musical chord plays faintly, growing in volume as you approach the light.

The door to this area is sealed by a complex lock. Forcing the lock without proper study requires a successful {@dc 21} Dexterity (thieves' tools) check. If the PCs first succeed on a {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check, the DC to force the lock is reduced to 10. Behind the door is a small alcove, containing an unending ritual begun when magic originated (see {@area Ritual of Endings|14.1|x} above). The three compartments are locked and can be opened with thieves' tools and a successful {@dc 14} Dexterity check. They can also be opened with a crowbar and a successful {@dc 15} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: There are 500 gp worth of spell components in the compartments of {@area 3|14.5|u}. A skilled blacksmith can reinforce existing plate mail with some of the pieces of the {@i armor of the keeper}. Plate mail strengthened with the armor gains 20 pounds of weight and provides the wearer with resistance to piercing damage.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: The first magic is kept active by several rituals similar to the one under the Claret Wellspring. To know the nature of the magic, the PCs must search for the locations. What is the ultimate effect of the first spell cast? Who was the caster, and how are the destinies of the PCs connected with the spell's resolution?

rows: {@b An adventure for four to six characters of 5th or 6th level}

entries: . . . for a cold-blooded killer.

entries.name: Background
entries: Bodies are turning up in a city (or large town). The organs of the victims appear to have been turned to solid crystal. In a gruesome twist, the hearts of the victims have been carefully removed. The mayor and the guard captain have hit an impasse in their investigation. Agreeing to assist in finding the murderer, the PCs find themselves under attack by infernal assassins as they follow the clues to a gemcutter's workshop.
In this rich and devilish adventure, the PCs must find and face a murderer and a charming devil.

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: A gnome gemcutter has made a bargain with a {@creature gilded devil|ToB|gilded devil}. The devil has granted the young woman unsurpassed skill in her craft, and in exchange, she has agreed to provide him crystallized mortal hearts. She and the devil are hiding in the gemcutting workshop of her former master, who was her first victim. The bargain made between the two is as follows:

items: The devil increases Jelfi's skill at gemcutting to surpass both rivals and mentors.
Jelfi must sacrifice (murder) one resident of the city each week.
She must perform an unholy ritual that crystallizes parts of her victim's body.
Jelfi must remove the crystallized heart of her victims and cut it into a beautiful stone.
The stone is given to the gilded devil, who now lairs in the basement of the workshop consuming the gems and jewelry.

entries: {@b {@i Mystery Presented.}} The PCs hear of the murders while staying in or traveling through the city. Inquiries made to inn keepers, guards, and general citizenry lead the party to a conversation with Mayor Enkam, who can be found in her official office most days.

The mayor ({@creature noble}) is a tall woman dressed in rich clothing. Mayor Enkam is straightforward and maintains eye contact during conversation, and she is never without her two personal guards ({@creature veteran||veterans}). She has only the best interests of the citizens at heart. The mayor's investigators have come up empty handed, and she is open to the PCs' assistance. She offers 1,000 gp if the party can solve the murders. She provides the following information:

items: The victims come from a wide range of backgrounds.
They have been stabbed to death.
Their internal organs, eyes, and bones are transformed into pure crystal.
The hearts of victims are missing.
The high alchemist has not been helpful in the investigation so far but may have useful information.
The bodies of the six victims are available for examination.
The guard captain has reached a dead end and is not sure what to do next. He is available for consulting.

entries: The following provides guidance for handling the PCs' investigation into the murders. It is likely that the party will solve the mystery and confront Jelfi at Kendrin's Fine Works on the second day, after speaking with the high alchemist and Argus. They may decide to investigate the gemcutting shops on the first day if they are clever. Improvise based on the party's actions, using the following topics and scenarios as required.

{@b {@i You Know Too Much!}} At some point in their investigation, likely on the evening of the first day or when they are close to investigating Kendrin's shop, the party is attacked by three (CR 8) or four (CR 9) assassins ({@creature bearded devil||bearded devils}). The assassins strike wherever the party attempts to rest. They may also lure them into an alley or uninhabited building by emulating cries of distress. The assassins are sent by Jelfi's patron, but they know nothing of the murders or bargain and are simply following instructions.

entries.name: In Your Campaign
entries: This adventure requires a city or large town capable of supporting competing gemcutting shops. It mentions a high alchemist and a gemcutting guild. It will likely take two days for the party to find their way to the murderer. It is assumed the party is staying in the city for a short while.
The {@creature crystalline devil|ToB|crystalline devil} and {@creature gilded devil|ToB|gilded devil} can be replaced by an {@creature earth elemental} and an {@creature oni}, respectively.

entries.name: In Midgard
entries: The Merchant District of Zobeck contains both of the gemcutting shops featured in this adventure. Jelfi's dead employer was an associate of House Greymark, and the party will have a run-in with a representative from the rich family during their investigation. Mayor Karillian Gluck is anxious to see the murders stopped as stories of a serial killer with grim magical predilections does nothing to help trade. Some of the citizens may well believe the Winter Court is to blame for the murders and fan the flames of tension between the fey and the mortal citizens of Zobeck.

entries.name: Day One
entries: {@b {@i Speaking with the Guard Captain.}} Mekno is a sturdy human with shockingly orange hair and beard. He is openly frustrated by his inability to solve these ritualistic murders. Strange chalk markings were found near the murder sites. He suggests the party visit one of the sites to see for themselves.

{@b {@i Examining the Bodies.}} A successful {@dc 5} Wisdom ({@skill Medicine}) check confirms the victim died from stab wounds. A successful {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check reveals that the heart was removed carefully, but the stab wounds are very rough and amateurish. A successful {@dc 13} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check concludes that the stab wounds were inflicted by someone small in stature and that someone with nimble hands must have removed the heart.

{@b {@i Examining the Murder Sites.}} The party finds a chalk symbol scrawled onto a nearby wall. A successful {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) or Wisdom ({@skill Religion}) check reveals it is infernal in nature, but casting {@spell comprehend languages} does not decode the symbol, though it does reveal its connection to the Infernal alphabet. PCs with a suitable background or who read Infernal automatically identify it and its meaning: {@i "Cage the soul."}

entries.name: Day Two
entries: {@b {@i Speaking with the High Alchemist.}} The high alchemist is unavailable for a meeting on the first day of the party's investigation. He agrees to meet with them in the morning on the second day. Tembor the Green lives and works in his laboratory and is attended by several servants and apprentices. He is an old human with an arrogant streak and is no friend of the mayor. The mayor slighted him by importing curative draughts once instead of ordering from him. He agrees to speak with the party but will not give his assessment of the murders freely. A successful {@dc 16} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check changes his mind, or alternatively, the party might explain the slight to the mayor who agrees to apologize to Tembor to further the investigation. Once properly convinced, Tembor informs the party that kyanite is known for its purity—energy stored within the crystal would be pristinely preserved. Kyanite is not overly common. He also suggests speaking with Argus at the Gemcutters' Guild Hall.

{@b {@i Visiting the Gemcutters' Guild Hall.}} Argus is the second-highest-ranking member of the guild and a slender elf with strikingly good looks. He knows nothing specific about the murders. He agrees kyanite is prized for its purity but also reveals the crystal is difficult to cut and would chip or shatter in all but the most skilled hands. He suggests visiting the city's jewelry and gemcutting workshops: the Emerald Dove and Kendrin's Fine Works.

{@b {@i Visiting the Emerald Dove.}} Anni is a pleasant half-elf who owns and runs a jewelry shop in a nice part of the city. She is troubled to hear about the murders. She admits she has never worked with kyanite. Her relationship with Kendrin has soured since he accepted the unpopular Jelfi as an assistant. Jelfi worked for Anni for a few months but had more talk than skill. She can't be sure, but she thinks the gnome even stole an old lapidary guide before her last day at work.
