{@b {@i Visiting Kendrin's Fine Works.}} The door is locked, and there is no response to knocking. The door can be forced open without a skill roll. Proceed to {@area Kendrin's Fine Works|15.5|x} once the PCs enter Kendrin's shop.

entries.name: Kendrin's Fine Works

entries: The storefront of this workshop is dark. A few ornate displays sit empty near the back of the chamber. A single door leads to the back of the building.

The store has been emptied of valuables, for the devil in the basement has eaten most of them. The place smells of decaying flesh. Old bloodstains mark the floor near the front. The blood belongs to Kendrin, Jelfi's first victim. His body was not recovered, and the apprentice hid it in the basement. A stairway in the backroom leads to the basement lair of the gilded devil. The heavy steel door into the lower workshop is open.
{@b {@i Murderer Revealed.}} Jelfi ({@creature spy}) is hiding (Stealth 17) behind the displays. When the PCs have entered the store and it's clear she will be discovered, she confronts them:
"No, no, no! I was promised unsurpassed skills! I will not be taken!"

The PCs have a moment or two to interact with Jelfi before she attacks them. She's happy to sell out the gilded devil lairing in the basement if she's allowed to go free. A successful {@dc 20} Charisma ({@skill Intimidation} or {@skill Persuasion}) check might diffuse the conflict, but otherwise, faced with imprisonment or worse, Jelfi attacks. She has been given a guardian by the gilded devil: Jelfi carries a large emerald that is in fact a {@creature crystalline devil|ToB|crystalline devil} in its gemstone form. The two attack the party. Jelfi does have Anni's stolen lapidary guide, which can be returned for a reward.

{@b {@i Devil in the Basement.}} Dwelling amongst the sacks of raw stones in the gemcutter's workshop is a {@creature gilded devil|ToB|gilded devil}. It has eaten most of the valuable items, but the six kyanite hearts of Jelfi's victims sit prominently on a small table. The devil, having heard the fight upstairs, has taken a relaxed position on the main worktable. It welcomes the party to its abode and apologizes for the smell. It explains the bargain made with Jelfi and expresses disappointment in her. The devil flatly offers the PCs the remaining 5,000 gp worth of finished precious stones to walk away and let it escape, promising to leave, and a successful {@dc 5} Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check reveals it is telling the truth. Otherwise, the devil gladly attacks the party. It may use an action to consume one of the six kyanite hearts. Doing so restores 25 hp and gives the devil advantage on its next attack.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Jelfi has Anni's lapidary guide stashed on the main floor of Kendrin's shop. The book is worth around 500 gp. Anni will pay half as much for its return. The party must decide what to do with the unfinished gems (worth 5,000 gp) in Kendrin's basement workshop. The mayor is pleased to pay the party the promised fee.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: The uncut gems that the gilded devil did not eat are in the hands of the PCs. Selling them in the city would incriminate them, and smuggling that many gems might prove difficult. There may be infernal allies of the slain devil living in the city who take offense at the party's actions.

data.name: Neither by Sail, Nor by Oar

rows: {@b An adventure for four to six characters of 5th or 6th level}

entries: It sailed up through the fog, a black ship that left no wake. It's come for the statue. It's come for us all.

entries.name: Background
entries: The PCs arrange for passage on a fast ship called the {@i Silver Slipper}. The good Captain Sara agrees to take them aboard for a reasonable fee. The voyage, however, is marred by strange events, and the crew begin whispering about a dark statue taken aboard as cargo. The statue is to be delivered to a port beyond the PCs' destination. When a fog rolls in one night, the ship is attacked by evil agents of a dark god come to claim the statue.
In this nautical nightmare, the PCs must travel aboard the ship, interact with the crew, and save themselves from a boarding party of eldritch evil.

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: The voyage may be of any length. Ideally, the party engages in some downtime activity as they travel aboard the Silver Slipper. The following events can be used to pass the time and reinforce the dark influence of the statue upon the crew.

entries.name: Strange Cargo

entries: A crude humanoid figure squats atop a roughly carved pedestal. The figure and its base are made from one piece of dark-gray stone. The face is brutish and scowling. Its ears rise to a point, and its teeth are jagged and broken.

Evil agents of a dark god have arranged for a cursed statue to be transported aboard the {@i Silver Slipper}. The statue is not intended to make it to its destination but rather be picked up by an intercepting ship filled with cultists. The statue is of great value to the cultists. It radiates both evil and magic and weighs about a 150 pounds. The PCs are assumed to be immune to the statue's more nefarious effects—the product of being seasoned adventurers. The crew, however, are not spared from its influence.

entries.name: Captain Sara

entries: Welcome aboard. Mind your step. The wind blows hard in our favor today, friends!
{@b {@i What She Wants Most.}} To retire in her hometown, rich and renowned.

{@b {@i Physical Traits.}} Captain Sara is a middle-aged woman with long grey and black hair tied back from her face. She carries herself about the ship on a sturdy frame and dresses in practical and well-made clothes. She dons an impressive captain's hat with fancy embroidery when the sun is hot.

{@b {@i Personality/Roleplaying.}} Captain Sara would have made a good adventurer. She is brave, cunning, and a natural leader. A look from her silences most complaints from her crew. She is loud, boisterous, and friendly. Her success at sea is owed to her professionalism, and she does not suffer fools aboard her ship, the {@i Silver Slipper}.
The PCs may engage the captain in conversation during the voyage. She is reasonably friendly and willing to trade stories. Asked directly about the statue, she reveals the following:

items: She's been paid to take it to a port beyond where the party is destined.
She was paid twice what she demanded.
She agrees the statue is ugly but is convinced it is harmless.

entries.name: In Your Campaign
entries: This adventure requires that the party travel by boat. It is intended to add some excitement to what would normally be uneventful downtime. A statue carved in the image of some dark god is mentioned, and the enemies have distinctly cult-like qualities.
The {@b {@creature fext|ToB|fext}} and {@b {@creature noctiny|ToB|noctiny}} can be replaced with a {@b {@creature mage}} and {@b {@creature berserker||berserkers}}, respectively.

entries.name: In Midgard
entries: Along the northern coast of the Southlands, perhaps near Nuria Natal, the PCs sail from port to port. The captain of the {@i Silver Slipper} has been paid a fortune by worshippers of an evil aspect of the god Anu-Akma. These cultists look to build a temple dedicated to their dark patron, who manifests as a large humanoid made from coal-like, stony shards. The statue serves as a centerpiece to their ritual chamber, but transporting it by land was too risky. Now, the PCs are caught in the worshipper's plot as the ship they hire meets its fate.

entries.name: Drinks with the Crew
entries: The crew of the Silver Slipper often pass the time by playing various drinking games. The games are simple as rum does not favor complication. The PCs might join the crew one night for such revelry.

{@b {@i Pearl in the Deep.}} This simple game requires two players. One is a salty crew member, the other a brave PC. Each player places 3 gp on the table. A soup bowl of rum is poured and set between them. Players alternate trying to flip their coins into the soup bowl. The player with the most coins in the bowl must drink but also keeps the gold. Ties are decided by a cursing contest with one of the other sailors as judge. Flipping a coin into the bowl requires a successful {@dc 12} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) ({@skill Intimidation}) check. Drinking a soup bowl of rum requires a successful {@dc 10} Constitution saving throw to avoid becoming incapacitated for an hour. The sailors each have +3 to all rolls when playing the game.

entries.name: Foreboding Signs
entries: The following strange events occur while the party is aboard the Silver Slipper.

{@b {@i Algae Bloom.}} The deck of the ship is covered in thick, ropy algae one morning. The PCs arrive from below to find the crew attempting to scrub it clean. Nobody knows how it grew so quickly. The blanket of algae radiates weak magic. A successful {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Nature}) check confirms it is natural, but its rate of growth suggests something is not quite right.

{@b {@i Jigging at Midnight.}} One of the sailors awakens the whole ship with furious jigging in the middle of the night. He too is being driven slowly mad by the statue, and its effect is to force him into a maniacal dance. He takes no joy in the dancing, and his face is a mask of uncertainty and fear as he drives himself into exhaustion. The crew have no luck convincing him to cease his dancing, and he eventually collapses.

{@b {@i Staring Sailor.}} One of the sailors goes missing. The crew enlists the aid of the party to find him, but they fear he has fallen overboard. After a brief search, he is found in the cargo hold, sitting before the statue. He stares at it-transfixed. A successful {@dc 10} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check releases him from its hold. Otherwise, he stands up and returns to his bunk after an hour. He has no memory of the event.

{@b {@i Sullen Captain.}} Captain Sara retreats to her cabin. She does not come out except to bark orders at the increasingly ornery crew. The dark magic of the statue in the hold has begun to affect her mood and mind. She is stubbornly resistant to conversing with anyone. She appears increasingly unwell as the voyage continues: her skin pales, and she is withdrawn.

{@b {@i Swarm of Seabirds.}} Six swarms of seabirds ({@creature swarm of ravens}) attack the deck of the ship early one evening. Though the encounter is trivial for the PCs, it rattles the crew, and many begin murmuring about turning back to port.

entries.name: Midnight Fog
entries: Near midnight on the eve when the black ship is to arrive and assault the {@i Silver Slipper}, a patchy fog rolls in around Captain Sara's ship. The fog masks the arrival of the dark forces come to collect the statue. For the duration of the coming encounter and as long as the ship remains in the fog, the deck is considered lightly obscured.

entries.name: Dark Agents

entries: Bursting up onto the deck, you see a great black ship has sidled next to the Silver Slipper. Neither sail nor oar can be seen propelling this dark craft. Spiked, wooden planks have descended, and loping humanoid shapes have made their way across. The deck is filled with panicking crew, and the captain's door remains shut. "We've come for it," one of the figures hisses. The ship is being boarded.

The dark agents have come to collect the statue. The party's rest is interrupted by cries from above deck. They arrive on deck ({@b B}) to find a boarding party intent on slaughtering the crew. The boarding party consists of a captain ({@creature fext|ToB|fext}) a second mate ({@creature noctiny|ToB|noctiny}) and two (CR 9) or four (CR 10) crew ({@creature cultist||cultists}). Combat begins with the noctiny and the cultists forming a loose defensive formation around their fext captain, having already made it onto the deck ({@b A}). The black ship sinks into the water and disappears as soon as the fext is slain. The noctiny wears a gilded pearl necklace worth 750 gp. The fext captain bears the {@i {@item Shark-Tooth Crown|KPPreparedExpanded|shark-tooth crown}}, which can be taken and used by the PCs.

{@b {@i Wild Eyes and Dark Thoughts.}} The crew of the Silver Slipper are temporarily mad. The appearance of the black ship and the statue's evil aura have turned them feral. Each round on initiative count 20, there is a 50 percent chance that a crew member ({@creature bandit}) attacks a PC randomly. The crew member does not stay active as a combatant. There are a total of six crew members running amok. A successful {@dc 17} Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) check sends them below deck, ending their random attacks.

{@b {@i Evil Goes Overboard.}} Successfully defending the {@i Silver Slipper} ends the maddening effect on the crew. Captain Sara wants to toss the statue overboard and let it sink quietly in the dark waves. She will not transport it any farther. Convincing her otherwise requires magic or a successful {@dc 20} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: For saving her ship, the captain offers the PCs free passage to their original destination and a free ride to another port if they so desire. Captain Sara believes herself to be indebted to the PCs and should prove a useful ally for sailing to various destinations when the campaign requires it.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: The PCs may have made an enemy. The agents of the dark god are slain, and its prized artifact likely cast to the bottom of the sea. What other black ships sail in the god's name? What evil comes seeking revenge once the party makes it back to land?

rows: {@b An adventure for four to six characters of 5th or 6th level}

entries: I watched it lope across the horizon of the wastes at dusk. That is the shape of the end.

entries.name: Background
entries: A great threat lopes toward a small city at the edge of a wasteland. One of the leviathans of the wasteland, a gigantic, malevolent creature known locally as a Walker, appears to be on a course directly through the city. The PCs are called to heroism by the city council who have learned that the Walker is being directed by a foul {@creature darakhul ghoul|ToB|darakhul} who has gained control of the creature and directs it from atop its shoulders! Scouts have discovered a portal used by the ghoul to teleport atop the Walker. With a hastily scrawled map, the party must navigate the hills to locate the magical doorway.

In this epic and deadly adventure, the PCs must navigate wild hills, locate a teleportation portal, and slay the darakhul and his minions on teetering platforms built atop the shoulders of the Walker.

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: The council of a city built at the edge of a vast wasteland has put out an urgent call for adventurers. The councilors have learned that a {@creature darakhul ghoul|ToB|darakhul} has devised a way to command one of the leviathans that dwell in the deep wastes. The darakhul is directing the Walker on a course that intersects the city in several days. A great dust cloud obscures the Walker and blots out the sun around it-evidence of dark magic. The Walker's arrival all but ensures the city's destruction. The councilors have offered 5,000 gp as a reward to any brave enough to stop it. They have obtained a map to the portal the ghoul is using to travel, located in a wild, hilly region nearby. They provide the map to the party should they answer the call.

entries.name: Wild Hills

entries: The hills rise and fall, punctuated by gnarled trees and ragged patches of briar. A light drizzle has set in, and thin mist gathers in the low places. A strange cry sounds from far away.

The hills where the darakhul sorcerer opened his portal are dangerous and unexplored. There is evidence that halflings lived here once a long time ago, and the party may discover the odd, caved-in burrow. The map provided to the party is adequate for finding the portal within a day. The hills are filled with strange and dangerous things. The following encounters are optional as the PCs navigate the hills:

items: {@b {@i Great Hall of the Burrfoot.}} A {@creature wyvern} has nested in the ruined remains of a halfling feasting hall dug into the side of a hill. Approaching the hall's entrance, the party smells carrion, and a successful {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check discovers fresh, dragon-like tracks. The wyvern also uses a collapsed portion of the roof to enter and exit its lair. The wyvern happily attempts to eat the party as they wander by or through its nest. Inside the hall are a few intact pieces of furniture and an {@i {@item +1 sling}} with 10 bullets.

{@b {@i Lowen's Regulars.}} Lowen ({@creature veteran}) and three (CR 6) or four (CR 7) henchmen ({@creature spy||spies}) have established a permanent camp in the hills. From this camp, they engage in all manner of villainy: banditry, extortion, kidnapping. The women and men appear as hunters initially. A successful {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check suggests they are flatly lying when asked their business in the area. They are not eager to die at the hands of a well-equipped adventuring party, but left alive, they will attempt to ambush the party later in the day. A locked chest (open {@dc 10}) in the camp contains their spoils: 400 gp, 200 gp in uncut gems, and two {@i {@item potion of healing||potions of healing}}.

entries.name: In Your Campaign
entries: This adventure requires a city to be threatened by the Walker and with a small range of wild hills nearby. It requires a city council calling the party to action. It mentions a nearby wasteland. It assumes that not everyone in the party can fly and instead has them searching for a portal to gain access to the platforms and pilot of the Walker. The scenario sets the scene for an invasion that might span several sessions. The specific agenda of the darakhul is not determined, but general destruction is likely only one aspect of its plan.

The {@b {@creature darakhul ghoul|ToB|darakhul}} and {@b {@creature goat-man|ToB|goat-men}} can be replaced with a standard {@b {@creature wight}} and {@b {@creature minotaur||minotaurs}}, respectively.

entries.name: In Midgard
entries: The necrophagi of the Ghoul Empire have perfected a form of command magic through foul necromantic rituals. They are eager to test their new power and conduct experiments across Midgard, taking control of larger and more powerful creatures with each passing day. One of the ghouls has had success in dominating a tortured Walker from the wastes and pushes his new steed onward to test the limits of his commanding staff. The town of Barenna is under threat, and the PCs must stop the Walker before it arrives.

entries.name: Portal

entries: The map has taken you to the far end of Shallow Valley in the hills. Near the center of the valley, nestled between two trees, is a crackling yellow field of magic. Several humanoid shapes wander around the portal. An empty wagon sits nearby.

This is the portal allowing access to the shoulder of the Walker. A successful {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check reveals the portal is not permanent and will likely last only a few more days. There are three (CR 6) or four (CR 7) {@creature ogre||ogres} guarding the portal. The last ogre alive attempts to put its head through the portal to warn the passengers on the Walker than intruders are coming. If the ogre manages to do this, the forces beyond the portal will not be surprised when the party arrives.

Traveling through the portal is unpleasant, though it has no detrimental effects. It is reasonable for the party to cast spells in preparation for a fight, and using the portal does not dispel effects. The party can arrive on the platform ready for combat.

entries.name: Walker
entries: The Walker is a prop for the action of this adventure. It is simplest to make it a non-combatant that is impervious to attacks and spells. Ignore this instruction if you have the time to invent a fantastic way to incorporate the Walker into a fight.

While the Walker is the ultimate threat, the villains in this adventure are the darakhul pilot and his minions. Without the darakhul commanding the Walker, it recedes into its wasteland and stops its destruction.

Though it is a non-combatant, the Walker's presence should still be felt during the combat. Here are several tools to use during the fight to remind the party that they are riding a leviathan nightmare.
{@b {@i Shake and Wail.}} Use this effect in the event the PCs unleash a very effective area attack or just to add color to the combat. It affects all creatures on the platform.
The floor begins to shudder and violently shake. The Walker's scream is deafening.

On initiative count 1 or in reaction to the fight occurring on its shoulder, the Walker violently shakes and wails. All creatures on the platform must succeed a {@dc 12} Dexterity saving throw or fall {@condition prone}. Creatures who fall prone next to the edge of a platform must succeed on a {@dc 10} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check or fall off the platform to the ground below. The wail forces a concentration check ({@dc 10}) on all casters.

{@b {@i Sweeping Claw.}} At least once, and no more often than is reasonable, the Walker attempts to slash and swat the bothersome enemies from its shoulder. The Walker's accuracy is poor, and the massive claw threatens all creatures standing on the platforms.
The platform leans suddenly. The Walker raises one of its loathsome limbs, brandishing its black talons, and the claw sweeps downward.

On initiative count 1, the Walker sweeps its claw across the platforms. All creatures standing on the platforms must succeed on a {@dc 14} Dexterity saving throw or be struck by the claw for 11 ({@damage 2d10}) slashing damage. Additionally, on a failed save, the target is dragged along with the claw toward the neck for 15 feet. Creatures whose trajectory would lead them off the platform must succeed on a {@dc 10} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check or be knocked off the platform and fall to the ground below.

entries.name: Teetering Platforms

entries: Three tiers of hastily built wooden platforms are installed on the shoulder of the Walker. Several figures hold on to the sparse railing as the leviathan's steps make the ground teeter precariously. A pale humanoid in dark robes holds a blackened staff over their head. As it directs the staff, so goes the Walker.

Provided the ogre did not warn the travelers on the platforms, the PCs surprise their enemies. They arrive at the portal ({@b C}). The platforms consist of three tiers and span an 80-foot-by-50-foot area. The portal is at the lowest tier while the darakhul "pilot" stands at the highest elevation. The platforms are 70, 75, and 80 feet above the ground.

{@b {@i Battle on the Shoulders.}} The {@b {@creature darakhul ghoul|ToB|darakhul}} (located at {@b A}) and two (CR 8) or three (CR 9) {@b {@creature goat-man|ToB|goat-men}} (located at {@b B}) engage the party on the teetering platforms. The ghoul uses his Claw attack on prone opponents as much as possible. He and the goat-men work together and retreat up the tiers to form chokepoints. The dust cloud hanging over the Walker prevents sunlight from reaching the platforms. A successful {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check made on the dust cloud reveals that it is magical (dispel {@dc 14}). If the dust cloud is dispelled, the darakhul may be forced to fight in direct sunlight. (Review {@area Walker|17.4|x} above to add the Walker's actions to the combat.)

The goat-men carry jade carvings of their foul god (worth 50 gp each). The darakhul wears a silver-and-gold pendant (worth 200 gp) and a {@i {@item Cloak of the Empire|KPPreparedExpanded}}, which can be taken and worn by brave PCs.
{@b {@i The Staff.}} Only the ghoul may use the staff. If he dies or the staff is lost over the edge, the Walker stops its advance and retreats into the wastes where it originated.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The city council rewards the party as promised. Alternatively, the party might accept an estate to form a home base for further adventures in the region.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: The next step is determining what the ghoul intended. The city may be a target for the Ghoul Empire, who plot various ways to overthrow or destroy the council. Additionally, what foul magic did the darakhul employ to manufacture the staff and dust cloud? Something with strong magic must lie behind this lone ghoul's efforts.

rows: {@b An adventure for four to six characters of 5th to 7th level}

entries: Through the Astral Sea, you will find your destiny.

entries.name: Background
entries: For centuries, the monastery of Gruma-Lo has offered a place for martial training and reflection to the communities around it. The Order of Wings has led the monastery since its establishment, and the small council of elders routinely sends the monks out to assist the local populations as needed.

At the heart of the monastery is a bundle of feathers from a legendary bird that imbues the elder monks with various magical abilities, including limited flight. Recently, the artifact has drawn the attention of a ruthless warlord named Eclipse, who plots to steal the feathers for her hoard.

When the PCs learn that the old monastery is under attack, they are implored to rush to its defense. Guided by a messenger monk, the party travels a secret path to reach the monastery quickly, where fire, violence, and foes await them.
Here are a just a few suggestions to bring the PCs into the adventure:

items: The party is traveling the wilds when they meet a monk named Veeth, who is hurrying along a narrow but well-worn path with a look of panic. He reveals his monastery is under attack, and he has been sent to find help from nearby communities. Veeth explains the elders of the monastery are in mortal danger, and there would be a reward if the party would help.

While staying in a small village or town, the party's activities are interrupted by a commotion. Veeth, a monk from the nearby monastery of Gruma-Lo, has arrived with pleas for help to save the place from invaders. Veeth promises favor and gold to those willing to help.

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: The following NPC will be present for this adventure:

{@b {@i Veeth, Foot of Gruma-Lo.}} Veeth ({@creature acolyte}) is an elf in his early 150s. He is dressed in plain gray monk's attire, including a belted tunic, simple breeches, and padded gloves. His boots are decorated with feathers collected during his time at Gruma-Lo. He carries no weapons, though a ceremonial knife hangs from his belt. Veeth is low-ranking within the monastery, but he knows a great deal about the land around it. He speaks purposefully and frequently pauses to ensure his words are precise. Veeth wants to save Gruma-Lo. He is dedicated to the task of recruiting help for his monastery.

entries.name: Meet with Veeth

entries: A tall elf in simple gray clothes stands calmly before you. His boots are adorned with dozens of feathers stitched carefully in a pleasing pattern.
Veeth seeks help in defending Gruma-Lo from the forces of the warlord Eclipse. Through conversation, Veeth reveals the following:

items: Gruma-Lo is a monastery less than 2 hours away by foot.
The monastery and its elders are in mortal danger.
Eclipse seeks the treasures of the monastery, including the fabled Feathers of Gruma-Lo.
Eclipse and her soldiers are already attacking.
The warlord's mount is a cruel, domesticated {@creature wyvern}.
The monastery can pay 1,000 gp to the party if they agree to help defend it.

entries: Veeth can guide them along a secret path to quickly reach Gruma-Lo.

entries.name: Travel the Secret Path
entries: The regular footpath from the nearest town to the monastery is approximately 5 miles. The monks know a path through a cave system that skirts the Astral Plane for a short distance and allows them to travel the path in half the time. If the party agrees to follow Veeth, he leads them to the caves and through its brief intersection with the other plane.
Roll a {@dice d6} and consult the {@b Astral Plane Events} table to punctuate the party's travels through the Astral Plane, or choose something appropriate:

rows: {@b {@i Darkness.}} The party enters a field of impenetrable darkness. Within the field, all sound is reduced to the volume of a whisper. The only way through the darkness is for each PC to whisper their worst fear to the rest of the party. Alternatively, a PC can lose 10 hit points to arrive on the field's other side. Once out of the darkness, each PC has advantage on saving throws against being {@condition frightened} until they complete a long rest.

{@b {@i Dreams.}} The party stumbles into the dreams of an {@creature owlbear}, slumbering in the material world nearby. In the dream, the PCs are the owlbear's cubs who are learning to hunt. Based on the PCs' personalities and traits, each player must describe how their PC would learn to hunt. Afterward, the PCs all have advantage on Intelligence ({@skill Nature}) and Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) checks until they complete a long rest.

{@b {@i Lessons Shared.}} The party arrives in the mind of a scholar attending a lecture at a nearby institute. After sharing a lesson learned in their time as an adventurer, each PC has advantage on Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) checks until they complete a long rest.

{@b {@i Light.}} The party is absorbed into an area of blinding light. Each PC must share their greatest aspiration in order to pass through the light and regain their sight. Alternatively, a PC can spend one Hit Die to navigate the blinding light. After leaving the illuminated area, each PC cannot be {@condition blinded} until they complete a long rest.

{@b {@i Nightmares.}} The party and Veeth fall into the nightmare of a sleeping hill giant. The nightmare consists of the giant desperately throwing rocks at an encroaching wave of farmers armed with spears and torches. After describing how they would throw the rock, each PC has advantage on their next Dexterity saving throw. This effect ends when the PC completes a long rest.

{@b {@i Unity.}} The party arrives inside the thoughts of a hivemind-like aberration. There, the party walks endless corridors lined with waves of pure emotion and need. Lost, the party must turn to one another to escape. The party must find a singular identity by each uttering a word that best describes the party as a whole. The chosen words become imbued with power. Once, before they complete a long rest, each PC can utter one of the chosen words to give another PC Inspiration.

entries.name: Save the Monastery

entries: Up the rise, you arrive at a small clearing before a bridge made from rope and vine. Everywhere is fire and smoke and the pitiful cries of the injured. Across the bridge, through the smoke, you see the monastery of Gruma-Lo burning.

The monastery is intended to offer two encounters chained together. If the party insists on engaging both the soldiers in {@area 1|18.1|u} and the warlord with mount in {@area 3|18.3|u} at the same time, let them.
{@b {@i Smoke.}} The entire map is lightly obscured by smoke. The smoke is not magical and can be dispersed with spells and effects normally.

{@b {@i Fire.}} The bridge and the monastery are currently on fire. Creatures who start or end their turn in a space that is on fire take {@damage 3} ({@damage 1d6}) fire damage. The fire is not magical and can be extinguished normally.

{@b {@i Injured Monks.}} The area is littered with dead and injured monks. During the chained combat encounters, a PC can use an action to stabilize a fallen monk. For each monk stabilized during the encounter, the party receives an additional 200 gp from the elders if Eclipse is defeated.
{@b {@i Blessing of Veeth.}} Veeth casts {@spell bless} on as many party members as possible before retreating to safety. He does not enter combat and maintains his spell for as long as he can.

entries.name: Area 1: Before the Bridge
entries: Three (four if the party is 7th level) of Eclipse's warriors ({@creature veteran||veterans}) guard the southern side of the bridge. They attack the party on sight. The battle has worn on the soldiers though, and they are demoralized by their losses. A successful {@dc 12} Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) check sends one soldier running before the fight starts.

entries.name: Area 2: Bridge
entries: The bridge spans 120 feet above the ground. Creatures attempting to cross on foot must succeed on a {@dc 10} Dexterity saving throw or trip on burning ropes and vines, and are {@condition restrained} until the end of their next turn.

entries.name: Area 3: Monastery Grounds
entries: Eclipse ({@creature gladiator}) stands beside her {@creature wyvern} mount, watching the monastery burn. Inside the monastery proper, her soldiers are busy retrieving the Feathers of Gruma-Lo. Eclipse and her mount attack the party on sight. The wyvern has been treated cruelly by Eclipse, and a character trained in Wisdom (Animal Handling or Insight) notices the creature's disdain for the warlord. A PC can attempt to stop the wyvern from attacking with a successful {@dc 15} Wisdom (Animal Handling or Insight) check. Reduce the wyvern's hit points by 30, if the party is 6th level, or by 60 if the party is 5th level.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: Provided the party defeats Eclipse and her mount, the soldiers flee. The monastery elders offer the party 1,000 gp as a reward for helping defend Gruma-Lo. If the party is willing, the monks offer to fly them to any destination they choose within 50 miles. Using the power of their magical feathers, the monks can deposit the party to such a destination within 2 hours.

rows: {@b An adventure for four to six characters of 6th to 7th level}

entries: It's true I used to run with the Untamed, back when Owl was the leader. I don't associate with 'em now though, not after what I saw. I got a stomach for all manner of things-except whatever it was I spied through the door at the back of the hideout. The room changed shape, like a puzzle putting itself together. Filled me with a kind of fear I ain't known before or since. I can't say what dark thing the Untamed are up to, but there ain't a one of 'em casts a shadow no more—not that you'd see 'em out in sun anyway.

entries.name: Background
entries: The Untamed are a street gang in a busy city. A recent change in leadership has transformed the members from pickpockets and second-story thieves into kidnappers for an interdimensional aberration named Xlrieh'oc. Their hideout is now a strange and wicked factory, capable of extracting the firm essence from a humanoid in a process that leaves the victim partly ethereal and casting no shadow. Though most victims die during the procedure, those who survive are conscripted into the gang. The extracted essence is crated and shipped to the aberration's home plane through a breach between worlds in the hideout's backroom.

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: The gang members are all survivors of the strange extraction ritual. As such, they are afflicted with a curse with the following effects:

items: Stealth +5
Vulnerable to fire
Resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical weapons
Disadvantage on all rolls made while in direct sunlight

entries: {@i Note: the curse affects only humanoid gang members.}

entries.name: Symbols of Xlrieh'oc
entries: Three symbols, drawn in reference to Xlrieh'oc, maintain the portal to his realm and cause various effects upon the viewer. After a PC has been affected by a symbol or makes a successful saving throw against its effect, the PC becomes immune to that particular symbol for 24 hours. If all three symbols are destroyed, the portal in the backroom closes. Destroying a symbol requires a successful {@dc 13} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check. Though the text suggests where the symbols are located, their placement is ultimately up to the needs of the GM:

items: {@b {@i Symbol of Anguish.}} Witnesses to this symbol within 15 feet of it must make a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw, taking {@damage 9} ({@damage 2d8}) psychic damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

{@b {@i Symbol of Fear.}} Witnesses to this symbol within 15 feet of it must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition frightened} for an hour. The saving throw is repeated every 15 minutes.
{@b {@i Symbol of Madness.}} Witnesses to this symbol within 15 feet of it must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition blinded} and {@condition stunned} for 1 minute.

entries.name: Area 1: Alley

entries: Refuse and rubble obscure the entry to this dark alleyway. Stepping over an open sewer channel, you find yourself standing in a passage between several warehouses. Small things scuttle between broken crates and general filth.

Three gang members ({@creature scout||scouts}) and a hired doorman ({@creature gladiator}) who is unaffected by the curse are hidden in the alley, and they attempt to take the PCs by surprise. A successful {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check finds the hidden entry to their hideout. Scrawled on the door is a {@i symbol of fear} (see {@i Symbols of Xlrieh'oc} above). Whoever finds the door, and those nearby, are subject to the symbol's effects.

entries.name: Area 2: Warehouse

entries: A maze of crates fills the warehouse. Rising to the bare wooden rafters, the crates vary in size, and each displays an enigmatic brand. Pale violet light emanates from unseen sources. A small footpath winds its way among the stacked cargo.
The warehouse proper is currently unoccupied. Most of the crates are empty. Within the crate labyrinth is the Untamed's extraction table:

A long, wooden table with leather restraints is bathed in the violet light of several candle stands. Knives in dark scabbards lay on its surface, and a peculiar burn mark is found repeated near the collar restraint at one end. On the floor are two sealed crates showing evidence of being recently used. A parchment is crudely nailed to the table, hanging apron-like from the table's edge.

The parchment is a set of instructions for removing the essence of a mortal. It is written in an unknown tongue. Looking too closely at the parchment triggers the {@i symbol of anguish} (see {@i Symbols of Xlrieh'oc} above) that marks it. Once looked at, the viewer and those nearby are subject to its effects. A successful {@dc 14} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana} or {@skill Investigation}) check reveals the diagram is a ritual object, describing a surgical technique of sorts. Opening the crate requires a successful {@dc 12} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check. Inside the crate is a harmless white powder.

entries.name: Area 3: Room with Five Corners

entries: The view through the doorway into the backroom portrays a dizzying nightmare spectacle. Beyond the threshold is a plain chamber, breached along one wall by a geometric impossibility: a fifth corner has appeared there, yet the room remains square. Space and time argue in this place, and a precipitation of dread hangs in the air. Pale figures pass crates into the anomalous corner as unseen hands receive them.
Two gang members ({@creature scout||scouts}) are passing crates to an unseen party through the extradimensional portal. Gang leader Emit ({@creature priest}) oversees the transaction.

When disturbed, the members take positions behind crates, providing half cover, near the portal. Two {@creature phase spider||phase spiders} lurk in the rafters and attempt to jump down behind the party once combat starts. The floor here displays the {@i symbol of madness} (see {@i Symbols of Xlrieh'oc} above), and PCs fighting near the portal trigger its effects. Shortly after the phase spiders descend, the PCs see the outline of a humanoid, stepping through the portal into the room. As it arrives, its shape transforms, and a {@creature gibbering mouther} emerges to joins the fight.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: For a street gang, the hideout is suspiciously devoid of stolen goods. Emit carries an impossibly complex navigation tool made from gold set with several perfect diamonds. A successful {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check suggests it is aligned to a fifth cardinal point. It is worth 300 gp in raw materials.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: Did the party close the strange portal in the back room? What horrible place does it lead them to if traveled through? What of the white powder in the crates? How long does Xlrieh'oc hold a grudge, and how is their anger manifested?

rows: {@b An adventure for four to six characters of 6th or 7th level}

entries: We left Gorol's Outpost and went north for several days. The weather held, and we counted our blessings. We'd heard stories of the place and had it in our hearts to find those ruins. Vladimir had a map we'd bought from some locals, who'd said it was as old as some worlds-whatever that meant. It was early evening when we saw the crack in the glacier. We went single file through a long tunnel that opened into a valley. Then we saw it: a stone terrace partially encased in ice. We made camp with the intention of exploring the ruins in the morning. What came for us just before dawn, I cannot say. White wings and cruel faces-laughter . . . I fear I am the only one left.

entries.name: Background
entries: {@creature Oithois|KPPreparedExpanded} the exceptional ice mephit and his foul underlings have uncovered a powerful relic at the entry to ancient ruins. The monstrous mephits seek to crack a hole between the Material Plane and their icy home world. Oithois plots to lead an army of elemental lackeys and conquer the civilized outposts of the north. This ice mephit has studied the machine and is confident he can open a gateway to the Elemental Plane of Ice.

PCs are approached by a frostbitten traveler, who pleads with them to assault the terrace. The adventurers must mount an attack against the mephits, contend with an unintentionally summoned young white dragon, and defeat Oithois upon the icebound terrace.

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: A stranger named Jom appears in a northern town or city, desperately seeking adventurers. He is a short man with pale skin and squinting eyes. He explains that his exploration party discovered ruins buried in a glacier. They'd decided to make camp for the night and explore the ruins in the morning but were attacked just before dawn by cackling monsters on frosty wings who murdered or captured his companions. Before he escaped, he saw a stone terrace rising out of the snow, and an ancient machine glinted from the topmost level.
He provides the following information:

items: The ruins are a day's walk away.
The ruins are massive, but only the entryway and its terrace are accessible.
The ruins are of unknown origin.
He does not know the fate of his companions. He sustained a nasty injury from the claw of the larger monster.
He hopes some of his companions still live.

entries: A successful {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check reveals he is ill. If pressed, Jom shows his injury. A massive laceration on his leg shows signs of a strange infection. A successful {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Medicine}) check uncovers the injury's magical nature, and a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check suggests Jom is slowly turning into an ice mephit. The only cure is to pour the melted remains of his attacker's clawed finger over the injury. Jom offers 100 gp to save him.

entries.name: Arriving at the Terrace

entries: A frosted stone terrace rises from the snowy ground and ends several levels up at a large door. A myriad of staircases provides access to elevated platforms while other regions of the terrace are locked behind massive walls of ice. Crystals, mounted in stone receptacles, pulse and hum in the cool air. A great bronze machine sits on the topmost level, and a spindly white figure hunches near it—whose long and wicked face regards you.
The mephits ({@b E} and {@b F}) attack the party. {@creature Oithois|KPPreparedExpanded} remains by the machine and works frantically to activate it.

items: {@b A}: Planewalking device, {@creature Oithois|KPPreparedExpanded} ({@creature ice mephit}; see {@area Oithois, the Larger-than-Average Mephit|20.9|x})
{@b B}, {@b C}, {@b D}: Gate crystals
{@b E}: Six {@creature ice mephit||ice mephits}
{@b F}: Three {@creature ice mephit||ice mephits}
{@b G}: Gate

entries.name: Fight on the Terrace
entries: A round-by-round suggested sequence for the encounter is provided here, but the details should be modified as needed to suit the GM's need:
{@b {@i Round 1.}} The {@creature ice mephit||mephits} attack the PCs.
{@b {@i Round 2.}} {@creature Oithois|KPPreparedExpanded} starts up the planewalking device.
{@b {@i Round 3.}} The crystals activate, a gate opens ({@b G}), and {@creature Oithois|KPPreparedExpanded} attacks the PCs (see {@area Oithois, the Larger-than-Average Mephit|20.9|x}).
{@b {@i Round 4.}} A {@creature young white dragon||young white dragon} emerges through the gate (see {@area Angry Dragon|20.6|x}).
{@b {@i Round 5.}} The dragon attacks, and the mephits flee.
{@b {@i Round 6.}} The gate pulses brightly, and the crystals deactivate.
{@b {@i Round 7.}} The gate unleashes a blizzard on initiative count 20 (see {@area Blizzard|20.7|x}).
{@b {@i Round 8.}} The gate closes.

entries.name: Angry Dragon
entries: When the gate opens, a {@creature young white dragon||young white dragon} named Halicix falls through. He is entirely surprised by his interplanar journey and is quickly enraged. He begins by using his Cold Breath on the largest clump of creatures. He has no affinity with the mephits and happily targets them as well (though they are immune to cold damage). Once Halicix attacks, the mephits use their turns to flee. {@creature Oithois|KPPreparedExpanded}, angry at being thwarted, remains and continues attacking the party until slain.

{@b {@i Bargaining with Halicix.}} Halicix is understandably angry, but a determined PC can halt the brute's aggression long enough for a short exchange. Two successful {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) checks combined with a cessation of attacks stops Halicix from attacking the party for a round. Assign further checks or a roleplaying challenge to determine if the adventurers are able to convince the dragon they are not to blame for his unplanned jaunt to the Material Plane. Keep in mind that white dragons are more beast than not, and an offering of something valuable may be required.

entries.name: Blizzard
entries: The round before the gate closes, on initiative count 20, a blast of powerful wind from the frozen world beyond blows over the terrace, causing the following effects:

items: Each PC must make a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw, taking 9 ({@damage 2d8}) cold damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

Small creatures must succeed on a {@dc 12} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check or be blown 20 feet in a direct line away from the gate. A further successful {@dc 12} Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check avoids falling prone at the end of this movement. Creatures running into a wall or other object during this movement take 2 ({@damage 1d4}) bludgeoning damage as they topple over the obstacle.
Snow covers the terrace, making the area difficult terrain.

entries.name: Gate Crystals
entries: Used to energize the planar device, the translucent white crystals on the terrace thrum and radiate magic. If a creature comes into contact with a crystal while it is energizing, they must succeed on a {@dc 14} Constitution saving throw or be stunned for 1 round. The crystals can be destroyed (AC 10, hp 10), and a destroyed crystal cannot power the machine. One crystal (C) has a small, removable crystal fragment set into its base, and a successful {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check reveals it functions as a {@i {@item lantern of revealing}}.

entries.name: Oithois, the Larger-than-Average Mephit
entries: {@creature Oithois|KPPreparedExpanded} has the following bonuses, owing to his Medium size: +1 AC, +7 hp, +1 to hit and damage for all attacks. Creatures struck by his claw attack must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw or suffer from {@disease Rime Disease|KPPreparedExpanded}.

{@b {@i Rime Disease.}} Victims of rime disease lose 25 percent of their movement speed immediately and 25 percent per day for 3 days. On the third day, the victim transforms into an {@creature ice mephit}. The disease may be cured with a {@spell lesser restoration} spell or by pouring the melted remains of Oithois's claw over the wound.

entries.name: Planewalking Device
entries: On the topmost platform ({@b A}) is an ancient machine capable of opening gates to other planes. The machine still functions. Operating the machine requires a successful {@dc 18} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check. Once activated, energy from the crystals located on the terrace arcs into the machine, and after 1 round, the machine opens a gate to a random plane for a minute. The gate appears within 10 feet of the large, dead tree ({@b G}). PCs could open a gate to a specific plane provided these conditions are met:

items: The user can conjure up a specific image of the destination in their mind.
The user can cast 3rd-level spells.
At least two gate crystals are intact on the terrace.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The stands containing the crystals have a total of six small diamonds (100 gp value each) set into their rims. Removing a diamond requires a successful {@dc 12} Dexterity ({@item thieves' tools}) check. A failed check results in a loss of 25 gp value for each point the attempt missed by (for example, a roll of 10 would reduce the value to 50 gp)

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: Where to from here? Do the icy ruins reveal a vast complex full of magical interplanar technology? Do the actions on the terrace catch the attention of the ruin's occupants, who take poorly to being discovered?

rows: {@b An adventure for four to six characters of 7th level}

entries: We saw it-don't turn your heads. Up near Hilltop Crossroad and the temple. It walked south, and the trees fell in its path. Even the moon hid. Gods help Father Dren. We saw it-don't turn your heads. Up near Hilltop Crossroad and the temple. It walked south, and the trees fell in its path. Even the moon hid. Gods help Father Dren.

entries.name: Background
entries: A colossal demon has trod upon a sandy temple. Following closely behind, gnolls and hyenas slay all living things that cross their path. PCs discover a grisly sight when they investigate: a pack of gnolls is finishing the ritual to summon a servant of their god. They have readied a great gift—the temple's sacred scythe—in preparation of its arrival. PCs must carve a path through hyenas and gnolls to reclaim the temple before facing it and its newly acquired prize.

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: An acolyte named Ider pleads for the party to save his master. He smooths his torn robes and tells the PCs that his temple is under attack from dark forces after a huge beast passed by. He offers the PCs his jeweled prayer mantle (worth 60 gp) to investigate and return the temple's holy relic (a scythe) to him.

First, a great evil passed. It crushed the graves and most of the eastern wall as it went. We cowered in the stores-overwhelmed by fear. We spent the next day in shock and prayer. On the following night, the unearthly howls and cries began. Soon after, they came. A horrible pack, eyes aglow in the darkness. I fled, but he remained . . . and his screams haunt me.

{@b {@i Scythe.}} The scythe is a holy symbol of the temple—and this particular scythe is a magic relic. The gnolls found it, covered it in their foul excrement, and transformed it into an instrument of evil. When wielded by their god's servant, the scythe has several effects:

items: The first 5 damage from any attack against the wielder is dealt instead to a random ally (gnolls and hyenas).
The wielder receives +1 to all saving throws against spells.
The wielder gains the following action, which must be used as an option for Multiattack:

entries: {@b {@i Abyssal Harvest.}} {@i Melee Weapon Attack:} +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., up to 4 targets. Hit: 5 ({@damage 1d8 + 1}) slashing damage.
Spellcasters whose primary attribute is Wisdom become aware of the following when they are within 20 feet of the scythe:

items: It is a corrupted holy relic.

It can be cleansed, requiring the spellcaster to expend a 4th-level spell slot and succeed on a {@dc 14} Wisdom check. Once cleansed, the scythe loses all powers and is dropped unceremoniously by its wielder.
The scythe can be cleansed after the combat in a similar manner that excludes the need for an ability check.

entries.name: Area 1: Temple Grounds

entries: Numerous stone cairns have been erected on the grounds of a small, walled temple. Great clawed footprints press into the grass and travel from north to south. The cairns directly in its path have been scattered and destroyed. The wind carries a foul smell from the temple, and smoke rises from within. Unsettling yips and stirrings are apparent among the ruined monuments.

The cairns contain the remains of the faithful. The destroyed cairns create difficult terrain and half cover. A successful {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check reveals the smoke is unnaturally thick, and a successful {@dc 14} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check confirms the smoke is rising from a magic ritual.

{@b {@i Lurking in the Cairns.}} Five {@creature hyena||hyenas} gnaw on the bones unearthed by the demon's passing. They are bolstered by having such close contact with the great evil (gaining +1 to hit and the {@creature panther}'s pounce ability). The hyenas attack loudly and alert the gnolls inside the temple. On the 2nd round, three {@creature gnoll||gnolls} arrive at one of the temple's entryways and fire their longbows at the PCs. They switch to melee attacks when pressed. The gnolls attempt to keep the party occupied while the pack leader (use the statistics of a {@creature gnoll} but with the Spellcasting ability of a {@creature cult fanatic}) finishes summoning a {@creature Fang of Nkishi|KPPreparedExpanded} (use the statistics of a {@creature gladiator}, except the fang has a {@creature giant hyena}'s Rampage trait and Bite attack). Move the action to {@area 2|21.5|u} when the PCs are within 10 feet of a doorway into the temple.

entries.name: Area 2: Temple

entries: Entrails have been strung up around the doorways—a grim decoration that confirms the fate of the priest. The temple's open-air worship area has been horribly desecrated. Dark smoke rises from a burning pyre of furniture and temple items. A towering, canine brute plants an excrement-covered scythe into the ground beside the fire, readies its glaive, and charges.

The gnolls' pack leader (see {@area 1|21.4|u}) joins the fray, inciting their followers: any gnolls or hyenas remaining gain a free and automatic use of the bonus action granted by their Rampage trait. The round after the pack leader attacks, the {@creature Fang of Nkishi|KPPreparedExpanded} (see {@area 1|21.4|u}) leaps from the smoky blaze and lands beside the scythe. The fang retrieves the weapon, and all attack the party.

{@b {@i Fire.}} The fire burning here is magical in nature. Used by the gnolls to summon the dreaded fang, the flames drive the evil pack into a frenzy. As long as the fire burns, on initiative count 10, all gnolls and hyenas within 25 feet of it regenerate 1 hit point. The fire can be extinguished with a {@spell create or destroy water} spell or with a successful {@dc 10} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check to scatter the fire's fuel.

From the smoke and flame, a charred canine monstrosity leaps toward the scythe. Its long teeth glow like smoldering embers. With a quick jerk, the creature frees the scythe and cuts a menacing swath before bounding into battle.
The fang of Nkishi prefers to be at the center of melee, engaging as many targets as possible.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The gnolls wear the jewelry collected from their victims as they follow the demon: there are four gold and silver earrings (worth 20 gp total), a fine leather belt with a copper buckle that depicts a ram's head (worth 10 gp), and an archer's gauntlet made from boiled leather and silver (worth 15 gp). The pack leader's coin purse has 30 gp, all encrusted in blood.

Once cleansed, the bone-and-wood scythe gleams an alabaster white. It is worth 70 gp. The acolyte happily trades his mantle for the scythe and offers his knowledge and healing for a week. He will not fight, but out of combat, he confers advantage to all Intelligence ({@skill Religion}) and Wisdom ({@skill Medicine}) checks made by the PCs.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: What brought the gargantuan evil into the Material World? It walks a straight path toward some undeclared destination. Tracking the abyssal evil is not difficult, but what allies and enemies are made when the PCs decide to follow?

rows: {@b An adventure for four to six characters of 7th or 8th level}

entries: Ladies and gentlemen, welcome to our humble show. The Night's Promise Theater Troupe has rehearsed a wondrous panoply of song, poem, and soliloquy. Lights dim, and let the show begin!

entries.name: Background
entries: A powerful evil plots to corrupt the fey audience that attends a performance as priests pose as performers to set the stage for their master's arrival in the final act.
While staying in the fey community—and perhaps as partial reward for some previous accomplishment—the party is invited to the performance.
In this dramatic and deadly adventure, the PCs witness a strange performance and the corruption of the fey audience before defeating a herald of darkness and her priests.

entries.name: Running the Adventure

entries: A folded leaf reveals golden writing when opened: "You are most cordially invited to attend our celebration and performance at the Odeum tonight," signed the Night's Promise Theater Troupe.

The party receives invitations to the performance by the leaders of the city. The villainous theater troupe have no idea that the PCs are attending and are under the assumption their corruption of the audience will go unchallenged.

entries.name: In Your Campaign
entries: This adventure requires a fey community large enough to support a theater. It assumes the PCs attend the performance. The {@creature herald of darkness|ToB} is a grand corruptor of the fey and has managed to enter the city under false pretenses. The performance is divided into acts, which you may supplement with found or created material that suits the theme of the act.
The {@creature herald of darkness|ToB} can be replaced with a {@creature medusa} in addition to the priests.

entries.name: In Midgard
entries: In the Arbonesse Forest, nestled in the trees a few miles from the River Court itself, lies the small fey village of Rigsbottom. Built in the ruins of an ancient elven town, Rigsbottom is populated by all manner of fey creatures, who trade freely with their brethren and the elves of the River Court. The village is famous for its restoration of an old elven performance house, and a theatrical festival is held in Rigsbottom each year. The party is drawn to the town during their adventures in the Arbonesse where the plot unfolds.

entries.name: At the Theater

entries: A semicircle of stone benches-built to gaze upon a gilded and ornate proscenium-ring the stage. Above you is a canopy of leaves and branches with tiny glowing lights that flit here and there. Fey citizens filter in and take their seats with you. Onstage, a number of performers make ready. A tall curtain conceals something toward the rear center of the stage.
Allow the PCs to take their seats. They may sit together or separately. Eventually the lights in the canopy dim, and the performance starts with a jaunty tune.
The performance is divided into three acts. There is no clear story to the performance. The acts are gestural and allow for as little or as much additional material as the GM would like to include.

entries.name: Act 1: Revelry

entries: It was a festival to celebrate all festivals, and even the mice danced.

In the first act, three clowns appear on stage. They engage in a number of entertaining and humorous antics. There is juggling, bawdy poems, obscene limericks, and other performances meant to celebrate the silly and trivial. Toward the end of the act, the clowns play an energetic jig. Many audience members stand and dance along with the performers. The PCs must succeed a {@dc 16} Wisdom saving throw or be compelled to dance as well. The dancing ends quickly, and there are no other effects. Be sure to keep the mood light in the first act, and feel free to bring original or classic limericks to the table.

entries.name: Act 2: Portents

entries: Winter came, and shadows grew. A new star rose in the night sky.

In the second act, two crones arrive onstage and deliver somber monologues. The crones philosophize and praise entropy. The theme of their performance is dark portents—the arrival of unwanted gifts, the grotesque faces of those in despair. Toward the end of the act, the crones begin talking with the audience. They begin revealing information about the audience that they should not know. Have the crones announce facts about the PCs that the performers would not know nor be capable of guessing. The tone of the second act is serious and slightly ominous. Bring grim verses to add tension to the act.

entries.name: Act 3: Darkness Arrives

entries: "And now, to close our humble show—the Lady of Loneliness, the Mistress of Melancholy—our true master of ceremonies." A performer draws back the curtain and reveals an impossibly tall elf. She smiles, and it is dreadful and beautiful at once. "I bring you such gifts . . ."

The woman is a {@creature herald of darkness|ToB}, and she begins to sing a low and frightening song. The fey in the audience clasp their ears or begin to writhe ecstatically. Combat begins with the herald onstage ({@b A}) and her two (CR 11) or three (CR 12) {@creature priest} spread out near the front of the stage. The herald uses her Majesty of the Abyss at the beginning of combat and Shadow Form to position herself best for her Embrace Darkness. The priests heal and assist the herald in bringing down the PCs, whose presence has frustrated the herald's plans. Slaying the herald ends the corrupting influence on the audience.

entries.name: Audience Participation

entries: The audience begins to tremble, wail, and thrash. The song sung by the creature onstage has a strong effect on the fey around you. Limbs elongate, jaws unhinge-what shadows burst from their heart cages?

The orations and singing of the {@creature herald of darkness|ToB} have a profound effect on the fey sitting beside the PCs. While some are able to reject the corrupting gifts offered by the herald, many cannot. The audience members do not move and should be treated like hazards—though the party can slay them automatically with any attack. The herald and her minions are unaffected by the audience. Distribute corrupted fey throughout the theater as desired, and use the following effects to add flavor and danger to the encounter.

items: {@b {@i Devourer.}} The audience member's mouth and teeth grow large, and its jaw unhinges. It gropes blindly for something to satiate its sudden hunger. PCs who start or end their turn next to a devourer are subject to its Bite attack: {@b {@i Bite.}} {@i Melee Weapon Attack:} {@hit 6} to hit, reach 5 ft., 1 target. Hit: 8 ({@damage 1d6 + 4}) piercing damage.

{@b {@i Dreamer.}} On initiative count 15 of the 1st round, all dreamers project their waking dreams into the world via a burst of psychic energy. The projections varysome are clouds of butterflies, others are waves of blood, and still others are sail boats navigating stormy seas. These projections have no mechanical effect but provide an opportunity to fill the theater battle with strange objects and visions. They remain manifested in the world until the herald is slain.

{@b {@i Thrasher.}} Thrashers' limbs extend unnaturally, and their movements become unpredictable. Their twisting forms are a danger to any who step too close. PCs who start or end their turn within 5 feet of a thrasher, or whose movement passes adjacent to a thrasher, must succeed a {@dc 16} Dexterity saving throw or be pushed 15 feet in a random direction and knocked prone.

{@b {@i Wailer.}} On initiative count 20 of the 1st round, all wailers cry uncontrollably, their bodies wracked by sobs. In their coherent moments, they can be heard complaining about the cold. PCs within 10 feet of a wailer must succeed a {@dc 16} Charisma saving throw or become inconsolably sad. Affected PCs have disadvantage on saving throws until the end of their next turn.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Provided the party didn't slay any of the audience, the fey community reward the party with a {@i {@item ring of shooting stars}}. An escort to the limits of the fey's domain is earned for slaying the herald, and the party earn the favor of a fey community.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: The herald's ploy has brought her success in the past. Perhaps she and her priests have left a trail of corrupted fey, human, and goblin communities behind her. What might save these communities from the corruption?

rows: {@b An adventure for four to six characters of 8th or 9th level}

entries: We've been running these fights since before my granddaddy helped drive them gnolls out. We have a proud history of taking care of the animals too-get 'em as pups from the dwarves up in Granitehold. Sure, it's bloody, but you're not in the soft lands of kings and queens anymore, are you. Say, did you hear that?

entries.name: Background
entries: Bleak Rock is a small village at the edge of civilization. The last outpost before a massive mountain range, its remote setting attracts those wishing to hide or escape. Trade with a nearby dwarven city has kept the village on the map: metal goods from the dwarves travel through before being sold in the markets of major centers.

While staying in Bleak Rock overnight, the PCs are invited to attend the town's only source of entertainment: dogmole fighting. The night's fights go awry when the animals' owners feed their fighters an alchemical concoction sold to them by an unscrupulous merchant. During the fight, the animals become magically enhanced, and the shallow fighting pit cannot contain their fury. When the town residents are threatened by the rampaging critters, the PCs must contend not only with the maddened dogmoles but also their owners, who refuse to let their prize fighters be put down.

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: Use the following as a round-by-round tactical guide or as a loose narrative sequence:

items: {@b {@i Round 0.}} Suddenly, the animals stop their growling, stop circling one another. Their small frames contort, and the snapping sounds of their skeletons changing shape echo off the pit's walls. Dust rises from the dry floor of the arena and obscures the view momentarily but soon settles enough to reveal the dogmoles' dreadful and gargantuan transformation. Otherworldly calls silence the crowd. "A bad night for betting," whispers a nearby villager, and then all is violence.

{@b {@i Round 1.}} Skitch ({@creature Dogmole Juggernaut|ToB|dogmole juggernaut}) leaps into the stands ({@b A}). Ingot ({@creature Dogmole Juggernaut|ToB|dogmole juggernaut}) starts at {@b B} but burrows east 10 feet through the wall of the pit. If attacked, Ingot flees his tunnel and fights in the pit. Magh begins at {@b C} while Old Balf begins at {@b D}.
{@b {@i Round 2.}} Skitch eats townspeople. Ingot burrows east 10 feet. Magh and Old Balf defend their pets as described below.
{@b {@i Round 3.}} Skitch continues to eat townspeople. Uncontested, Ingot burrows out of the ground and begins eating townspeople ({@b F}).

entries.name: Magh Udneer

entries: A tall woman in stained coveralls and enormous leather mitts, Magh stares unflinchingly with hard gray eyes.

{@b {@i Miner, Mother, Dogmole Owner.}} Magh is the tough-as-nails glue that holds the Bleak Rock mining operation together. She oversees a crew of 12 in the iron mine just north of town. Magh's dogmole, Ingot, is the love of her life, much to the chagrin of her husband Uro and son Klip. Having won many battles against the region's inhospitable invaders, Magh is considered a {@creature veteran} in combat: she has no crossbow and has an AC of 12 (leather armor).

Attacking Ingot makes her hostile toward the PCs, and she attacks them to defend her pet. Magh is immune to intimidation attempts, but a successful {@dc 14} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check convinces her to stop attacking the party. Beating the DC by 7 or more enlists her aid in putting Ingot down. ("If anyone's to do it, it ought to be me.")

Killing Magh incurs the wrath of the miners (twelve {@creature thug||thugs} without crossbows), who attempt to drive the PCs out of town after the {@creature Dogmole Juggernaut|ToB|dogmole juggernaut} combat is resolved. Calming them requires a successful {@dc 17} Charisma ({@skill Intimidation} or {@skill Persuasion}) check, which is reduced to 12 if a PC first succeeds on a {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check to determine that only a quarter of the miners are committed to fighting.

entries.name: Old Balf

entries: Bent and wiry, Old Balf wears fine clothing and a fancy hat. He moves with an unsettling speed for such an old man.

{@b {@i Rocking Chair Warmer, Darts Enthusiast, Coot.}} Old Balf is a long-retired performer turned town crank. His past as an acrobat and juggler for the Yellow Haze traveling circus show makes him surprisingly limber and quick. His dogmole, Skitch, is the only living thing in town that feels affection toward the crotchety crack shot.

An avid fan of darts, Balf always carries a magical dart that returns to his hand after being thrown. Balf is treated as a {@creature spy} in combat: he carries no melee weapons and uses darts instead of a shortbow. Attacking Skitch sends Balf into a cunning rage. He Sneak Attacks as often as he can by hiding in the seating around the fighting pit and hurling darts at PCs who engage Skitch. Balf is too deaf to be sweet-talked and is immune to persuasion attempts, but a successful {@dc 17} Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) check drives him off and ends his sniping. If Balf is the target of two or more melee attacks, he gives up fighting and resorts to cursing. Killing Old Balf has no immediate consequences, but he was loved and respected by his circus mates, and the Yellow Haze might or might not be a cover for welltrained assassins.

entries.name: Area 1: Fighting Pit

entries: A circular pit dug 10 feet into the ground, the dogmole's arena is 45 feet across at its widest point. Dried blood from previous contests is visible on the bare earthen walls. Two heavy wooden poles serve as tether points for the animals.

The walls of the pit are easily climbed. A row of vicious wooden spikes lines the wall at the pit's floor. Creatures forced onto the spikes must make a {@dc 14} Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) saving throw, taking 6 ({@damage 1d8 + 2}) piercing damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. The dust kicked up from the animal's transformation fills the air in the pit and in the tunnel dug by Ingot. PCs who start their turn in the pit must succeed on a {@dc 10} Constitution saving throw or have disadvantage on their attacks. The dust persists for 2 rounds and can be dispersed with magic.

entries.name: Area 2: Audience Stands

entries: The impressive carpentry and design of these wooden bleachers suggests the people of Bleak Rock take their dogmole fighting seriously. Small barrels full of cheap mead punctuate the roughly circular rows of seating that rise steeply from the edge of the pit.

The benches are made of plain, unfinished wood. A {@creature Dogmole Juggernaut|ToB|dogmole juggernaut} moving over the seats crushes them, leaving behind a trail of difficult terrain. Humanoids gain advantage on all {@skill Stealth} rolls made on the bleachers since the barrels and open rises between benches make ideal hiding spots in the dim evening light.

The audience stands are also highly combustible, and if a target standing in the bleachers is targeted by an attack dealing fire or lightning damage, the bleachers catch fire. The fire spreads randomly at a rate of 5 feet per round and causes 4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) fire damage to any creature ending its turn in the flames.

{@b {@i Eating the Townspeople.}} {@creature Dogmole Juggernaut|ToB|Dogmole juggernauts} that begin their turn in the stands may use their action to eat a hapless town resident. There are a total of six residents who can be eaten in this way. Targeting a {@creature Dogmole Juggernaut|ToB|dogmole juggernaut} with an attack draws the attention of the brute, who no longer munches on the gristly audience members.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: There is not much treasure in the ruins of Bleak Rock's fighting arena. Each of the six townspeople who survive offer the PCs 10-15 gp or other valuables as thanks for saving their lives.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: Who sold the townspeople such monstrous potions? What price does the town put on the head of that vile swindling alchemist? What secrets does Magh keep in her iron mines, and why is Old Balf such a steady hand in combat?

rows: {@b An adventure for four to six characters of 8th or 9th level}

entries: What dwells at the top of that spire? Bad memories and scaled malice. Stay away.

entries.name: Background
entries: The spire has existed for as long as locals can remember. Rising above the sand near the ocean, the spire is topped by a natural cave system. Stories about the place circulate around the docks and taverns of the nearby towns-dark tales of ritual sacrifice and the worship of long dead gods of lightning and storm. Many claim the victims of the old cult still crawl through the tunnels accessible at the peak of the spire. Others say a new scaly threat now lairs there, and the storms of late have been most violent near that place.
In this explorative and perilous adventure, the PCs ascend a great rocky spire to face the place's past and the blue dragon currently in residence.

entries.name: In Your Campaign
entries: This adventure requires a coastal setting. It suggests the caves at the top of the spire were used for rituals and worship. There is a magical altar inside a dragon's lair.
The {@creature Drowned Maiden|ToB|drowned maidens} can be replaced with {@creature roper||ropers}.
This scenario can be used as content for a quest provided by NPCs or as an exciting and dangerous place to explore while the PCs adventure along the coast.

entries.name: In Midgard
entries: A high-ranking member of the Order of the White Lions in Perunalia has discovered an ancient tome of worship to Perun. In it, she also found a single sheet of parchment, detailing a very old ritual site where some of the first priests of Perun performed magic and rites to their god. The text suggests the site contained an altar powered by a magical pearl. The party is tasked with finding and exploring the old spire and recovering the pearl from the altar for the paladin, though what they do with such a treasure is ultimately their choice . . .

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: Leading the PCs to explore the spire can be achieved in a number of ways. The locals are generally afraid of the place and avoid sailing by it, let alone walking near it. The spire looms large in the imagination of everyone living nearby. The PCs might hear of the spire as they travel the coastal region, though the stories about the place vary from person to person.
Alternatively, the party may be sailing and spy the impressive stony finger from afar—a single flash of lightning emanates from its peak. Perhaps their own curiosity takes them to it.

The caves at the top of the spire were once used for rituals of a sinister and electric nature. It could be that the party is led to the site by some priest who wishes its religious significance explored. Details may be added as needed to weave the spire into the campaign.

The rocky spire rises from the sand, a great stone finger pointing at the sky. A few gulls circle lazily above its peak, and the sound of the ocean mixes with their cries. A few scuttling things break into panic before your steps, their pearlescent shells gleaming in the sun.

The spire is roughly 500 feet in diameter and rises 60 feet into the air. The rocky face of the spire provides many handholds for those endeavoring to climb. The dragon has pushed the bones of the creatures it has eaten out of its lair, and they have formed a pile at the bottom, in which all manner of sea creature and humanoid remains can be found. A careful search of the bones and a successful {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check uncovers a few very long strands of black hair mingled in with the bones. The hair belongs to the drowned maidens who dwell in the chamber outside the dragon's lair. PCs who touch the hairs find them clinging and difficult to remove.

entries.name: Charged Coral
entries: The walls of the caves inside the spire are made from magical coral that feeds on electricity. The coral glows, alternating vibrant blue and pink. The entire cave system is lit with dim light from this spectacular display. Creatures who come into contact with the walls must succeed on a {@dc 14} Constitution saving throw or take 7 ({@damage 2d6}) lightning damage. On a failed save, the creature is also affected by one of the following effects (choose or roll randomly):

items: {@b {@i 1-2 Twitchy.}} The PC feels overly alert. They have advantage on initiative rolls and disadvantage on Dexterity checks for an hour.
{@b {@i 3-4 Humming.}} The PC emits a constant audible hum, which is soothing and restores them to full hit points. However, they have disadvantage on {@skill Stealth} checks for an hour.

{@b {@i 5-6 Buzzed.}} The PC feels intoxicated by the electrical field. They have advantage on saving throws against spells and effects that cause fear and disadvantage on Intelligence checks for an hour.

entries: Note that once a PC has been affected by the coral's magic, they are immune to the extra effects for 24 hours. However, they may still take damage from coming into contact with the walls again.

A successful {@dc 17} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check suggests the coral was once used as storage for magical energy. It seems likely the magic animated the coral in unpredictable ways. A successful {@dc 17} Wisdom ({@skill Nature}) check reveals the coral has adapted to live out of water and likely uses electricity to maintain itself.

{@b {@i Living Arcs.}} At random times, the coral manifests small, humanoid-shaped beings of pure electricity ({@creature dust mephit||dust mephits}). These living conduits act unpredictably: they may attack the party, follow them curiously, or attempt to aid them. Use these creatures to reinforce the mystery of the place. They may come to the defense of the dragon if the battle seems very one sided.

entries.name: Area 1: Maidens' Pools
