entries: This large, rocky chamber is punctuated with stalagmites and stalactites. The walls appear to be made from stone and coral. The coral sheds dim blue light that crackles and hums. The slight sound of lapping water can be heard from farther inside.

A few of the unhappy victims sacrificed in this strange place remain trapped here. The pools in this chamber serve as the resting place for these bitter spirits, and they are relatively neutral about the dragon's decision to occupy the upper chamber of the spire. The few explorers who came before have been trapped and eaten in these grim and watery caves long before reaching the dragon's lair.

{@b {@i Bitter Cries, Spectral Sighs.}} The caves sound with the angry and mournful cries of the dead. Each PC who hears it must succeed on a {@dc 14} Wisdom saving throw or feel a deep sense of dread and begin their next round of combat {@condition frightened} by the nearest enemy. The effect lasts until the end of their next turn.

{@b {@i Floating in the Water.}} The largest pool contains two {@creature Drowned Maiden|ToB|drowned maidens}, who attempt to pull the PCs into the pool with their grasping hair. The maidens have advantage on Hair attacks made while standing in their pool.

entries.name: Area 2: Isondim's Lair

entries: The ceiling of this large, natural cavern is almost entirely open to the air. In the center is a seemingly very old stone-and-shell altar that sparks occasionally. A very big pearl has been embedded in the top of the altar and crackles audibly. The coral walls are aglow with electrical energy, shedding bright light throughout. There are blue scales littering the floor, and the walls show evidence of being scraped or clawed.

This is the lair of Isondim, the {@creature young blue dragon}. He has grown very attached to the altar and enjoys its effect on him and the coral walls. He assumes the PCs have arrived to steal the pearl and will likely attack them immediately. Isondim may engage the party in conversation if they make a large effort to avoid combat. He might spare them, provided they offer him something valuable. He will not tolerate deception or exploration of his lair. He begins combat in the skies above the spire and uses his Lightning Breath before landing and continuing his attack.
{@b {@i Master of the Altar.}} On initiative count 1 of each round, Isondim draws on the magic of the altar to do one of the following:

items: Summon a living arc (see {@area Charged Coral|24.3|x}) to assist him. Isondim can never summon more than one living arc at a time.
Heal half the amount of damage he successfully dealt with his Lightning Breath this round.

Expel a shockwave, emanating 30 feet in all directions from the altar. Any creature caught by the shockwave must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw or be thrown 40 feet away from the altar. If the creature strikes a wall during this movement, they take {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet it was thrown. (Remember that touching a wall has additional effects covered in {@area Charged Coral|24.3|x}.) Isondim may only use this effect once per long rest.

entries: {@b {@i Fulminating Altar.}} In the center of the old ritual chamber (now the dragon's lair) is the ancient altar once used in sacrificial rites by forgotten worshippers. The altar maintains some of its original power, and its effects on creatures within 50 feet of the spire are as follows:

items: Spells that deal damage have a 50 percent chance of dealing lightning damage instead.
Spells that deal lightning damage have a 50 percent chance of dealing maximum damage automatically.
The dragon's Lightning Breath is altered when used inside its lair, increasing its recharge rate by one ({@b {@i Recharge 4-6}}), though the damage of the ability remains the same.

entries: The altar is powered by the massive pearl embedded in its top. The pearl is worth at least 3,000 gp. Removing it requires a set of thieves' tools and a successful {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) check.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Isondim has amassed a small hoard of treasure inside his lair. There are 700 gp and 1,100 sp spread about the dragon's chamber. There are also {@dice 1d8 × 10} precious stones of various types (25 gp value each) stored in ornate wooden boxes stacked among the coins.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: The altar is surely desired by a variety of creatures. Perhaps Isondim's presence prevented the others from claiming it, but now with the dragon slain, an opportunity presents itself. The magical pearl in the altar might be sought by dark forces who look to seize it from the PCs should they hold onto it.

rows: {@b An adventure for four to six characters of 8th or 9th level}

entries: Tell your secrets to the jungle.

entries.name: Background
entries: While traveling through a jungle expanse, the PCs meet a trader named Smera who relays a strange tale. Turned away from a nearby outpost, the trader is now heading back to civilization. Curiosity leads the party to the outpost, which has been destroyed. A strange disease has taken the outpost's inhabitants, who built the place in support of a scholarly excavation of a nearby temple ruin. Following the path carved through the jungle by the excavation team, the PCs find the temple and its secrets.
In this moss-covered and dark adventure, the PCs explore an old temple, faces its verdant guardians, and find the source of the strange disease.

entries.name: In Your Campaign
entries: This adventure requires the party to be traveling through or near a jungle. It assumes the party meets and interacts with NPCs on the road. There is an outpost and ancient temple placed in the jungle.
The {@creature Vine Troll Skeleton|ToB|vine troll skeleton} can be replaced with two {@creature troll||trolls}. If making this substitution, only allow one troll to use the lair actions each round.

This scenario is a straightforward delve into a dark temple. It uses a disease to add color and a unique threatening element. It could easily be used as an introduction to a larger dungeon expedition.

entries.name: In Midgard
entries: Princess Perititi of Nuria Natal has funded an expedition into the deep jungles of the south. She is hunting for artifacts from a long-ago expired tribe who worshipped Veles. She has received no word from the expedition in several weeks and hires the party (500 gp contract) to travel by river to the expedition site. The party meets Smera in their travels, who informs them she was turned away when she tried to trade. The princess will be keenly interested in the magical staff the party finds in the temple and offers them 1,000 gp in exchange.

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: A local trader meets the PCs as they travel or camp near the road. She and her entourage of 10 guards ({@creature thug||thugs}) are returning to civilization after selling their goods to remote communities living in the jungle. She is charismatic with a keen wit and a penchant for drinking. Smera was supposed to make a stop at a certain outpost but was turned back a few days ago by its inhabitants due to some sort of illness taking hold there.

I was paid well to bring supplies to an outpost not far from here. Some scholars decided one of the old temples was worth their gold and time. Built a stronghold of sorts-brought soldiers and servants and everything! Cut their path a few miles up the road.
Smera provides the following information:

items: The outpost is in support of an excavation of some nearby temple site.
She is surprised anyone thinks the old ruins of the jungle are worth that kind of coin and effort.
She can provide the location of the footpath leading to the outpost-about a day's travel farther along the road.

entries.name: Mineral Rot
entries: Upon contracting the disease, a creature feels immediately unwell and gains a level of {@condition exhaustion}. During its next long rest, the creature must make a successful {@dc 14} Constitution saving throw or lose half its Charisma score as its flesh begins transforming into a pock-marked, stony surface. The disease can be cured by magic during this stage.

The creature must repeat the saving throw during its next long rest, fighting off the disease on a successful save or succumbing to it on a failed one. Creatures who fail are changed into twisted moss-and-stone covered versions of themselves. Mindless and malicious, the creature attacks any living thing it meets. From this point on, creatures bitten by the afflicted must make a successful {@dc 14} Constitution saving throw or contract the disease. Once fully transformed, only a {@spell wish} spell can restore them.
Use the following template to apply the end stage of mineral rot to foes faced by the party. The disease raises a creature's challenge rating by 1, so adjust encounters accordingly:

items: Increase the AC by 2.
The creature gains resistance to slashing damage from non-magical sources.
The creature is immune to disease and poison.
The creature's unarmed attacks are magical.
The creature gains extra hit points equal to half its current hit point maximum.

If it does not already have one, the creature gains a bite attack with hit and damage ranges appropriate to its CR. Creatures bitten by this attack must make a successful DC 14 Constitution save or contract mineral rot. A successful save results in immunity to contracting the disease for 24 hours.

entries.name: Afflicted Outpost

entries: The smoldering remains of the outpost lie before you. Its timber walls appear torn apart in several places. Through the gaps, you can see the place in various states of ruin.

The exploration outpost was built to support the excursion to the temple but fell to the infection several weeks ago. The workers and hired mercenaries fought against one another and against the infected animals that prowl the region.

entries.name: Exterior
entries: The exterior of the outpost hints at the battles that occurred here. A successful {@dc 14} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check deduces that some of the inhabitants of the outpost died while trying to flee. Nearby is a recently blazed path through the jungle.

entries.name: Interior
entries: The outpost is destroyed. The living quarters and mess hall have been badly damaged by fire. Small animals flit here and there among the rubble and ash. Corpses litter the outpost. Those who dwelled here either died or succumbed to the Mineral Rot disease and fled into the jungle.

entries.name: Storehouse
entries: Several humanoid figures sit, staring vacantly at the dirt floor. Their clothing has fallen away, revealing the moss-covered, stony crust that spreads across their skin. Three (CR 8) or four (CR 10) afflicted mercenaries sit, panting mindlessly in the half-dark of the storehouse. They sprint at the PCs and attempt to bite them. Treat the mercenaries as {@creature berserker||berserkers} with the {@area Mineral Rot|25.3|x} disease template applied to them. They wield no weapons but have the following Bite attack:

{@b {@i Bite.}} Melee Weapon Attack: {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft., 1 target. Hit: 8 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) piercing damage, and the creature must succeed on a {@dc 14} Constitution saving throw or contract {@disease Mineral Rot|KPPreparedExpanded}. A successful save results in immunity to the disease for 24 hours.
There are still some intact supplies here: 20 days' worth of rations, several barrels of good drinking water, and two healer's kits can be found in the rubble.

entries.name: Area 1: Temple Entrance

entries: A sliver of a passage has been excavated, allowing access to the temple's interior. The thin passage eventually opens into a small entry chamber. Piles of moss-covered stones lie against the walls, and a stone staircase descends deeper into the darkness.

The walls here are marked with glyphs and pictographs. A successful {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check suggests the glyphs are likely a warning of some sort, and succeeding by 5 or more deduces that the temple was likely abandoned and sealed at some point in the distant past in order to contain a threat.
There is some equipment belonging to the excavation team on the floor: broken tools and spilled parchment cases litter the ground.

{@b {@i Piles.}} The two piles of stones are the remains of most of the expedition team. The Mineral Rot disease has fused the remains together, forming two semi-sentient piles of limbs and mossy crust. The piles are functionally {@creature shambling mound||shambling mounds} (CR 9) and attack the party once they arrive, attempting to grapple the PCs and drag them down the stairs into the {@area chamber below|25.6|x}.

entries.name: Area 2: Chamber of Sealed Urns

entries: The bottom of the stairs opens into a great, circular chamber. The roots of the jungle have penetrated this stony place, and a tangle of vines spread down from above. In the center of the chamber are six stone urns. All but one are sealed tight. The open one's lid sits on the floor nearby.

The urns contain the remains of ancient humanoids afflicted by the {@disease Mineral Rot|KPPreparedExpanded}. Unable to cleanse the corpses properly and afraid the disease would spread, the builders of the temple locked the corpses away-successfully stopping the transmission of the disease. The recent excavation unearthed the remains and allowed the disease to find new hosts.

{@b {@i Stone Urns.}} Each urn contains the desiccated remains of an afflicted human. A pictograph on the exterior of the urns shows the stages of the disease. Opening an urn risks contracting the disease and requires a successful {@dc 14} Constitution saving throw to avoid. Each urn contains gold and silver jewelry (worth 200 gp total). The valuables in the open urn have spilled out onto the floor.

{@b {@i Tangle.}} The roots from above hide a malevolent guardian ({@creature Vine Troll Skeleton|ToB|vine troll skeleton}). Awakened by the excavators, the creature descends and attacks the PCs, attempting to surprise them from its hiding spot ({@skill Stealth} 19). The guardian remains attached to the tangle as it fights. On initiative count 1 of each round, the guardian may take one of the following lair actions:

items: {@b {@i Vine Escape.}} The guardian ascends into the tangle and reappears in any unoccupied space in the chamber. Opportunity attacks made against the guardian due to this movement have disadvantage.

{@b {@i Whip.}} Two vines lash out from the tangle and attempt to trip any creature standing in the chamber. Targeted creatures must make a successful {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw or be knocked {@condition prone}.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: In addition to the jewelry in the urns, a {@i {@item staff of the python}} clatters to the ground from the tangle once the guardian is defeated. It is very old and covered in glyphs similar to the ones found in the entrance.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: The disease may have spread beyond the temple and outpost. One of Smera's guards could easily have contracted Mineral Rot, bringing it to nearby civilization. Alternatively, the temple's urn-filled chamber may provide access to a larger structure where the nature of the disease becomes clearer.

rows: {@b An adventure for four to six characters of 9th or 10th level}

entries: The mountains are the border between our kingdom and the realm of the {@creature fire giant||fire giants}. Look far eastward. See how the peaks turn black? Their forges must burn night and day to mark the mountains so. Some mornings, sunrise dims from the smoke and soot. Long have we watched the pass and tallied our fortunes at its stillness. Recently though, there are signs our luck is turning. Fiery orbs sail through the night skies and land too near these woods. Scouts report deep craters shrouded in smoke and ash. One sits a mere hour's walk from this outpost. I fear the enemy makes ready some terrible weapon.

entries.name: Background
entries: In a remote mountain range, a clan of {@creature fire giant||fire giants} prepares for war. The plains at the base of the mountains host a number of human communities. The recent heavy smoke from the giants' forges marks their manufacture of a terrible new weapon: hellshot. A single large metal sphere of hellshot launched from an arcane cannon can strike targets several miles away. The impact of these dread munitions is only the initial threat though, for {@creature hell hound||hell hounds} have been packed into the hollow space within-emerging when the sphere lands, along with a toxic gas. The giants now test their new weapon with mixed results.

entries.name: Running the Adventure

entries: Night falls. The stars are numerous and bright, and the mountains to the east are silhouetted. A fiery light erupts suddenly from the stony ridges and sails through the air, crashing to the ground several miles away.

As the PCs camp in the area, they witness the giants testing one of the hellshot rounds. Several minutes pass and traces of the telltale gas are noticed in camp. A successful {@dc 12} Intelligence check determines the gas would be poisonous in larger concentrations.

entries.name: A Fire in the Field

entries: In the distance, a column of thick yellow smoke rises into the sky. A murder of crows appears suddenly, cawing and winging away from the area. The mountains loom nearby, their peaks obscured by encircling clouds.
PCs trained in {@skill Survival} or whose class or background is connected closely with the natural world, notice that there are no animals or insects within 2 miles of the smoke plume.

entries.name: Area 1: Rim

entries: A large crater smolders before you. Shattered trees and upturned soil rest in heaps around the site. A noxious white gas rises from the obscured bottom of the pit. All around the impact site are twists of glowing metal.

The crater is 40 feet across. The twists of melted metal provide no indication as to their origin. The noxious gas is caused by an enchanted brazier at the bottom of the crater, which was designed to break away from the main projectile when it landed. The gas affects anyone in the crater or within 10 feet of its rim. Magical in nature (cast as a 5th-level spell), it can be dispelled, but it otherwise remains toxic for 6 hours. The effects are as follows:

items: Visibility reduced to 15 feet.
PCs breathing the gas must succeed on a {@dc 14} Constitution saving throw or become {@condition poisoned}, which ends 1 minute after the PC is no longer exposed.

entries.name: Area 2: Crater

entries: You arrive at the bottom of the crater. On your descent, you saw an abundance of metal shards sunk into the blackened walls. A freshly bored tunnel extends deeper into the earth. An oddly shaped brazier sits at the center of the crater. Plumes of choking gas rise from its bowl.

The floor of the crater is 20 feet down from the rim. PCs with experience in smithing recognize that the brazier's metalwork originated in fire giant forges. PCs can "disarm" the brazier with a successful {@dc 13} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check followed by a successful {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) check. Success ends the gas's effects. If the PCs succeed on the checks, read the following:
Your close examination of the strange brazier suggests superior metalwork combined with complex mechanisms and magic. The number 14 is impressed on its bottom.
A thorough examination of the crater in combination with a successful {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check reveals a large piece of metal embedded in the crater wall.
Though warped by heat, a clear imprint of a fiendish wolf's head surrounded by flame is visible on the surface of the metal wall.
A successful {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana} or {@skill Nature}) check recognizes the head as that of a {@creature hell hound}.
The tunnel's entry is 6 feet in diameter. PCs standing in or near the entry find it uncomfortably hot.

entries.name: Area 3: Tunnel

entries: The tunnel slopes slightly downward for 30 feet before ending abruptly. Intense heat makes the walls smoke, and exposed roots snap as they slowly burn. Shards of red-hot metal protrude from the ceiling and floor. At the end of the tunnel is a pit roughly 12 feet in diameter. Inside the pit, a large metal ball has come to rest. The sides of the ball are contorted by the impact, and the interior of the projectile is exposed.

The tunnel presents a hazard to any PCs attempting to traverse it. The heated metal studs the walls and falls randomly from the ceiling, burning those who pass. Passing between entryway and pit, a creature must make a {@dc 14} Dexterity saving throw, taking 9 ({@damage 2d6 + 2}) fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

The projectile is dangerously hot, and climbing atop it is a foolish notion. Its contents can be seen from the edge of the pit. Inside the hollow metal ball are the remains of several large creatures. Their charred skulls and limbs suggest a canine form.

The remains belong to six {@creature hell hound||hell hounds} launched inside the ball from the nearby fire giant stronghold. The giants' experiment with a living payload has proven unsuccessful. Eventually, and likely just as the party discovers the metal ball at the end of the tunnel, a {@creature fire giant||fire giant scout} and her {@creature hell hound} companion arrive at the scene. The giant's duty is to investigate whether any of the hounds survived but is happy to engage the PCs in combat. The general tactics of the monstrous pair are as follows:

items: The {@creature hell hound} engages in melee while the giant stays back and hurls boulders.
The giant is content throwing boulders until she is forced into melee.
Both enemies attempt to push PCs standing near the rim into the crater if possible.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The giant carries a leather satchel with some supplies for an overnight stay in the wilds. She wears a masterfully crafted steel gauntlet embellished with small rubies (worth 125 gp total).

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: How close are the giants to perfecting these horrible missiles? Which settlements in the area are likely to be targeted, and do they require warning? What motivates the giants to create such a weapon after many years of peace?

rows: {@b An adventure for four to six characters of 10th or 11th level}

entries: In this lost place, even the stones weep.

entries.name: Background
entries: An evil oracular being has taken up residence in a lonely valley. The only access to the valley is through a thick, dead wood whose shadows draw out foul memories from those who travel within. The oracle, Lurinax, has divined the season in which the world will end. This knowledge is greatly prized by many, so the evil fortune teller hides in his lair, protected by maddening winds and the souls of those he slew to obtain his knowledge.
In this grim and dark adventure, the PCs must travel the trail of shadows, face the manifestations of Lurinax's victims, and finally meet the evil oracle himself.

{@b Lurinax, Master of Visions.} Lurinax is a powerful magical being ({@creature spirit naga}) who has spent centuries studying calendars and prophecies related to the end of the world. He appears as a great spectral serpent with an old man's bearded head. Twisting, shadowy arms float beside him, unhinged and disconnected from his scaly body. Some say he was once an elf wizard who went mad after discovering some uncommunicable mathematical truth. Others say he is a traveler from beyond the stars who has studied cataclysms on multiple worlds. Though his origins are unknown, his nature is obvious: Lurinax is a deeply evil creature—so evil that his very presence in the valley has transformed the nearby region. The dead woods and valley itself have been drawn partly into a demiplane, caught between the Material World and a dark magical realm. Lurinax is not interested in bargains or conversation.

Through magical rituals involving the destruction of mortal souls, Lurinax has recently discovered a shocking truth: the season in which the end of the world will occur. Many wizards, bards, and scholars would be keenly interested in obtaining this knowledge.
The PCs might be hired by some agent to explore the valley and recover his tomes in hopes of learning the truth. How the agent came to learn of Lurinax's discovery is unknown.
Alternatively, the PCs might find themselves on the trail of shadows by accident as they travel the wilds, pursuing their own ends.

entries.name: In Your Campaign
entries: This adventure requires a dead wood or forest and a valley setting. It assumes the location can be partially in the Material World and partially in a plane created by magic. It deals with prophecy and information about the end of the world. At the heart of the adventure is a clue about the end of everything, so it is easily used in a quest involving scholars or prophets.

entries.name: In Midgard
entries: The Haunted Lands of the Giants is the perfect location for Lurinax's valley and lair. Perhaps one of the theurges of Bourgund has had their own prophetic vison, and in secret, they hire the PCs to travel to the lonely, ghost-infested stretch south of the Pytonne Mountains. Or one of Baba Yaga's daughters—a blind, beautiful vela—bargains with the party, offering them audience with Grandmother if they return Lurinax's grim booklet to her.

entries.name: Running the Adventure

entries: Through the dead wood, a path uncoils. The lifeless branches above form a dense canopy, blotting out all but tiny specks of sky, which appear like stars in the darkness. Shadows grow long here, and the dry air leaves a bitter taste in your mouth and a burning in your lungs.

The path through the dead wood is the only reliable means of reaching the valley. PCs who attempt to fly, scry, or otherwise find an alternate route find themselves unable to pierce the obscuring magic of Lurinax. This trail of shadows leads the PCs from the mortal world to the demiplane of the evil master oracle.

{@b {@i Dark Heart.}} The PCs' thoughts become troubled the deeper into the wood they go. Their fears begin to manifest among the dead trees around them. Each PC must name their fear and describe how they might overcome it. Encourage the PCs to assist one another in overcoming their fear. An appropriate monster could be summoned for them to fight, or it could remain strictly a roleplaying experience. Alternatively, the PCs must each succeed on a {@dc 15} Wisdom saving throw or be shaken by their time in the woods, losing Inspiration and having disadvantage on their next ability check or attack roll.

entries.name: Valley

entries: The woods open into a long and grim valley. The stone walls rise upward into a shifting gray sky. No evidence of the world beyond the valley can be seen. It bends ahead and opens further. A terrible wind blows through this place. Nothing grows from the blasted, slate ground.

The valley stretches on for a little over a mile. Lurinax's lair is near the end of the valley. The travel is dangerous (see {@area Dust and Madness|27.4|x}), and the air causes living things to become extremely thirsty. After each half hour of travel, each PC must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw or be compelled to drink half their carried supply of water. If they fail this save and have no water to drink, they suffer one level of exhaustion. Other PCs may offer their water to stave off this effect. Lingering in the valley is dangerous, but the threat of the unnatural thirst may lead the party to move more quickly than is prudent.

As the party travels onward, they are witness to a strange phenomenon. The walls of the valley begin sweating—the condensation collecting and eventually running down the stony face. As it goes, the water collects the black dust that swirls through the valley, creating a tear-streaked effect. The walls appear to weep these blackened tears. A creature touching the tears must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition poisoned} for an hour.

entries.name: Dust and Madness
entries: A howling wind blows eternally through the valley. It shapes small cyclones of dust and grit from the floor of this forlorn place, blowing it here and there. The dust is made from the sundered souls of the unfortunate visitors who came before. Lurinax has means to tear the spirit from the flesh, render it into something tangible, and crush it-destroying the creature permanently. The dust in the valley contains traces of all the creatures Lurinax has annihilated in his search for knowledge. Use the dust and maddening wind described below to add tension and danger as the party traverses the valley.

{@b {@i Annihilum.}} The swirling dust can form a humanoid shape with a twisted visage caught in an eternal, openmouth scream. These eyeless beings are evil and want to draw the life from any creature entering the valley. The annihilum ({@creature air elemental||air elementals}) protect the valley and appear in groups of two (CR 9) or three (CR 13). A successful {@dc 18} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check made while observing the annihilum suggests that, while they appear elemental in nature, the magic that created them is necromantic. Each annihilum repeats the horrible pleading last words of their long-dead living form. Even in combat, the monstrous beings beg those around them to let them live.

{@b {@i Mad Gusts.}} Every so often, a powerful plow wind blows through the valley. Creatures caught in the path of the wind must succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw or take 14 ({@damage 4d6}) bludgeoning damage and be knocked {@condition prone}. Creatures knocked prone by the wind must also succeed on a {@dc 15} Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition incapacitated} for {@dice 1d4} rounds as they experience maddening visions caused by Lurinax's magic.

entries.name: Lurinax's Lair

entries: A short, stony tunnel leads to a massive cave in the side of the valley. Large piles of lit candles reveal hundreds of strange glyphs and sigils painted on the floors and walls. Bones are scattered everywhere, and the skulls leer silently. A massive painted eye dominates the floor of the main chamber. A trick of the light gives it the illusion of moving-watching you as you arrive.

Lurinax ({@creature spirit naga}) meditates near the back of the lair on a pile of splintered bone. He does not appreciate interruption and sees the PCs as little more than fuel for his continued research. A large mortar and pestle sits near Lurinax and is surrounded by various arcane tomes. A pile of armor and equipment taken from his victims sits near his meditation mound.

{@b {@i Ocular Sigil.}} The great eye painted on the floor of the room is infused with protective magic. On initiative count 20 of each round of combat in which Lurinax still has hit points remaining, the eye stares at one randomly chosen enemy of Lurinax. That creature must succeed on a {@dc 17} Wisdom saving throw or feel a sense of impending doom, having disadvantage on attacks against Lurinax until the end of its next turn.

{@b {@i Eyes of Lurinax.}} Two {@creature gibbering mouther||gibbering mouthers} patrol the lair and join Lurinax in combat (CR 14). Their Gibbering trait is empowered by Lurinax, increasing the save DC to 12. The mouthers utter a constant stream of nonsense prophecies, likely involving the PCs or their loved ones.

{@b {@i Soulgrinder.}} Lurinax's mortar and pestle is designed to grind the essence from a living creature. Its interior is coated with a foul mix of dried blood and powered bone. This alchemical implement radiates magic and evil and weighs 50 pounds. It would surely fetch a tidy sum to a collector of such things. A successful {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check allows a creature to activate the mortar and pestle-Lurinax's remains could be slowly destroyed this way, ensuring the beast's permanent death.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The oracle has many tomes stacked in his lair. Among his research is a thin booklet bound in humanoid skin. In it is a simple statement written in Infernal that details the season in which the world will end. Also in the stacks is an ancient text filled with elven prophecies. The book is actually a {@i {@item tome of understanding}}.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: Knowledge such as this is a dangerous thing. What might the PCs do or be forced to do with the knowledge? Who might work against them to take possession of Lurinax's booklet?

rows: {@b An adventure for four to six characters of 11th level}

entries: The shroud was a gift, brought by a traveler from the East. She said it had fooled the gods themselves in the past—though who it was that crafted it, she could not say.

entries.name: Background
entries: A bargain struck between a dwarf chieftain and a great divine power forms the heart of this adventure. The chieftain, unwilling to step down from her position as ruler, seeks a way to hide from the god. When the party rescues some of her kin, they are offered riches for recovering a long-lost magical shroud with the power to obscure mortals from the eyes of the gods. But recovering the shroud draws the attention of the god's agents, and the party must choose a side.
In this storied and fate-filled adventure, the PCs must battle their way through a ruined dwarven armory before deciding the fate of the chieftain.

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: The party hears the unmistakable sounds of a battle raging over the next ridge. Investigating, they discover a small unit of dwarves losing a battle to five {@creature hill giant||hill giants}. Two of the giants have engaged the dwarves in melee while three more are positioned on a nearby ridge, taking pleasure in throwing rocks down on the battered defenders. Once the dwarves are aware of the PCs, the leader—a grim-faced dwarf with a badly broken arm signals them that the rock throwers are the real threat.

If the PCs assist the dwarves, the leader asks them outright to take on the giants on the ridge. If they leave the dwarves to their fate, ensure they encounter the five hill giants shortly after leaving the scene.
Provided the PCs assisted in the fight, the dwarves invite the party to receive thanks from Aganatha in the Hall of the Unmoved.

entries.name: In Your Campaign
entries: This adventure requires a hilly or mountainous terrain. It assumes a clan of dwarves could be allies of the PCs. It refers to dwarven halls and armories built into the stony terrain and uses giants as an enemy to set up the initial plot hook.
The {@creature skein witch|ToB} can be replaced by a {@creature deva}. If this substitution is made, have the deva offer a treasure reward instead of the skein witch's Sealed Destiny ability.
This adventure can be used to establish the PCs in the region and, depending on their choices, can lead to further plots and stories with the NPCs.

entries.name: In Midgard
entries: Traveling through the Ironcrags for their own reasons, the party discovers the Unmoved, a breakaway from the minor canton of Templeforge. Aganatha carries with her some knowledge of creating the gearforged, and her hall's defenses might be bolstered by automatons. Aganatha and her people worship Volund, but her bargain was made with Khors, who recognized the Unmoved would fall to shadow should its venerable ruler die. Khors is angered by Aganatha's refusal to uphold her end of the bargain.

entries.name: Hall of the Unmoved

entries: Powerful columns rise from the stone floor into the darkness above. Great metal braziers have been lit, casting light and smoke into the impressive hall. Tall banners depicting an axe, a hammer, and an ornate chalice hang from the columns. Here and there, dwarves mill about and regard you as they pass, nodding at the warriors with whom you walk this sturdy place.
The dwarves of the Unmoved happily trade with the PCs, who may also rent a humble but clean room from the clan's single inn: the Yellow Stone.

The principal experience in the hall should be an audience with the chieftain, Aganatha the Ageless, who thanks the PCs for assisting her scout with the giants and suggests they dine with her at the next reasonable occasion. If they refuse her invitation, the chieftain likely attempts to speak with them about her dilemma immediately, having recognized the PCs as possible allies in her personal plight.

{@b {@i Feast with Aganatha.}} The party is well fed and toasted by the chieftain and a dozen or so dwarves of import. After the meal is over, Aganatha bids her brethren goodbye, ushering them out, so she might speak with the party alone. During this meeting, she explains her situation and attempts to enlist the party's aid. Her story can be improvised using the following information:

items: Nearly 100 years ago, her health was failing.
Her people were fighting a war against orcs and needed a strong leader.
She summoned a medium from afar with the ability to speak with divine powers.
For days, Aganatha and the medium attempted to contact the gods in hopes of granting Aganatha more life-enough to lead her people through the wars.
Eventually, a divine being of unknown origin agreed to grant Aganatha a whole century of vigor, and in exchange, Aganatha would die and serve the being eternally.
Her time is coming to an end, and the dwarf wishes to continue as leader.

She has found record of an ancient magical object with the power to hide a mortal being from the gods: the {@i {@item Shroud of Oth|KPPreparedExpanded}}. The shroud was a gift to the dwarves, but it was abandoned in an armory in one of the countless wars.
She would see the PCs retrieve it for her, and in exchange, the dwarves would give them two objects of great magical power.

entries.name: Aganatha, the Ageless Chieftain

entries: I've seen my clan through countless wars, invasions, plagues, and cataclysms. Each time, the three banners of the Unmoved triumphed. I'll not give up my rule for something as changing as fate.
{@b {@i What She Wants Most.}} To extend and solidify her rule over her clan.

{@b {@i Physical Traits.}} Aganatha is a broad-shouldered dwarf with emerald eyes and a permanent wry grin. Her white hair is worn in three long braids, each tipped with a silver figurine representing the three symbols of her clan: the axe, the hammer, and the chalice. Out of battle, she wears simple clothing and a wide leather belt with a dragon's tooth on the buckle. In combat, she wears a suit of adamantine armor with milky quartz adornments on the breastplate and gauntlets. The chieftain is incredibly strong and, as her bargain dictated, has lost none of her vitality to time.

{@b {@i Personality/Roleplaying.}} Aganatha is a warrior at heart. Having survived numerous battles, she is extremely confident and unshakable. In her younger years, the bright fire in her spirit won her the hearts of her people. She has been the leader of the Unmoved for almost 200 years, and her role as chieftain is a part of her being. She is direct and places little value in small talk and niceties although she has an excellent gallows sense of humor.
Aganatha knows the following:

items: She can direct the PCs to the location of the abandoned armory.
The mountains around the armory are wild and dangerous.

entries.name: Journey to the Armory
entries: The armory is located 30 miles from the Hall of the Unmoved. The mountains and hills of the region are difficult to traverse, and the party's normal travel speed is reduced by half. Use the following encounters to challenge the party as they travel:

items: {@b {@i Bulette Storm.}} A flash storm precedes an attempted ambush by 3 (CR 13) {@creature bulette||bulettes}, who use the heavy rain and thunder to mask their approach. The monsters leap on the party from above.

{@b {@i Ettins in Love.}} The party hears a terrifying series of screams and curses emanating from a cave in the mountains. Investigating, they discover three {@creature ettin||ettins} (CR 10) feuding with one another. Their conversation suggests that a love-triangle of sorts exists between several of the heads, creating a confusing and loud confrontation.

entries.name: Area 1: Abandoned Armory Entrance

entries: This long-crumbling hall reeks of waste and rot. Humanoid and animal bones litter the stony floor.

The entrance is the lair of six (CR 9) or eight {@creature ogre||ogres} (CR 12). Their leader, a smarter-than-average brute named Turg, wields a {@i {@item +2 greatclub}} and has the maximum number of hit points. The ogres have not explored the deeper sections of the armory, as the cold winds and hissing have been enough to keep them out, and have erected crude walls at either end of the entry hall. They defend their lair with mindless violence. Once two or more of their number fall in combat, the rest attempt to flee into the collapsed chamber—their fear of the PCs outweighing their fear of the depths. Any ogres who manage to escape can be heard dying horribly in the darkness of the collapsed chamber, slain by the {@creature wraith||wraiths} within.

entries.name: Area 2: Empty Halls

entries: The air is stale, and all is in ruins. These rooms and passages might have once served as living quarters for those who worked the armory. A few skittering things flee from your footsteps.

The halls and chambers beyond the ogre lair are mostly empty. They can serve as a place for the party to hunt down fleeing ogres. A few dwarf-sized {@creature skeleton||skeletons} are found as the party moves through the place. A successful {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Medicine}) check suggests they died of injuries caused by weapons of some kind. Before the party reaches the collapsed chamber, they hear agonized screams and ghostly battle sounds that come from no specific direction.

entries.name: Area 3: Collapsed Chamber

entries: This chamber once served as a storeroom for weapons and armor. Dwarf-sized suits of plate and scale mail lie corroding in piles on the floor. Empty weapon racks line the walls. The back quarter of the room has collapsed, and stony rubble prevents further access.

Three (CR 13) or four (CR 15) dwarf-shaped {@creature wraith||wraiths} haunt this chamber. Having freshly killed any fleeing ogres, the wraiths spend the first round of combat raising the fallen beasts as {@creature specter||specters}. The wraiths guard the {@i {@item Shroud of Oth|KPPreparedExpanded}}, which is kept in a secret room (spot {@dc 14}) connected to the chamber. The shroud is rolled around a platinum cylinder (worth 500 gp) and stored inside a large silk bag.

{@b {@i Fate's Enforcer.}} Should the party recover the shroud, as they leave the armory, they will be met by a divine agent. Sent by the power with whom Aganatha has made her bargain, the agent appears as a floating, faceless humanoid with magical strands swirling around its body. The {@creature skein witch|ToB} does not attack. Instead, it attempts to explain that Aganatha cannot be allowed to break the bargain. It demands that the shroud be taken far away and that the PCs must not concern themselves with the fate of the Unmoved. It offers to use its Sealed Destiny ability to entice the PCs to agree and explains the consequences of this gift. After making its case, it awaits the parties' response. It will attack if the PCs refuse its request.

entries.name: Returning the Shroud
entries: Aganatha is true to her word. She rewards the party with two rare magic items (GM's choice) and provides them and honorary estate within the walls of her hall. The PCs make a powerful ally who might assist them in a variety of ways in their future adventures. Aganatha uses the shroud to obscure herself from the divine being.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The PCs are free to keep the {@i {@item Shroud of Oth|KPPreparedExpanded}} for themselves. Though the great witch who made it will undoubtedly come to reclaim it.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: Keeping the shroud leads to a confrontation with the minions of its creator. Returning the shroud to the great witch might result in further adventures as the witch has lost many such items. Returning the shroud to the dwarf likely makes the divine power angry, and the party might have to contend with its servants or make amends by performing some other tasks.

rows: {@b An adventure for four to six characters of 11th level}

entries: She lay down her sword and wept; her tears are the water. She lay down her body and slept; her bones are the fountain. Atop the mountain, at the war's end, a place for gods to wonder.

entries.name: Background
entries: A planetar rests at the top of a mountain. A veteran of an ancient war against the hells and a champion to a god long forgotten, sleep has transformed her into a radiant fountain, which now serves as a place of reflection for good-aligned clerics. One such cleric has returned from the mountain with an unsettling tale: the fountain's waters are spoiling, and strange magics hover visibly near the holy place. In truth, a host of devils plots to corrupt the fountain and claim the planetar as a servant of an unnamed arch-devil.
Arriving atop the mountain, the PCs must battle through crumbling pillars, repel the devilish corruption, and prevent the planetar's dark awakening.

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: The threat of the planetar's awakening is very real. The chain devil in {@area 2|29.6|u} is performing a ritual that, if completed, awakens the planetar as a corrupt and evil being. Left unassailed, the chain devil completes the ritual in 3 rounds. If the ritual is interrupted, the chain devil does not attempt to restart, and it attacks the PCs. There are several ways to interrupt the ritual:

items: Compel the chain devil to move from its place beside the fountain.
Deal radiant damage to the chain devil.
Hit the chain devil with a melee weapon.

entries: If the ritual is completed, a {@creature planetar} appears above the fountain, and after 2 rounds, its coloration changes to a deep crimson. It attacks the party. It does not pursue if the PCs retreat.

entries.name: Tethered to Hell
entries: The mission to acquire a planetar is important to the unnamed arch-devil, and the infernal patron has provided its minions with an additional boon. Smoky-violet tendrils from the deep reaches of hell appear from the ether and attach to the shoulders of the devils. The tethers provide advantage on saving throws against magical attacks and effects. The tendrils can be physically severed by an attack (AC 13, hp 10) or withered by clerics or warlocks with a successful {@dc 10} check using their spellcasting ability (counts as a 60foot ranged attack). A warlock may expend one of their spells granted by Mystic Arcanum to sever the tendrils of all devils within 60 feet, replacing the normal effect of the mystic arcanum.

entries.name: Seat of the Planetar
entries: The fountain is actually a potent weapon that can battle the invading devils. Any spellcaster within 60 feet of it knows it's magical. Any good-aligned PC may sit in the throne-like seat and attempt to use its magic. Understanding the powers of the fountain requires a successful {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana} or {@skill Investigation}) check, and divine spellcasters have advantage on this roll. The fountain can be used to perform one of the following as an action:

items: {@b {@i Holy Motes.}} The fountain casts {@spell magic missile} as a 12th-level spellcaster: 12 missiles that deal radiant damage. The occupant of the seat chooses the targets.

{@b {@i Repel Evil (Recharge 5-6).}} All evil-aligned creatures with 10 or fewer Hit Dice are instantly moved to the perimeter of the fountain's flagstones. Affected creatures move in the straightest path possible and must succeed on a {@dc 12} Dexterity saving throw or fall {@condition prone} at the end of the forced movement.

entries.name: Area 1: Columns in the Wind

entries: The trail passes between two rows of crumbling columns. A stone tablet has fallen from its place atop one of the columns, and its face appears vandalized. A cold wind blows through the ruined approach, and with it comes a faint, dark whispering.
Hiding in the toppled columns are two {@creature barbed devil||barbed devils}. They attempt to ambush the party and attack from different directions once the PCs are among the columns.

A message is scratched crudely into the tablet in Infernal: "She will serve, and all will serve." A successful {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check on the tablet reveals it bears some strange features reminiscent of scribed scrolls. Any spellcaster may attempt to read the tablet with a successful {@dc 14} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana} or {@skill Religion}) check. Reading the tablet restores 10 hit points to all good-aligned PCs within 20 feet. If the reader is a good-aligned divine spellcaster, the affected PCs also gain the benefits of a long rest.

A successful {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check while searching the area uncovers several traveler's packs abandoned among the columns. The packs contain a quiver (12) of +2 arrows, two potions of supreme healing, and a small pouch containing finely cut rubies (worth 300 gp).

entries.name: Area 2: Fountain of the Planetar

entries: Climbing the final short ascent, you see a great stone fountain standing at the highest point of the mountaintop clearing. Flagstones are set in a circular pattern surrounding the large basin, and a throne-like seat is mounted on a pedestal at the fountain's center. A small host of devilish figures cavort in the basin. The water near them darkens.

The contingent of devils consists of a {@creature barbed devil}, two {@creature bearded devil||bearded devils}, and a {@creature chain devil}. They grin at the PCs as they approach the fountain. The chain devil attempts to corrupt the fountain as described above. The remaining devils attack the PCs. The bearded devils actively try to block the PCs' movement toward the chain devil. The barbed devil focuses its attacks on PCs attempting to use the Seat of the Planetar, using its Hurl Flame from range before diving into melee.

Although interrupting the devil's ritual does end the threat posed by the awakening planetar, it does not remove the brackish spoiling of the water. A {@spell heal} or {@spell greater restoration} spell restores the water entirely. Alternatively, good-aligned divine spellcasters may also restore the water by succeeding on a {@dc 18} Wisdom ({@skill Medicine}) check. Restoring the water grants a boon on the PCs, and they have advantage on all attacks against chaotic evil opponents of 10 or greater Hit Dice for 24 hours.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: How is the history of the planetar connected with the identity of the arch-devil? Perhaps a war long forgotten is but postponed as the infernal forces gather strength and launch new plots. Maybe a divine complex hidden below the fountain offers answers, treasures, and further battles with the damned?

rows: {@b An adventure for four to six characters of 12th or 13th level}

entries: Let nothing end the Feast by the River. Let the celebration of our enemy's vanquishing ring out night and day for eternity. Let the bones of our enemies and our prey mingle under our feet. This is your time, our time, the best time.
{@i — (Queen Gellao on the eve of her victory over the followers of Dur, decreed at the River's Bend feast hall)}

entries.name: Background
entries: A feast hall by a swiftly moving river has hosted six weeks of continued celebration. The owner of the hall, Johan Bathe, is giddy from the riches the feast has brought him and is sincerely doing his best to keep the party going forever. A local monarch's victory over a dangerous group of rebels caused the elated queen to fund a feast without end. The merriment can be heard a mile away.

However, the last several days have seen some strange and ominous events occurring at River's Bend. Johan's hired help, responsible for cleaning out the refuse pit under the main hall, have gone missing. Worse, a guest perished mysteriously last night when a fragment of bone erupted from her abdomen. Johan is looking for adventurers to investigate the storeroom and refuse pit and to do what they can to ensure the gold keeps pouring in.
If the PCs take Johan's offer, they descend into the dark where the bones of vanquished enemies and roasted animals mingle and conspire under revelers' feet.

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: Throughout the PCs' exploration of the feast hall's basement, they can hear the sounds of merriment above. The grating in the ceiling of {@area 2|30.5|u} allows light from the feast to stream down in eerie columns. Furthermore, refuse cast to the floor by the revelers occasionally falls through the grate. On initiative count 20 of each round, refuse falls into the room. Each PC must succeed on a {@dc 12} Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 1} piercing damage from the falling debris. Additionally, PCs struck by the debris must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw or have disadvantage on attack rolls and skill checks that round. The bone collective and its undead minions are unaffected.

entries.name: Johan Bathe

entries: A weary, middle-aged halfling with a bright-red beard and an expensive hat, he can't hide his sleep deprivation as his mood turns from elation to anxiety in the same breath.

{@b {@i Overworked, Anxious, Emotional.}} The owner of the River's Bend, Johan Bathe is currently experiencing the joys and hardships of catastrophic success. His livelihood, and likely his neck, requires that the feast continues. He has sent out word for adventurers to investigate the strange goings-on under his hall and offers the PCs 500 gp and lifetime access to the feast.

Johan is keeping a dark secret: he offered refuge to the defeated rebels during the rebellion. He is sure their spirits have now returned to the storeroom and waste pile with but one thought—that of revenge. A successful {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check suggests he is hiding information, and a successful {@dc 14} Charisma ({@skill Intimidation} or {@skill Persuasion}) check convinces him to reveal his secret.
In conversation, he also provides the following information:

items: A guest was killed when a fragment of bone burst from her stomach.
A horrific stench has been wafting up from below. He uses perfume, but the guests have begun to complain.
Two hirelings went missing while working downstairs.

entries.name: Area 1: Storeroom

entries: The cold stone storeroom of River's Bend is stocked to bursting capacity. Hanging from the ceiling are countless haunches and whole sides of game and livestock. Barrels of mead and wine line the walls under overflowing shelves of preserves and cheeses. Under the pleasant aroma of the food is a note of rot.

A {@creature Bone Collective|ToB} in its humanoid form begins to stalk the PCs in the storeroom. It remains well hidden ({@skill Stealth} 25) and watches them from among the hanging meats. PCs trained in {@skill Survival} or those with a hunting background sense they are being watched. If discovered, the bone collective transforms into a swarm and flees to {@area 2|30.5|u}, dashing as required. After a short while in the storeroom, the PCs notice one side of beef swaying in a strange way. If they investigate, they are surprised when the following happens:

Suddenly, like worms burrowing to the surface, the bones of the cured meat escape from within and clatter in a pile on the floor, forming into a small, fanged humanoid. As you watch, the other hanging carcasses begin to sway.

At this point, 25 Small {@creature skeleton||skeletons} attack the party. They have no weapons, but their bite is equivalent to their {@item shortsword} attack. A party that is the correct level should have spells and abilities that trivialize this threat: the potential to destroy all 25 in a single round is expected. This encounter is meant to add flavor but adjust it to create a greater threat as desired.
The bone collective stealthily retreats into {@area 2|30.5|u} when the skeletons form.

entries.name: Area 2: Refuse Pile

entries: The door opens to reveal a massive chamber of stinking refuse. Along the far wall of this rectangular room is a large opening with an iron cover, dangling on its hinges. Shovels lean near the dark chute. Fresh air from the riverbanks beyond the room mingles with the smell of rotting waste and something far worse. Tall piles of garbage rise from the floor, and a steady downpour of food and bones and broken dishes fall from the grates in the ceiling high above.

The floor of this room is considered difficult terrain. The {@creature Bone Collective|ToB} and its minions, a pair of {@creature wight||wights}, are hidden in the piles of garbage. Once the PCs are well into the room, they attack-rising to ambush the party. Garbage from above continues to fall as described previously.

The bone collective attempts to attack and move away. If the bone collective has no enemies adjacent to it at the beginning of its turn, it may attempt to hide. All {@skill Stealth} checks made by the bone collective in this area have advantage. If no wights remain alive at the beginning of the bone collective's turn, it may use an action to summon two additional {@creature wight||wights} within 15 feet of itself. The haunts rise from the piles of seeping garbage and join the fray. Once the bone collective is defeated, the strange haunting of the hall is ended.

entries.name: Teetering Piles of Garbage
entries: Any enemy can use its action to push over a pile of garbage (located at {@b A}, {@b B}, {@b C}) onto a PC provided both the enemy and the PC are adjacent to the pile. The PC must succeed on a {@dc 14} Dexterity saving throw or be {@condition restrained} for a round. On their next turn, the PC can use an action to free themselves from the waste. There are three such piles, and once used, they may not be used again.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: Attempting to communicate with the bone collective is a very real possibility. What unsettling truth does the creature reveal about the queen's victory? Is the rebellion against her truly defeated?

rows: {@b An adventure for four to six characters of 14th or 15th level}

entries: Once, we were friends. She used her spells to ward our grove against the darkness in the woods. It was the mirror that turned her mind to covetous thoughts. She saw its power and changed. We have kept the mirror safe for an era, but her soldiers grow strong and now something makes for our tree that we cannot repel. If her aberration reaches the grove, the mirror will be hers, and then we will all know what lies at the tip of the wickedest branches.
{@i — (Queen Gellao on the eve of her victory over the followers of Dur, decreed at the River's Bend feast hall)}

entries.name: Background
entries: A fey village in an ancient grove has been repelling the aggression of a sorcerer living in the nearby mountain. The village leader, Eusim Bladewreathe, is very concerned that the enchanted mirror that the faeries protect will be taken by the sorcerer. The mirror, also known as the Bending Glass, is a powerful artifact made to amplify magic.

Eusim has received word that the sorcerer has created a monstrous siege weapon and is moving its two halves across a nearby pass. The sorcerer's soldiers have reinforced the forest side of the pass to secure the area for the arrival of the siege weapon's power source. If the two halves are joined, the resulting weapon would be near impossible to stop. Eusim offers the PCs permanent access to the faerie's teleportation portal if they agree to prevent the siege weapon from being constructed.
Arriving at the front line, the PCs must break the fortified positions of the sorcerer's clockwork soldiers and stand before a true juggernaut: the salt golem.

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: Spending time in Eusim's grove has the following effects:

items: All PCs gain the ability to cast {@spell misty step} as a move action. This ability may be used only once.
For a week, all PCs gain the monk's Timeless Body ability.

entries.name: Eusim Bladewreathe

entries: A fading amber light emanates from this small, concerned faerie. His wings curl slightly at the tip, and unlike those of his kin, they are slightly frayed. His voice sounds of rain falling on a forest canopy.

{@b {@i Ancient, Severe, Weary.}} Eusim brought the Bending Glass to the grove many centuries ago. He swore to a fey god that he would keep it safe, for its power to amplify magic was deemed too dangerous for mortal hands. In his small village, he has worked tirelessly to ensure the mirror was kept out of sight. He cast a spell that hid the mirror in the grove's great tree, and it is bound thereone with the boughs and the roots.

The grove has a small portal enchanted with teleportation magic that allows two-way travel between the Material World and the wild dimension of the fey. He offers free travel through the portal to the PCs if they agree to stop the sorcerer's siege weapon.
He reveals the following information:

items: The Obsidian Pass is half a day's travel to the east.
The siege weapon has two halves. The first is already across the pass. The second half now makes its way down from the mountains—a massive golem crafted to be the siege weapon's engine.
The sorcerer's soldiers reinforce the forest side of the pass.

entries.name: Juggernaut Formed

entries: The golem steps into the harness of the massive, bladed drill. A terrible whine amplifies to an unbearable volume before stopping abruptly. The ground trembles as the juggernaut stands upright.

Though the juggernaut defends itself, its primary target is the grove. It does not pursue the PCs if they retreat. If the salt golem in {@area 1|31.6|u} reaches the other half of the siege weapon, the following occurs instantly:

items: The salt golem is fully healed and any conditions on it are removed.
The salt golem gains vulnerability to lightning damage.
The salt golem gains resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage and to cold and fire damage.
The salt golem gains the following action:

entries: {@b {@i Annihilating Swathe.}} Melee Weapon Attack: +11 to hit, reach 5 ft., up to 3 targets. Hit: 14 ({@damage 4d6}) slashing damage.

entries.name: Fight Choreography
entries: Use the following as a round-by-round tactical guide or as a loose narrative sequence, depending on GM's needs:

items: {@b {@i Round 1.}} Begins when the PCs engage the soldiers. Two veterans collaborate to use the arcane cannon (see {@area 1|31.6|u}) while the other two fire crossbows. The clockwork myrmidons rush to engage in melee.

{@b {@i Round 2.}} {@i At the top of the pass, moving slowly and deliberately, a towering humanoid figure appears, and its footsteps can be felt even at this distance.} The salt golem appears ({@b A}) and begins its journey to the first half of the siege weapon ({@b B}). The golem moves 40 feet per round, using both its actions to move. If engaged in melee, the golem ceases its journey and defends itself. If there are no adjacent enemies, it uses its actions to continue moving toward its destination.
{@b {@i Round 4.}} Uncontested, the golem travels the 120 feet required to reach the first half of the siege weapon (see {@area Juggernaut Formed|31.4|x}).

entries.name: Area 1: Obsidian Pass

entries: The trees and loam give way to rocky soil at the edge of the forest. A jagged mountain range dominates the eastern sky, and snowcapped peaks are shrouded by swift-moving clouds. A wide pass descends into a fortified camp. The spiked barricades and rough stone walls encircle a wicked, bladed drill attached to a large leather harness. Figures move behind the walls.

There are two {@creature Clockwork Myrmidon|ToB|clockwork myrmidons} and four {@creature veteran||veterans} inside the camp. They guard the first half of the siege weapon with their lives. The object has been magically strengthened (AC 15, hp 90). Destroying the harness and its bladed drill prevents the juggernaut from forming, but it does not stop the arrival of the {@creature Salt Golem|ToB} (see {@area Juggernaut Formed|31.4|x}). One veteran keeps watch at all times.

If attacked, the myrmidons are deployed first and engage in melee while the veterans stay behind the walls (half cover) and attack with their heavy crossbows. The soldiers do their best to prevent the PCs from hampering the approach of the golem. The myrmidons use their Grease Spray strategically, and the veterans use the arcane cannon (see below) to slow the PCs' advance.

entries.name: Arcane Cannon
entries: Two veterans can coordinate to use the arcane cannon provided by their mistress. The cannon can be destroyed (AC 12, hp 25). Firing the cannon requires the action of both veterans: {@b {@i Arcane Pulse.}} {@i Ranged Weapon Attack:} +7 to hit, range 60/120 ft., one target. Hit: 8 damage, and the target must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw or be stunned for a round.

entries.name: Concluding the Adventure
entries: Clearly the threat of the sorcerer remains. What vengeance does she seek to enact upon the PCs for their meddling? What terrible evil does she unleash should she possess the Bending Glass?
